pairs.name: Night Stalker
pairs.reason: Crippling Fear prevents AM from abusing his amazing mobility by not allowing him to use Blink. Dark Ascension makes it hard for AM to play on the outskirts of fights and wait for his opportune moment as NS's vision outranges Blink substantially. NS has one of the lowest Intelligence gains in DOTA and generally builds for rightclick making him a poor Mana Void target.

pairs.name: Meepo
pairs.reason: Simply put Meepo stats checks AM like no other hero as any stats he builds get it's value multiplied and is easily able to overwhelm AM after just a couple of items and a couple of extra Meepos. Earthbind can be used to chain root AM to death.

pairs.name: Huskar
pairs.reason: Mana Break and Mana Void literally do nothing against Huskar as he is the only hero in DOTA without a Mana pool. Counterspell does NOT block/ reflect Life Break nor does Blink disjoint it as Huskar still follows him.

pairs.name: Phantom Assassin
pairs.reason: AM has amazing Magic Resistance and a low HP pool to balance that out, while PA does huge bursts of Physical Damage and can usually delete an AM with a single Phantom Strike and a couple of Coup de Grace crits. PA is not the best target for Mana Void as she has low Intelligence gain and does not itemize for Mana much and forces AM into investing in a MKB due to her massive built in evasion.

pairs.name: Lone Druid
pairs.reason: Simply put Lone Druid stats checks AM to an overwhelming degree as he is essentially 2 heroes that do exclusively Physical Damage. Summon Spirit Bear's base stats are already too much for AM to deal with and a single Etangling Claws proc into a Save Roar fear is usually enough to get him killed.

pairs.name: Axe
pairs.reason: Counter Helix and Culling Blade both do Pure damage, which does not get mitigated by Counterspell's Magic Resistance and are especially effective versus low HP pool heroes like AM. Berserker's Call provides reliable lockdown for AM that cannot be dispelled. AM having one of the lowest BATs in the game make him trigger Counter Helix frequently and usually a single Call+BM+CB combo from Axe is more than enough to kill him.

pairs.name: Troll Warlord
pairs.reason: Troll simply scales exponentially better than AM to a point where in a straight up fight AM simply gets overwhelmed. Troll can chain ensnare AM preventing him from using Blink and cause him to miss attacks with Whirling Axes (Melee). Mana Void doesn't do much to Troll as he has one of the lowest Intelligence gains in DOTA.

pairs.name: Legion Commander
pairs.reason: Legion does infinitely scaling Physical Damage and provides a long duration lockdown trough Duel. Counterspell CAN both block and reflect Duel, however reflecting it is almost always an outcome AM would've rather avoided. AM has one of the lowest BATs in the game making it easy for LC to get Moment of Courage procs.

pairs.name: Kez
pairs.reason: With high DPS and a silence that shuts down his Blink, leaving him vulnerable. Kez's mobility lets him kite or close the gap, controlling the fight's pace. This prevents Anti-Mage from escaping, farming, or initiating effectively, especially before he gets key items like Manta Style.

pairs.name: Abaddon
pairs.reason: Abaddon's ulti can be used DURING Berserker's Call.Despite Culling Blade going trough Borrowed Time, Abaddon still provides barriers and healing for allies caught out by Axe's Berserker's Call. His Aphotic Shield additionally dispells Battle Hunger.

pairs.name: Shadow Demon
pairs.reason: SD can use Disruption on Axe to interfere with his with Berserker's Call, or an ally to provide them with invulnerability during it. Aghanim's Scepter gives Break to his ultimate, which greatly cripples Axe's capabilities.

pairs.name: Tusk
pairs.reason: Tuskar can use Snowball to save his entire team from Berserker's Call and provide them with invulnerability. Additionally, his Aghanim's Scepter allows him to reposition Axe a great distance away from his Called targets.

pairs.name: Bane
pairs.reason: Bane's Nightmare provides 1 second of invulnerability that could be more than enough to save his allies from Berserker's Call. Addiotionally, if timed accurately Nightmare can completely dodge Berserker's Call taunt effect altogether.

pairs.name: Doom
pairs.reason: Doom's ultimate essentially takes Axe out of the game for a period of time. When put on autocast his Infernal Blade can trigger during Berserker's Call stunning Axe briefly and doing Max HP percentage damage.

pairs.name: Pugna
pairs.reason: Pugna's Decrepify can be used both on Axe to prevent allies from attacking him or on allies to prevent them from attacking Axe during Berserker's Call. Additionally, he can use Life Drain on Taunted allies to sustain them trough it.

pairs.name: Witch Doctor
pairs.reason: Witch Doctor's ultimate - Death Ward is great at killing Axe as it does Pure damage, which is not mitigated by armor. Despite Death Ward attacking quickly it does not trigger Counter Helix. Voodoo Restoration provides healing for his allies.

pairs.name: Lifestealer
pairs.reason: A natural counter to Axe as he has built in Lifesteal that scales with Axe's high HP, making him significantly difficult to burst in a single combo. Additionally, Rage causes him to avoid BM damage and Open Wounds provides him even more Lifesteal.

pairs.name: Spectre
pairs.reason: Spectre's Dispersion reduces all types of damage, including Pure Damage, which makes her a hard target to burst in a single Axe Combo. Additionally, her other passive Desolate deals Pure damage, which does not get mitigated by Axe's armor.

pairs.name: Leshrac
pairs.reason: Leshrac consistent output of Magic and Pure damage do not get mitigated by Axe's armor. His low Attack Speed and general tanky itemization make him impossible for Axe to kill him on his own. This relegates Axe to using his Call for Crowd Control.

pairs.name: Necrophos
pairs.reason: Necro's kit leaves Axe in shambles. He deals exclusively Magic damage, which also scales with % Max HP that does not get reduced by Axe's armor. He provides hefty AOE healing, which helps keep his team topped up. His low attack speed barely procs Counter Helix.

pairs.name: Primal Beast
pairs.reason: Primal's natural large HP pool and slow attack speed make him a poor target for for Berserker's Call in terms of bursting him. His ult pierces BKB and his Aghanim's Scepter gives him an AOE Break, which further limits Axe's damage and kill potential.

pairs.name: Pudge
pairs.reason: Pudge's natural large HP pool and slow attack speed make him a poor target for for Berserker's Call in terms of bursting him. Additionally, he can hook Axe or any of his allies to disrupt his Combo. Aghanim's Shard allows him to Dismember a teammate and save them.

pairs.name: Spirit Breaker
pairs.reason: Bulldoze provides SB with a large amount of Status Resist, which mitigates the duration of Berserker's Call greatly. Planar Pocket prevents Axe from casting CB on his targets as it redirects it to SB. SB has low cooldown BKB piercing Crowd Control to interrupt Axe consistently.

pairs.name: Timbersaw
pairs.reason: Whirling Death reduces a percentage of Axe's total Strength, for scaling damage troughout the game. All his spells are Pure damage, which do not get mitigated by armor. He generally has low Attack Speed and his ultimate prevents him from attacking, making it hard to get CH procs.

pairs.name: Wraith King
pairs.reason: A natural counter to Axe as he has built in Lifesteal to sustain trough his Berserker's Call. Additionally, he can deal Pure damage to Axe, which does not get mitigated by armor and has at least 1 extra life, making it impossible to kill him in a single Call+BM+CB combo.

pairs.name: Venomancer
pairs.reason: Venomancer's overwhelming Magic damage does not get mitigated with armor. In lane, Veno has constant poke, slow and harass to prevent Axe from cutting creep waves or sustaining. Plague wards do NOT take damage from Counter Helix nor do they proc it.

pairs.name: Outworld Devourer
pairs.reason: OD's ability to deal heavy Pure and Magic damage naturally counters Axe as it doesn't get reduced by armor. Astral Imprisonment can be used both on Axe and allies to disrupt his Call. If set to autocast Arcane Orb persists during Call.

pairs.name: Ursa
pairs.reason: Ursa's ultimate 'Enrage' allows him to mitigate all damage by 80%. Aghanim's Scepter further allows him to even use it during Berserker's Call. His infinitely scaling damage would eventually overwhelm even Axe's high armor and HP.

pairs.name: Pudge
pairs.reason: Pudge has various ways of saving his teammates from Bane's spells. He can Meat Hook stationary allies under the effects of Nightmare and Fiend's Grip as well as pick up an Aghanim's Shard to Dismember them and cancel their effects altogether.

pairs.name: Naga Siren
pairs.reason: Bane's lack of AOE damage makes it difficult for him to deal with Mirror Image Illusions - this allows Naga to keep the waves pushed, giving her and her team the upper hand. Song of the Siren can interrupt Fiend's Grip even when upgraded by Aghanim's Scepter and more importantly even if it connects with the real Naga then Mirror Image Illusions can be sent to dispatch of the channeling Bane.

pairs.name: Silencer
pairs.reason: Global Silence interrupts Fiend's Grip from anywhere on the map, even if upgraded with Aghanim's Scepter. BKB and any debuff immunity effects do not prevent this as it pierces debuff immunity making it almost impossible for Bane to get of a full duration Fiend's Grip on any of Silencer's teammates.

pairs.name: Abaddon
pairs.reason: Aphotic Shield is a low cooldown Strong Dispel, which can dispel Enfeeble, Nightmare and even Fiend's Grip. Additionally, Borrowed time can be used DURING Fiend's Grip to remove it even if upgraded with Aghanim's Scepter.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: Dark Pact is a low cooldown Strong Dispel, which can dispel Enfeeble, Nightmare and even Fiend's Grip. Additionally, his Aghanim's Shard Depth Shroud can be used on any of his teammates during Nightmare or Fiend's Grip to provide sustain and protect them from any single target damage.

pairs.name: Visage
pairs.reason: Familiars are able to use Stone Form and interrupt Fiend's Grip even if Visage is affected by it. Additionally, Familiar can issue an attack command on any Nightmared targets in order relocate the sleep onto them and free the initial target.

pairs.name: Tidehunter
pairs.reason: Blubber allows Tidehunter to dispel Enfeeble, Nightmare and even Fiend's Grip upgraded by Aghanim's Scepter with 0 cooldown, given he is taking enough damage. Fiend's Grip damage is Pure and by itself does enough damage to not be able to get more than a couple of seconds of it's duration off in the best case scenario.

pairs.name: Medusa
pairs.reason: Mana Shield provides the perfect defense for Medusa against Thirst as you generally have to go through her entire Mana Pool before being able to reduce her HP significantly. She can use Stone Gaze to stand her ground in order to deal with Rupture and Blood Mist is horrible against Mana Shield as it does not trigger any Lifesteal and her low HP pool counteracts the max HP percentage damage. Cold Blooded (Aghanim's Shard) procs from Rupture providing her an extra layer of protection.

pairs.name: Storm Spirit
pairs.reason: Ball of Lightning provides invulnerability allowing Storm to stay mobile, while affected by Rupture as it does not damage him during it. This also allows Storm to dodge Blood Rite or just move out of it entirely and keep his distance from Bloodseeker.

pairs.name: Juggernaut
pairs.reason: Healing Ward provides massive AOE healing, which makes it significantly more difficult for Thirst to empower Bloodseeker. Blade Fury can be used to soak Blood Rite, while Omnislash and Swiftslash (Aghanim's Scepter upgrade) provide invulnerability allowing Jugg to use them during Rupture without getting damaged and pack enough burst damage to outright kill Bloodseeker.

pairs.name: Oracle
pairs.reason: Fortune's End can dispel Blood Rite's silence, while Purifying Flames and Rain of Destiny (Aghanim's Shard ugprade) can provide significant sustain to mitigate Thirst's effects. False Promise also dispels Blood Rite but more importantly provides a save for any Ruptured targets allowing them to further engage or disengage.

pairs.name: Ember Spirit
pairs.reason: Fire Remnant and Sleight of Fist provide invulnerability allowing Ember to stay mobile and do damage, while affected by Rupture. - these also allow Ember to dodge Blood Rite or just move out of it entirely. Flameguard can soak a significant portion of Bloodseeker's Magic Damage output and Searing Chains provides a low cooldown root to better control him.

pairs.name: Abaddon
pairs.reason: Abaddon can keep his allies healthy preventing Bloodseeker from being empowered by Thirst. Aphotic Shield can dispel both Bloodrite's and Bloodrage's Silences. Borrowed Time just heals up Abaddon to full HP and allows him to keep moving without taking damage.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: His high mobility and Spell Shield make it hard for CM to land spells. He easily jumps and kills her due to her low mobility and armor. Mana Void punishes her high mana pool and teamfights.

pairs.name: Nyx Assassin
pairs.reason: He easily sets up kills on CM with Vendetta and Mana Burn. Spiked Carapace reflects her AoE spells, punishing her in fights. CM’s low HP makes her an easy target for Nyx’s burst combo.

pairs.name: Pugna
pairs.reason: Nether Ward heavily punishes CM’s high mana-cost spells.

pairs.name: Clockwerk
pairs.reason: He traps CM with Hookshot and Cogs, making her an easy kill. CM can’t escape due to low mobility and lack of defensive tools. Her channeling ultimate gets canceled easily by Battery Assault and Hookshot.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: He shrugs off her slows and roots with Dark Pact. Essence Shift makes him stronger the longer fights go, while CM gets weaker. Hard to lock down and escapes easily after picking her off.

pairs.name: Rubick
pairs.reason: He can steal powerful spells like Frostbite or Freezing Field and use them more effectively. Rubick outranges her and can disable or zone her with Telekinesis.

pairs.name: Pudge
pairs.reason: He can Hook CM out of position and kill her quickly. Flesh Heap’s magic resistance helps him survive her spells. Rot and Dismember counter her low mobility and squishy nature

pairs.name: Faceless Void
pairs.reason: Time Walk can be used to close the distance within Drow Ranger, hindering her Marksmanship bonus. Faceless Void can also lock down Drow Ranger with Chronosphere before she has the chance to retaliate due to her low health pool.

pairs.name: Arc Warden
pairs.reason: Flux along with Spark Wraith allows Arc Warden to quickly burst down Drow Ranger due to her low health. Magnetic Field will be a big nuisance while pushing towers against Arc. However, Drow Ranger can bypass Magnetic Field's evasion bonus thanks to Marksmanship but only while hitting heroes.

pairs.name: Chaos Knight
pairs.reason: Drow Ranger cant deal with illusion heroes naturally so Chaos Knights Phantasm will be a big problem as well as Reality Rift being able to pull you in closer and disabling your Markmanship.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: A well-timed Dark Pact can dispel Frost Arrows and Gust, letting Slark engage and escape freely. Essence Shift is very detrimental for Drow Ranger as the loss of agility means that Marksmanship will also suffer from getting weakened. Shadow Dance lets Slark quickly close the gap and deal heavy damage without giving Drow Ranger a chance to retaliate. Pounce counteracts Frost Arrows's slow, and also allows Slark easily pin Drow Ranger down or flee from her. Depth Shroud from Aghanim's Shard will allow Slark to save both, himself and his allies and will also allow them to freely fight back against Drow Ranger without her noticing them. Others

pairs.name: Earth Spirit
pairs.reason: Earth Spirit’s powerful initiation and disables quickly close that gap. Earth Spirit’s Boulder Smash and Rolling Boulder can stun and silence Drow, disrupting her attacks and forcing her to retreat. Additionally, Earth Spirit’s ability to control terrain and displace heroes makes it hard for Drow to find safe spots to deal damage, limiting her effectiveness in fights.

pairs.name: Primal Beast
pairs.reason: Drow struggles against Primal Beast because he is a tanky, melee initiator who can easily close the gap on her and disrupt her positioning. His high burst damage and disables prevent Drow from staying at a safe distance to deal damage. Primal Beast’s strength and crowd control make it difficult for Drow to kite or escape, and his durability allows him to survive her attacks while locking her down early in fights.

pairs.name: Zeus
pairs.reason: Zeus is effective against Drow because his high magical burst damage can quickly punish her relatively low magic resistance and fragile health pool. His Lightning Bolt and Arc Lightning reveal invisible heroes like Drow when she uses shadow blade, preventing her from safely initiating or escaping. Additionally, Zeus’s ultimate, Thundergod’s Wrath, can finish off fleeing enemies, making it hard for Drow to survive team fights or pickoffs.

pairs.name: Bloodseeker
pairs.reason: Drow struggles against Bloodseeker because his high mobility and burst damage can quickly close the gap and punish her low health pool. Bloodseeker’s Thirst lets him track and chase her even when she tries to escape, while his Blood Rite silence can prevent her from casting Gust to control fights. His aggressive playstyle and healing from damage make it hard for Drow to stay safe and farm effectively.

pairs.name: Mars
pairs.reason: Drow struggles against Mars because his tankiness and crowd control make it hard for her to find safe angles to deal damage. Mars’ Bulwark blocks Drow’s ranged attacks, reducing her damage output significantly. His Arena of Blood traps her and her team, limiting mobility and forcing close-quarters fights where Drow is vulnerable. Mars’ ability to initiate and control fights disrupts Drow’s positioning and prevents her from kiting effectively.

pairs.name: Muerta
pairs.reason: Muerta’s Pierce the Veil increases her attack speed and damage making her immune to drow right clicks, Muerta’s ultimate can overwhelm Drow’s team, disrupting positioning and forcing fights that favor Muerta’s aggression.

pairs.name: Wraith King
pairs.reason: Reincarnation serves as a natural deterent for Earthshaker to all in Wraith King with an Echo Slam as he would shortly come back to life, while Shaker would be left with not much in the tank. WK can select Spectral Blade as a facet instead of Bone Guard in order to reduce the number of Echo Slam targets.

pairs.name: Spectre
pairs.reason: Disperion + BM is a huge deterent for Earthshaker to drop Echo Slam whenever he wants, as often times it would mean his own death. Spectral Dagger can be used to move through Fissure's wall to prevent being blocked. Spectre's ability to instantly get on top of Earthshaker with Shadow Step or Haunt ruins his initiation and doesn't allow him to comfortably wait for his opportune moment.

pairs.name: Night Stalker
pairs.reason: Dark Ascension providing unobstructed vision and flight, while reducing Earthshaker's and his team's vision allows NS to spot Shaker and stick on him relentlessly with Crippling Fear, not allowing him to get of a clean initiation or any spells for that matter. Despite Fissure being able to stun NS he can still fly over it.

pairs.name: Tidehunter
pairs.reason: Blubber allows Tidehunter to instantly dispel Aftershock's stun with Echo Slam's damage and to instantly counter initiate with Ravage. Dead in the Water (Aghanim's Shard upgrade) prevents Earthshaker from jumping with Enchant Totem when upgraded by Aghanim's Scepter.

pairs.name: Clockwerk
pairs.reason: Battery Assault can stun Shaker so often that he would be unable to use Fissure due to it's long cast points. Rocket Flare can scout Shaker out and disrupt his Blink initiation, while Hookshot can be used to stick on him and further disrupt him with Power Cogs. Jetpack (Aghanim's Shard Upgrade) allows him to fly over Fissure.

pairs.name: Abaddon
pairs.reason: Apothic Shield can dispel any of Shaker's stuns to save Abaddon's allies, while Borrowed Time makes Abaddon close to impossible to kill within a single burst.

pairs.name: Axe
pairs.reason: Berserker's Call pierces spell immunity, making a Blade Fury teleport escape impossible. It's very useful against Omnislash as well. Juggernaut's low base health and high attack speed causes him to take a lot of damage from Counter Helix. Axe is a common Blade Mail and Blink Dagger carrier making him a very big potential threat before Juggernaut get his items.

pairs.name: Legion Commander
pairs.reason: Duel pierces spell immunity, making a Blade Fury teleport escape impossible as well as being a threat with Blink Dagger and Blade Mail all over the map.

pairs.name: Windranger
pairs.reason: Windrun negates the damage from Omnislash and gives Windranger enough movement speed to get out of Blade Fury range.

pairs.name: Lone Druid
pairs.reason: Lone Druid's Spirit Bear can tank Juggernaut's Omnislash effectively, reducing its impact. The bear’s Entangling Claws can disable Juggernaut even through Blade Fury. Lone Druid out-pushes and out-farms, forcing early fights Juggernaut isn’t ready for.

pairs.name: Visage
pairs.reason: Familiars soak Omnislash hits and can stun him repeatedly. Visage’s tanky nature and armor reduce Juggernaut's kill potential. His burst damage can overwhelm Juggernaut’s sustain.

pairs.name: Muerta
pairs.reason: Muerta’s Pierce the Veil makes her immune to physical damage—Juggernaut’s main output. She can kite Juggernaut and deal magic damage outside his Blade Fury immunity. Omnislash is completely negated during her ultimate.

pairs.name: Night Stalker
pairs.reason: Night Stalker excels in nighttime vision and silences Juggernaut. The silence disables Blade Fury. He also builds tanky and can chase Juggernaut with ease making it easy to lock down juggernaut before he gets spells off.

pairs.name: Riki
pairs.reason: Riki’s Smoke Screen disables Juggernaut’s right-clicks and spells. Juggernaut struggles to deal with invisibility without detection. Riki can gank and snowball early, shutting Juggernaut’s farm.

pairs.name: Morphling
pairs.reason: Morphling’s high armor and Agi-based tankiness make him hard to burst. He can waveform out of Omnislash or replicate Juggernaut’s stats/abilities. Magic burst and sustain make him win drawn-out fights.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Anti-Mage blinks out of Omnislash easily. He burns Juggernaut's mana, making it harder to Blade Fury or heal. AM scales faster and wins late-game duels.

pairs.name: Bloodseeker
pairs.reason: Rupture damages Mirana during Leap and is a big deterent for her to spam it as she has one of the lowest strength gains in the game and Pure Damage is primarily countered by flat HP and HP regeneration. Thirst allows BS to reveal any opponents under the effects of Moonlight Shadow that have been damaged sufficiently.

pairs.name: Puck
pairs.reason: Dream Coil prevents Mirana from using Leap. Waining Rift, Phase Shift and Ethereal Jaunt can be used to dodge Sacred Arrow and Starstorm. Jostling Rift can cancel Leap mid air.

pairs.name: Mars
pairs.reason: Arena of Blood prevents Mirana and her teammates from attacking across its walls, mitigating a huge component of her damage output, while simultaneously preventing her from Leaping in and out of it. Bulwark can mitigate the damage from her attacks and further re-direct them to Mars. God's Rebuke and Spear of Mars can interrupt Leap mid air.

pairs.name: Spectre
pairs.reason: Mirana is one of the squishiest heroes in the game with good mobility. This makes her a perfect target for Spectre to eliminate. Spectral Dagger provides partial vision of her enemies allowing Spectre and her team to track the movements of their enemies during Moonlight Shadow.

pairs.name: Nyx Assassin
pairs.reason: Mirana is one of the squishiest heroes in the game, making it a nightmare for her to survive a Nyx's burst combo at all stages of a game as Vendetta does Pure damage. Impale can interrupt Leap mid air, while Spiked Carapace can soak the damage from Sacred Arrow and Starstorm, locking down Mirana in the process.

pairs.name: Abaddon
pairs.reason: Sacred Arrow can be dispelled by both Aphotic Shield on any of Abaddon's allies, as well as Borrowed Time from Abaddon himself.

pairs.name: Alchemist
pairs.reason: Morphling naturally has high base attack damage and Alch is capable of significantly reducing it with Corrosive Weaponry and cripple Morph's overall damage output. Chemical Rage is by far Alchemist's best spell, which Morphling is unable to copy with his ult - Morph. Morph can be slow to ramp up and generally speaking by the time he's ready to fight Alch is ready to take his Ancient.

pairs.name: Ancient Apparition
pairs.reason: Ice Blast prevents Morphling from using Attribute Shift (Strength Gain) to increase his HP pool and 'heal' up. To farm optimally Morphlings keep their HP low in order to have as much Agility as possible, which allows AA to snipe him across the map with Ice Blast.

pairs.name: Axe
pairs.reason: Axe counters Morphling with instant disable from Blink Call into Blade Mail. Morphling’s low armor while shifting strength becomes a liability. Axe punishes greedy Morph builds with pure initiation. Morphling can’t avoid dying if caught while not fully morphed.

pairs.name: Doom
pairs.reason: Doom disables Morphling’s ability to Attribute Shift, leaving him very vulnerable. Once Doom is cast, Morphling can be bursted down quickly. Morphling relies heavily on abilities to live and fight. Doom’s spell removes his entire playstyle temporarily.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: PL overwhelms Morphling with illusions that deal fast damage and are hard to identify. Morphling’s single-target abilities don’t counter illusion spam. Morphing into PL is ineffective due to low stat scaling. In the late game, PL is too much to handle without AoE.

pairs.name: Rubick
pairs.reason: Rubick becomes a threat if he steals Waveform or Morph. He can burst Morphling with his own tools. Morphling’s valuable spells often get turned against him. Rubick can outplay Morph if Morphling is careless with spell usage.

pairs.name: Luna
pairs.reason: Luna’s fast-paced teamfight damage bursts Morphling before he can shift. She takes objectives quicker and snowballs faster. Morphling doesn’t enjoy early fights and Luna forces them. Eclipse punishes Morphling’s weak early-game.

pairs.name: Nyx Assassin
pairs.reason: Nyx punishes Morphling with Mana Burn based on high INT from Attribute Shift. His Carapace triggers easily on Waveform or Adaptive Strike. Nyx scouts Morphling and disables him before he reacts. Mana burn spam ruins Morph’s sustain and forces defensive play.

pairs.name: Lion
pairs.reason: Lion disables Morphling instantly with Hex and burst combo. His Finger of Death punishes Morph’s low HP when morphed to Agility. Lion doesn’t care about Morph’s shift due to chain disables. Morphling dies in one rotation if not extremely careful.

pairs.name: Dark Seer
pairs.reason: Dark Seer’s Wall creates a strong illusion of Morphling that turns fights against him. Ion Shell and Vacuum force him to fight on DS’s terms. Morphling has a hard time bursting illusions fast enough. He becomes his own worst enemy in wall-heavy fights.

pairs.name: Bane
pairs.reason: Bane’s Fiend’s Grip pierces BKB and disables Morphling fully. Enfeeble reduces his damage and healing during fights. Bane also sets up ganks that Morph can’t dodge. Morphling suffers if caught before shifting or after Waveform.

pairs.name: Chen
pairs.reason: Chen’s creeps pressure Shadow Fiend in lane, and his team-wide sustain punishes burst-based heroes like SF. Shadow Fiend has a hard time dealing with spread-out fights and split-push.

pairs.name: Troll Warlord
pairs.reason: Troll is a hard counter in manfights. Shadow Fiend relies on burst and kiting, but Troll wins long engagements and can disarm Shadow Fiend with Whirling Axes and lock him down with bash.

pairs.name: Zeus
pairs.reason: Zeus outranges and out-pokes Shadow Fiend. He doesn’t care about armor or BKB early, and constantly chips SF down. Zeus can cancel Blink Dagger from fog with his global ult.

pairs.name: Lina
pairs.reason: Lina outranges SF and can kill him before he gets BKB. Her high burst and fast right-clicks make laning and mid-game fights difficult for Shadow Fiend unless he gets the jump first.

pairs.name: Shadow Demon
pairs.reason: Shadow Demon can disrupt Shadow Fiend’s combos. He removes SF from the fight with Disruption, sets up ganks, and can use Shadow Poison to scout and cancel Blink Dagger.

pairs.name: Sniper
pairs.reason: Sniper’s range makes it difficult for Shadow Fiend to approach. Unless SF blinks directly onto him, Sniper can kite him all fight long. Headshot also prevents SF from closing the gap effectively.

pairs.name: Keeper of the Light
pairs.reason: Keeper blinds and wave clear delay Shadow Fiend’s push. Chakra Magic and Will-o-Wisp are disruptive during Requiem channeling. His mobility makes it hard for SF to catch and burst him.

pairs.name: Tiny
pairs.reason: Tiny can burst SF down instantly with a combo. He wins early skirmishes, tosses SF out of position, and scales into a tanky initiator. Shadow Fiend struggles to survive without BKB.

pairs.name: Windranger
pairs.reason: Windranger’s Windrun negates SF’s right-click damage unless he has MKB. Shackleshot can interrupt Requiem and she can burst SF with Focus Fire if he doesn’t have Ghost Scepter/BKB.

pairs.name: Spirit Breaker
pairs.reason: Spirit Breaker punishes SF’s low mobility and poor defensive options. Charge cancels SF’s channeling and blink. In the early and mid-game, Spirit Breaker is a constant threat across the map.

pairs.name: Underlord
pairs.reason: Atrophy Aura reduces BASE attack damage and PL being an Illusion hero greatly benefits from stacking Agility and increasing his Base damage and Attack Speed to empowers his Illusions. Agility stacking means high armor so both Firestorm and Pit of Malice are great at providing reliable Magic damage and Crowd Control for him and his Illusions due to their AOE properties.

pairs.name: Leshrac
pairs.reason: Leshrac's AoE abilities destroy Phantom Lancer's illusions. Diabolic Edict and Pulse Nova require no targeting, thus hitting Phantom Lancer whenever he's nearby.

pairs.name: Jakiro
pairs.reason: Jakiro's AoE abilities are great against Phantom Lancer: Dual Breath slows down and damages Phantom Lancer and his illusions. Liquid Fire will not only deal AoE damage but also lowers Phantom Lancer's attack speed. Ice Path and Macropyre combo can easily clear all of Phantom Lancer's illusions. Jakiro can predict Doppelganger and Ice Path on top.

pairs.name: Earthshaker
pairs.reason: Earthshaker absolutely destroys Phantom Lancer with Echo Slam, which scales with number of illusions. Every illusion becomes a source of damage in teamfights. Fissure and Enchant Totem also stop PL’s movement. One good Echo can turn the tide and win the fight outright.

pairs.name: Sven
pairs.reason: Sven’s cleave from Great Cleave and huge burst from God's Strength wipe out Phantom Lancer’s illusions. Storm Hammer stuns all units in a small radius, making it easy to hit the real PL. Sven scales just as well and brings more raw damage to fights. If Sven gets a good initiation, PL dies before illusions matter.

pairs.name: Axe
pairs.reason: Axe is one of the best illusion counters with his passive Counter Helix. Berserker’s Call forces PL and illusions to attack him, triggering spins. Blade Mail punishes illusion damage and Culling Blade finishes off the real PL. He dominates mid-game and forces PL to avoid direct fights.

pairs.name: Sand King
pairs.reason: Sand King has multiple AOE tools like Burrowstrike, Sandstorm, and Epicenter. Phantom Lancer can’t stand in fights due to continuous AOE damage. Blink initiation from Sand King disrupts PL’s positioning instantly. If Sand King gets a good Epicenter, illusions vanish in seconds

pairs.name: Timbersaw
pairs.reason: Timbersaw excels at killing clustered illusions with Chakram and Whirling Death. He is incredibly tanky and doesn’t care about physical damage from PL. Timber Chain helps him escape and reposition while continuing AOE spam. PL can’t kill him unless massively ahead.

pairs.name: Dark Seer
pairs.reason: Dark Seer’s Ion Shell deals AOE damage and clears illusions while farming. Wall of Replica creates a strong PL illusion, turning his own power against him. Vacuum combos well with AOE allies and punishes clumped illusions. PL’s illusions become more of a liability than an asset.

pairs.name: Necrophos
pairs.reason: Necrophos punishes drawn-out fights, which PL often thrives in. Ghost Shroud protects Necrophos from physical damage and heals him massively. Reaper’s Scythe punishes low-HP heroes like PL after extended pokes. He thrives while PL struggles to finish him off due to his sustain.

pairs.name: Ember Spirit
pairs.reason: Ember Spirit clears illusions effortlessly with Sleight of Fist + Maelstrom or Battle Fury. Remnants allow him to escape and poke PL without commitment. Phantom Lancer’s illusions don’t survive long enough to do meaningful damage. A well-farmed Ember becomes untouchable for PL and his illusions.

pairs.name: Night Stalker
pairs.reason: Night Stalker silences and reveals Puck during Night Time. Crippling Fear prevents all spellcasting and forces BKB. Puck has no safe escape once silenced. Night Stalker is one of the best counters to mobile, squishy heroes.

pairs.name: Riki
pairs.reason: Riki’s Smoke Screen disables Puck’s spell usage completely. He can scout and follow Puck even in trees or during Orb. Diffusal Blade and burst damage kill Puck fast. Puck struggles in teamfights when silenced from invisibility.

pairs.name: Lone Druid
pairs.reason: Lone Druid’s bear is tanky and applies strong push and root pressure. Puck can’t clear the bear easily with his burst. Once rooted, Puck dies quickly to physical damage. Druid forces early towers and ends games before Puck scales.

pairs.name: Huskar
pairs.reason: Huskar shrugs off magic damage and forces fights before Puck is ready. Burning Spear and Inner Fire punish Puck’s low HP pool. Coil doesn’t stop Huskar’s aggression. Puck can’t burst him without coordinated help.

pairs.name: Dragon Knight
pairs.reason: Dragon Knight’s magic resistance and regen negate Puck’s early damage. He doesn’t care about being silenced. Dragon Form allows safe pushing, making Puck’s split-push less effective. He tanks Coil and shrugs off poke damage.

pairs.name: Spectre
pairs.reason: Spectre haunts into Puck’s backline and forces him to disengage. Dispersion punishes constant spell spam. She thrives in long fights while Puck relies on quick kills. Spectre wins in the late game and scales harder.

pairs.name: Broodmother
pairs.reason: Broodmother overwhelms Puck with spiderlings and map control. Puck can’t clear spiders fast enough and lacks physical burst. Brood also builds items like Orchid that punish squishy spellcasters. Puck cannot contest her in the early-mid game.

pairs.name: Bane
pairs.reason: Bane’s Fiend’s Grip goes through Puck’s shift and disables for a long time. Nightmare forces awkward Phase Shift usage. Bane has more lockdown than Puck can escape from. Puck gets punished if he mistimes spell dodges.

pairs.name: Nyx Assassin
pairs.reason: Nyx reflects Puck’s spells with Carapace and uses Mana Burn for heavy damage. Vendetta makes Puck cautious in side lanes. Nyx locks Puck down longer than she can Phase Shift or Blink. He also builds natural detection and disables.

pairs.name: Tiny
pairs.reason: Tiny bursts Puck instantly with Avalanche-Toss combo. He can Blink in and catch Puck before she reacts. Tiny’s physical and magical burst are dangerous. Puck often dies before she can cast anything when caught.

pairs.name: Abaddon
pairs.reason: Aphotic Shield is a low cooldown ability that can outright dispel Dismember and when combined with Mist Coil, Pudge finds himself struggling to output enough damage to get through all the sustain. Withering Mist provides additional healing mitigation, which is one of core Pudge's main strengths he plays for. Borrowed Time can be used during Dismember to dispel it.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Counterspell can block and reflect Dismember, while providing significant Magic Resistance that mitigates a lot of Pudge's damage from Rot and Dismember. Blink's mobility makes it hard for Pudge to keep up with Anti Mage, or lock him down and stay on top of him when combined with Counterspell.

pairs.name: Beastmaster
pairs.reason: Meat Hook is Pudge's signature and arguably most impactful ability. Call of the Wild Boar makes it hard for Pudge to land a Meat Hook on Beastmaster or any of his allies, while Call of the Wild Hawk summons hovering in a circle around Beastmaster makes it a complete Hail Marry play whether the Meat Hook would connect or not. Primal Roar interrupts Dismember.

pairs.name: Bristleback
pairs.reason: Bristleback's dominant physical damage and armor reduction through his spells and right clicks makes short work of a low armor Pudge. Bristleback cares little about getting Hooked by Pudge, and actually wants to get Hooked to immediately be in the middle of fights and burst down Pudge with his Quill Spray and right clicks. Pudge's spell combo also doesn't threaten Bristleback because of his tankiness.

pairs.name: Chaos Knight
pairs.reason: Chaos Knight and his Phantasm illusions easily burst down a low armor Pudge with their dominant physical damage during the armor reduction from Reality Rift. Pudge also has a difficult time Hooking his target among the Chaos Knight illusions, and his AoE Rot damage isn't enough to immediately find the real hero. Pudge's spell combo also doesn't threaten Chaos Knight because of his tankiness and lifesteal through Chaos Strike procs.

pairs.name: Clockwerk
pairs.reason: Clockwerk's long range stun through Hook Shot lets him interrupt Pudge's Dismember channel on his target. Clockwerk also isn't threatened by Pudge's Meat Hook into Dismember as he can activate Battery Assault when next to him to interrupt his ultimate easily. Pudge also has a hard time running down Clockwerk with Rot as Power Cogs can easily push him away.

pairs.name: Legion Commander
pairs.reason: Legion Commander's Press the Attack is a strong dispel that stops Pudge's Dismember channel when she presses her spell on the Dismember target. Legion Commander's dominant physical damage also makes short work of a low armor Pudge, and gives her easy Duel wins to accumulate damage throughout the game.

pairs.name: Lifestealer
pairs.reason: Feast scales with Flesh Heap - you know it's a bad matchup when your own scaling powers up your opponent as well. Rage is amazing against Pudge as the debuff immunity avoids the slow from Rot, while the magic resistance reduces the damage from Dismember and Rot. Between Open Wounds and Feast, Pudge struggles to output enough damage to get trough Lifestealer's sustain alone. Even Infest can be used as a save by instantly healing a Dismembered ally.

pairs.name: Lina
pairs.reason: Lina's burst damage spells take down Pudge in fights as his damage block from Meat Shield does him little help to reduce the damage. The Light Strike Array stun also stops the Dismember channel to prevent Pudge from locking down and killing anyone.

pairs.name: Lone Druid
pairs.reason: Lone Druid and his Spirit Bear dish out a ton of physical damage to make short work of a low armor Pudge, who struggles to get away from the Spirit Bear because of the Entangle root. Lone Druid also becomes extremely tanky during True Form, and the hero as well as his Spirit Bear are not threatened by Pudge's Meat Hook into Dismember combo. Savage Roar from either Lone Druid or his Spirit Bear can also disrupt the Dismember channel.

pairs.name: Monkey King
pairs.reason: Pudge's Meat Shield does little to negate the massive burst damage done by Monkey King's Boundless Strike and Primal Spring. Monkey King also gets to build up Jingu Mastery stacks easily by attacking an immobile Pudge and burst him down because of his low armor. Boundless Strike also lets Monkey King stop the Dismember channel.

pairs.name: Necrophos
pairs.reason: Necrophos' Heartstopper Aura reduces the max HP of heroes around him, which works incredibly well against a high HP Pudge and his Flesh Heap strength gain. Pudge also does self damage with Rot and relies on his high HP pool to run down heroes, but Necrophos threatens to kill Pudge with Reaper's Scythe whenever he falls below half HP, making it extremely difficult for Pudge to get aggressive in fights.

pairs.name: Outworld Devourer
pairs.reason: Pudge's Meat Shield does little to reduce Outworld Destroyer's massive damage through his spells and Arcane Orb right clicks. Pudge's low mana pool also lets Outworld Destroyer threaten him with Sanity's Eclipse after just one Astral Imprisonment usage. Astral Imprisonment on Pudge or his Dismember target also interrupts the ultimate, as long as Outworld Destroyer isn't stunned himself by the spell.

pairs.name: Slardar
pairs.reason: Slardar's dominant physical damage and armor reduction through his spells and right clicks makes short work of a low armor Pudge. Slardar's lockdown through Slithereen Crush and Bash of the Deep interrupts the Dismember channel, as long as Slardar isn't stunned by the spell himself. Slardar's high movement speed through Guardian Sprint also lets him dodge Meat Hook, as well as distance himself from Pudge and his Rot damage.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: Pudge's high HP pool and Flesh Heap strength gain works against him as it only gives Slark a bigger HP pool to right click and build up Essence Shift stacks throughout the game. Slark's mobility through Pounce lets him dodge Meat Hook as well as get away from Pudge and his Rot damage. Slark can also easily dispel Dismember off himself with a timely Dark Pact, and is never threatened by Pudge as long as Shadow Dance is off cooldown. The Depth Shroud from Aghanim's Shard also stops the Dismember channel on an ally.

pairs.name: Tidehunter
pairs.reason: Tidehunter is never threatened by Pudge's Meat Hook into Dismember combo because of his high HP pool, and Kraken Shell always dispels Dismember if Pudge's damage exceeds the threshold of the spell. Tidehunter also cares little about getting Hooked, and actually wants it to happen when Ravage is off cooldown, as it brings him right in the middle of the enemy team to stun all of them. Ravage also interrupts the Dismember channel.

pairs.name: Timbersaw
pairs.reason: Timbersaw's burst damage through his spells makes short work of Pudge, as his Meat Shield does little to reduce the damage coming towards him. Timbersaw's Whirling Death connection on Pudge also reduces his strength, turning his Flesh Heap stacks against him and making him much less tanky. Timbersaw's mobility through Timber Chain also lets him avoid Meat Hook, and his high HP pool means Pudge never threatens him with his spell combo.

pairs.name: Undying
pairs.reason: Undying's Tombstone is a massive counter to Meat Hook as it spawns zombies on top of Pudge and his team, which compels him to right click and kill the zombies if he wants to Hook anyone in fights. Undying also steals strength through Decay, making himself extremely tanky while rendering Pudge's Flesh heap stacks completely useless. This leads to Undying never feeling threatened by Pudge's Meat Hook into Dismember combo.

pairs.name: Ursa
pairs.reason: Fury Swipes makes it so that no itemization would ever make Pudge unkillable. Earthshock is effective at dodging Meat Hook as well as staying on top of Pudge. Enrage gives Ursa an abundance of damage reduction to mitigate even Meat Hook's pure damage, as well as status resistance to reduce Dismember's duration. Aghanim's Scepter can further upgrade Enrage allowing Ursa to use it during Dismember and dispel it.

pairs.name: Weaver
pairs.reason: Weaver's high mobility through Shukuchi makes it extremely difficult for Pudge to ever land a Meat Hook on him, while Rot does not slow Weaver at all during Shukuchi, meaning Pudge can never run him down with his spell. Weaver can also undo all the damage and get away with Time Lapse. Weaver's dominant physical damage and armor reduction through The Swarm beetles also makes short work of a low armor Pudge.

pairs.name: Wraith King
pairs.reason: Wraith King's dominant physical and pure damage with his Spectral Blade facet makes short work of a low armor Pudge. If Wraith King has the Bone Guard facet, his skeletons make it extremely difficult for Pudge to land the Meat Hook on his target. Pudge's spell combo also doesn't threaten a tanky Wraith King, while the second life from Reincarnation means Wraith King doesn't have to worry about Dismember on both lives.

pairs.name: Primal Beast
pairs.reason: Primal Beast closes gaps quickly, making Razor’s kiting ineffective. Onslaught and Trample punish Razor’s lack of lockdown or escape. Razor gets interrupted before Static Link becomes impactful. Primal Beast snowballs easily through Razor’s weak early damage.

pairs.name: Queen of Pain
pairs.reason: Queen of Pain out-ranges and out-pokes Razor in lane. Her Blink allows easy escapes from Static Link attempts. She builds magical burst damage that Razor cannot reduce. Razor is forced to waste Plasma Field just to stay relevant in fights.

pairs.name: Bloodseeker
pairs.reason: Bloodseeker thrives on fast movement and punishes Razor’s chase attempts with Rupture. Razor cannot run without taking massive damage. Blood Rite zones Razor from using Static Link safely. Razor gets outpaced in tempo and punished in overextensions.

pairs.name: Enigma
pairs.reason: Enigma can farm freely against Razor and Black Hole stops all his mobility. Razor has no disables to stop Enigma from channeling. Eye of the Storm cannot break through Black Hole without external help. Enigma’s teamfight presence overshadows Razor in big engagements.

pairs.name: Arc Warden
pairs.reason: Arc Warden’s magnetic field nullifies Razor’s physical attacks. Tempest Double can bait out Static Link and abilities. Razor cannot lock down Arc Warden long enough to prevent split-push. Arc Warden wins through patience, poke, and map pressure.

pairs.name: Morphling
pairs.reason: Morphling can disengage and reposition faster than Razor can catch. Static Link gets dodged through Waveform or Attribute Shift. Morphling deals mixed damage and scales harder into late game. Razor’s lack of burst makes Morphling difficult to punish.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Anti-Mage avoids Static Link completely with Blink. Mana Break prevents Razor from casting spells consistently. Razor cannot chase Anti-Mage effectively and loses in split-push scenarios. In the late game, Anti-Mage scales far beyond Razor’s power peak.

pairs.name: Chen
pairs.reason: Chen can heal allies through Razor’s damage over time. Summoned creeps tank Eye of the Storm and block Plasma Field. Razor’s single-target nature cannot overcome Chen’s team-based sustain. Chen thrives in fights Razor tries to isolate.

pairs.name: Weaver
pairs.reason: Weaver kites Razor easily and avoids Static Link with Shukuchi. Razor cannot chase or lockdown Weaver reliably. Time Lapse removes Razor’s chip damage and resets engagements. Razor gets outmaneuvered and outscaled over time.

pairs.name: Techies
pairs.reason: Techies sets mines that punish Razor’s linear chasing. Razor often overextends and walks into Proximity Mines. Static Link does not stop Techies’ area control and zoning. Razor is vulnerable during fights and cannot burst Techies.

pairs.name: Lifestealer
pairs.reason: Lifestealers Rage provides Magic Resistance and Debuff Immunity which helps with all of Sandkings Spells.

pairs.name: Juggernaut
pairs.reason: Blade Fury provides Magic Resistance and Debuff Immunity which helps with all of Sandkings Spells.

pairs.name: Wraith King
pairs.reason: Sand King relies on comboing enemies from 100 to 0 using Epicenter and Burrowstrike. However, Wraith King's Reincarnation makes him a poor target, as Sand King usually doesn't want to commit his full combo on a hero who immediately comes back to life

pairs.name: Ursa
pairs.reason: Ursa can pressure Sand King in lane because Fury Swipes deal significant damage, and as a melee hero, Sand King often struggles to trade effectively. Additionally, Ursa’s Enrage helps him mitigate much of Sand King’s combo damage, allowing Ursa to survive and stay in the fight longer

pairs.name: Oracle
pairs.reason: Oracle can consistently save allies targeted by Sand King using False Promise and Fate’s Edict, either allowing them to keep fighting or completely mitigating the burst of magical damage Sand King deals

pairs.name: Vengeful Spirit
pairs.reason: Vengeful Spirit can save her allies by using Nether Swap to reposition them away from Sand King’s Sandstorm and Epicenter after he initiates. However, if she has Aghanim's Scepter, Sand King tends to avoid committing his full combo on her due to the threat of her second life

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Mana Break can quickly burn Storm Spirit's mana, preventing him from escaping. Blink allows Anti-Mage to catch up to Storm Spirit when he tries to use his Ball Lightning to escape. Mana Void deals massive damage to Storm Spirit as well as his teammates, as Storm Spirit depletes his mana pool by using Ball Lightning. Counterspell's passive magic resistance reduces much of Storm Spirit's magical damage dealt to Anti-Mage, and the active aspect may even make Storm Spirit disable himself

pairs.name: Doom
pairs.reason: Doom prevents Storm Spirit from using all of his abilities and items, rendering Storm Spirit useless in a fight.

pairs.name: Ember Spirit
pairs.reason: Flame Guard absorbs up to 500 magical damage (700 with Level 10 talents), which helps Ember Spirit survive against Storm Spirit's high magical damage. Searing Chains can root enemies up to 3 seconds, making Storm Spirit unable to escape with Ball Lightning. Fire Remnant deals high magical damage when casting multiple instances at once, granting Ember Spirit the damage to burst Storm Spirit down in the early to mid game.

pairs.name: Silencer
pairs.reason: Silencer can permanently silence Storm Spirit once he jumps in, especially if Storm doesn’t have a BKB. Global Silence shuts down Storm’s mobility and spell usage, making him an easy target for follow-up disables and burst. Without BKB, Storm is extremely vulnerable to Silencer’s kit.

pairs.name: Meepo
pairs.reason: Meepo can lock down Storm Spirit using his Earthbind (net) and burst him quickly with Poof combos. If Meepo catches Storm without backup, he can prevent Storm’s escape and secure a kill before Storm can react.

pairs.name: Puck
pairs.reason: Storm Spirit cannot escape Puck’s Coil, and Puck’s Silence completely disables him, preventing any spell usage or escape. This makes Storm extremely vulnerable during fights if caught by Puck’s setup, especially without BKB

pairs.name: Night Stalker
pairs.reason: Night Stalker’s superior night vision and silence make it difficult for Storm Spirit to safely commit to teamfights. The silence prevents Storm from using his spells or escaping, while Night Stalker’s vision control limits Storm’s ability to roam and initiate.

pairs.name: Bane
pairs.reason: Bane can lock down Storm Spirit with Fiend’s Grip and Nightmare, disabling his mobility and burst potential.

pairs.name: Tidehunter
pairs.reason: Storm Spirit cannot use Ball Lightning if Tide hunter casts Dead in the Water on him.

pairs.name: Razor
pairs.reason: Razors high movement speed will kite and Static Link will sap Sven's insane attack damage, and it even goes through Black King Bar.

pairs.name: Medusa
pairs.reason: Mana Shield makes it very hard for Sven to burst her within Storm Hammer's stun duration. Stone Gaze makes it very difficult for Sven to fight Medusa at any stage of the game.

pairs.name: Axe
pairs.reason: Berserker's Call prevents Sven from bursting his targets before Axe can interfere. The worst kind of opponent for Sven is one who can stop him from attacking who he wants to, which is exactly what Axe does. Culling Blade may finish off Sven before he has the chance to lifesteal or run with Warcry. Axe is a very common Blade Mail carrier which will make very short work of a Sven with God's Strength activated.

pairs.name: Slardar
pairs.reason: Slardar shreds Sven's high armor advantage with Corrosive Haze, turning him from a tank into a glass cannon. Slardar’s bash interrupts Sven's movement and combos, making it harder to burst down targets. Once Slardar initiates first, Sven often gets killed before even casting his ult. Vision from Haze also makes Sven’s farming patterns more predictable.

pairs.name: Troll Warlord
pairs.reason: Troll Warlord thrives in long, drawn-out fights, while Sven is all about quick bursts with God Strength. If Troll survives Sven’s combo, he wins the fight almost every time with his attack speed and Battle Trance. Troll also builds Basher and Satanic, making him tanky and hard to kite. Sven's stun is unreliable if Troll gets BKB first.

pairs.name: Templar Assassin
pairs.reason: Templar Assassin is a huge problem for Sven because of her Refraction, which blocks his burst damage and wastes his God Strength window. She can kite Sven using her traps and outrange him while keeping her armor intact. If Sven doesn’t have nullifier , TA can dodge most of his pressure. Her faster farming tempo also outpaces Sven's in many games.

pairs.name: Phantom Assassin
pairs.reason: Phantom Assassin is a nightmare if Sven doesn't build Monkey King Bar, since her Blur and evasion allow her to survive his burst. Once PA gets Desolator and BKB, she can outfight Sven with faster crits. Her mobility lets her dodge Warcry's effectiveness and reach Sven’s supports first. If Sven’s combo fails, he becomes easy prey.

pairs.name: Bristleback
pairs.reason: Bristleback is simply too tanky for Sven to deal with, especially in prolonged fights. Sven’s physical damage feeds Quill Spray, which returns more punishment the longer the fight goes. Bristle shrugs off burst and builds items like Crimson Guard and Shiva’s, further reducing Sven’s impact. He becomes impossible to kill without magic burst.

pairs.name: Lifestealer
pairs.reason: Lifestealer is a direct counter due to his Rage, which makes him magic immune and immune to Storm Hammer. He sustains through Sven’s physical burst with Feast and Armlet, outlasting Sven in a man-fight. Lifestealer can also infest into tanky allies to initiate safely. Sven has a small window to act before he’s kited and brought down.

pairs.name: Phoenix
pairs.reason: Phoenix completely ruins Sven’s teamfight with Supernova, which requires physical attacks to destroy. Sven can’t hit fast enough during BKB, especially with Phoenix slowing attack speed. The Sun Ray also cuts through Sven’s high HP pool, and Fire Spirits reduce his DPS to nothing. Phoenix is a strong disengage tool when Sven jumps in.

pairs.name: Enchantress
pairs.reason: Enchantress takes very little damage from Sven’s right-clicks due to Untouchable, drastically slowing his attack speed. She also uses Nature’s Attendants to heal through his burst. Sven relies on speed to kill squishy heroes, and Enchantress is anything but. With proper positioning, she kites him endlessly with slows and range.

pairs.name: Batrider
pairs.reason: Batrider counters Sven with his Flaming Lasso, which pulls him away from the fight and wastes his ult duration. The sticky napalm stacks reduce Sven’s mobility and make him easy to kill. Even with BKB, Batrider can reposition Sven and throw off his whole initiation. Sven can’t stand and fight when constantly being moved and slowed.

pairs.name: Alchemist
pairs.reason: Tiny naturally has high base attack damage due to his ult - Grow. Alch is capable of reducing it with Corrosive Weaponry and cripple Tiny's overall damage output significantly. Alch acquires items quite fast to build up his HP pool, making it hard for Tiny to burst him with a single Toss + Avalanche + Tree Throw combo and can quickly heal back up with Chemical Rage.

pairs.name: Lifestealer
pairs.reason: Lifestealer’s Rage makes him immune to all of Tiny’s magic-based combo. He out-sustains Tiny in fights and bursts him with Feast damage. Tiny can’t kill Lifestealer unless he’s controlled by someone else. Lifestealer shrugs off every spell and punishes his low armor.

pairs.name: Necrophos
pairs.reason: Necrophos shrugs off Tiny’s burst with sustain and Ghost Shroud. Reaper’s Scythe punishes Tiny’s low status resistance early. Avalanche and Toss do little once Necrophos is tanky. He scales better and punishes Tiny’s lack of BKB early.

pairs.name: Enchantress
pairs.reason: Enchantress survives early burst with Untouchable and heal. Tiny cannot deal enough right-click damage to finish her off. Nature’s Attendants keeps her alive through Avalanche Toss. She dominates long fights where Tiny runs out of impact.

pairs.name: Undying
pairs.reason: Undying’s zombies and Tombstone make it hard for Tiny to engage. Decay reduces Tiny’s damage and survivability. Tiny’s burst is wasted on tanky targets like Undying who soaks up spell combos that would otherwise kill squishies heroes.

pairs.name: Death Prophet
pairs.reason: Tiny can’t burst Death Prophet fast enough to prevent Spirit Siphon. Exorcism forces him to disengage as he can’t trade in teamfights. Death Prophet tanks the combo and punishes Tiny during cooldowns. Her sustained DPS scales better.

pairs.name: Underlord
pairs.reason: Underlord punishes Tiny with Pit of Malice and high base health regen. Firestorm burns him down after his initial combo. Tiny can’t deal with tanky frontliners without follow-up damage. Underlord’s root delays Tiny’s escape and cuts his impact.

pairs.name: Ember Spirit
pairs.reason: Ember Spirit dodges Avalanche with Sleight of Fist and escapes Toss with Remnant. His magic immunity scaling punishes Tiny’s reliance on burst. Tiny can’t lock him down without extra disable. Ember punishes any missed combo with high DPS.

pairs.name: Viper
pairs.reason: Viper zones Tiny out of lane with poison and breaks his armor gains. Nethertoxin prevents combo usage under towers. Tiny gets melted by damage-over-time effects and lacks sustain. He can’t fight back once Viper gets even a slight lead.

pairs.name: Huskar
pairs.reason: Huskar shrugs off burst and punishes Tiny with Burning Spear stacks. His passive makes Avalanche’s burst less effective. Once Huskar gets armlet or BKB, Tiny has no way to stop him. Huskar snowballs past Tiny before he finishes his core items.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: Venge struggles to deal with PL’s illusions and has no AoE clear. Swap becomes ineffective when she can’t identify the real one. Her armor reduction barely affects his illusion damage. PL overwhelms Venge by dragging fights out.

pairs.name: Naga Siren
pairs.reason: Naga's illusions ignore armor reduction and punish Venge’s low AoE. Her Song of the Siren cancels Venge’s aggression and resets fights. Naga scales far better and pushes lanes too quickly. Venge can’t control the tempo late game.

pairs.name: Elder Titan
pairs.reason: Elder Titan removes base armor with Natural Order, making Venge and her illusions extremely vulnerable. His stun and stomp combo disable her before she casts. ET’s AoE zoning keeps her away from her ideal positioning. Venge becomes fragile in fights.

pairs.name: Brewmaster
pairs.reason: Brew’s Primal Split ruins Venge’s coordination and prevents focus fire. He can cyclone Venge or her carry during Swap attempts. Brew’s survivability means her armor reduction has less value. Venge can’t stop him once he splits.

pairs.name: Terrorblade
pairs.reason: Terrorblade shrugs off armor debuffs with high stats and illusions. Venge can’t disable him long enough to prevent Sunder. His illusions melt her with right clicks. Swap doesn’t remove his massive damage presence from the fight.

pairs.name: Sand King
pairs.reason: Sand King punishes grouped positioning and burst-kills Venge with Epicenter. Her low HP and low BKB priority make her vulnerable. Venge gets zoned out by Caustic Finale and Burrowstrike. Her tools can’t stop his AoE damage output.

pairs.name: Chaos Knight
pairs.reason: CK’s illusions overwhelm Venge, and she lacks tools to deal with the chaos. Swap is ineffective when he pulls in a target and spawns illusions around them. Venge's low armor becomes a liability. CK benefits from extended messy engagements.

pairs.name: Beastmaster
pairs.reason: Beastmaster’s long-range disable pierces BKB and cancels Venge’s presence. His summons ignore her armor debuffs and help push. Roar stops Swap from saving anyone. Beastmaster takes map control quickly and snowballs harder.

pairs.name: Muerta
pairs.reason: Venge’s spells don’t affect Muerta during Pierce the Veil. Swap does nothing when she’s ethereal. Her range punishes Venge for poor positioning. Venge’s toolkit fails against Muerta’s unique mechanics and range.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: AM jumps backlines and punishes Venge’s low mobility. She can’t disable him long enough to kill him. AM ignores her armor debuff and escapes before dying. Mana Break ruins her low mana pool, and she has no lockdown to stop him.

pairs.name: Centaur Warrunner
pairs.reason: Retaliate will shred through Windranger's health if she chooses to attack him during Focus Fire. Stampede can help his teammates escape from Windrun and Focus Fire.

pairs.name: Bloodseeker
pairs.reason: Rupture turns Windranger's mobility against her. Blood Rite's silence makes Windranger totally useless, since she's extremely reliant on abilities.

pairs.name: Axe
pairs.reason: Windranger’s long channeling Focus Fire makes her a prime target for Berserker’s Call. Axe forces her to attack him, triggering counter helix and controlling her. She gets countered hard during her burst window.

pairs.name: Tiny
pairs.reason: Tiny can burst Windranger instantly with Avalanche and Toss combo. Her Windrun does nothing to stop his magic burst and toss disables her mobility. She has trouble locking him down before he deletes her. He invalidates her midgame power spikes with his quick burst.

pairs.name: Queen of Pain
pairs.reason: Queen of Pain bursts Windranger down with Scream and Sonic Wave before she can Windrun. Her mobility allows her to escape Focus Fire and avoid Shackleshot setups. Windranger can’t contest her laning pressure or match her tempo. Queen of Pain thrives against squishy mids like her.

pairs.name: Clockwerk
pairs.reason: Clockwerk traps Windranger inside Power Cogs, forcing her to use Windrun defensively. Battery Assault cancels her channeling abilities like Focus Fire and Powershot. She gets isolated and controlled before she can contribute. Clockwerk punishes her weak escapes under pressure.

pairs.name: Arc Warden
pairs.reason: Arc Warden out-ranges Windranger and uses double Magnetic Fields to evade her damage. His clone soaks Shackleshot and Focus Fire, wasting her cooldowns. He forces Windranger to commit spells inefficiently. Over time, he zones her out and controls the map safely.

pairs.name: Tusk
pairs.reason: Tusk closes the gap on Windranger with Snowball and disables her with Walrus Punch. He tanks her initial burst and returns with high-impact control. Shackleshot is hard to land reliably on him. Windrun cannot save her from physical burst while stunned or isolated.

pairs.name: Razor
pairs.reason: Razor drains Windranger’s damage with Static Link, making her Focus Fire weak. Windrun does not stop his movement-based chase or Eye of the Storm. She cannot trade damage effectively in prolonged fights. Razor punishes her need to stay close during engagements.

pairs.name: Kunkka
pairs.reason: Kunkka catches Windranger with X Mark and follows with Torrent and Boat combo. Her Windrun doesn’t dodge his magic burst or disable chain. He forces fights where her mobility is ineffective. Kunkka can out-tank and control her in most encounters.

pairs.name: Storm Spirit
pairs.reason: Storm counters Zeus by using Ball Lightning to quickly close the gap and dodge Zeus’s spells. His mobility and Electric Vortex allow him to lock Zeus down, preventing him from casting spells and bursting him down before Zeus can react.

pairs.name: Meepo
pairs.reason: Meepo can chain Net to lock down Zeus and quickly burst him down with multiple clones, making it hard for Zeus to escape or cast spells effectively.

pairs.name: Broodmother
pairs.reason: Broodmother’s webs let her sustain against Zeus’s nukes by providing regeneration and damage reduction. Her mobility in the webs also allows her to chase down Zeus easily, making it hard for him to escape.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Anti-Mage’s built-in magic resistance reduces Zeus’s damage, making it harder for him to burst AM down. Additionally, Anti-Mage can reflect Zeus’s spells with Counterspell and quickly kill him using Mana Void when Zeus’s mana is low.

pairs.name: Void Spirit
pairs.reason: Void Spirit can quickly close the gap on Zeus and burst him down. His Resonant Pulse allows him to block incoming magic damage, reducing Zeus’s burst effectiveness and giving him an edge in fights.

pairs.name: Tusk
pairs.reason: Tusk can easily gank Zeus in the early game, punishing his low mobility. In the late game, Tusk’s Snowball can save allies by blocking damage, reducing the effectiveness of Zeus’s spells in team fights.

pairs.name: Ember Spirit
pairs.reason: Ember Spirit can use Sleight of Fist to dodge Zeus’s spells, while Flame Guard blocks magical damage, allowing him to tank Zeus’s burst and effectively take him down.

pairs.name: Io
pairs.reason: Io provides constant healing and sustain to allies, making it difficult for Zeus to secure kills. With items like Mekansm and Glimmer Cape, Io can keep teammates alive through Zeus’s burst damage.

pairs.name: Brewmaster
pairs.reason: Brewmaster is naturally tanky, and when low on health, he can use Primal Split to avoid damage and negate Zeus’s spells by splitting into his elemental clones, making it harder for Zeus to finish him off.

pairs.name: Timbersaw
pairs.reason: He shrugs off Kunkka’s physical damage with Reactive Armor. Kunkka lacks magic burst to bring him down. Timber also out-pushes and controls lanes faster than Kunkka.

pairs.name: Lifestealer
pairs.reason: Lifestealer is immune to X-Torrent combo while Rage is active. He can use Infest to dodge Boat and burst squishy supports around Kunkka. Kunkka struggles to kite or kill a fat Lifestealer.

pairs.name: Alchemist
pairs.reason: Alchemist farms faster and scales harder than Kunkka. Acid Spray + Radiance burn ruins Kunkka’s Cleave-focused fighting style. He tanks through combo and recovers instantly with regen or BKB

pairs.name: Juggernaut
pairs.reason: Blade Fury dodges Torrent and Boat entirely. Juggernaut can Omnislash Kunkka before he combos. Healing Ward sustains his team through Cleave poke.

pairs.name: Undying
pairs.reason: Undying punishes long fights, which Kunkka prefers. Tombstone demands early team fight items, delaying Kunkka’s damage output. He also reduces Kunkka’s strength, weakening his tankiness over time. Undying can save teammates with Tombstone by buyying aghanim's shard nullifying kunkka combo's.

pairs.name: Pangolier
pairs.reason: Highly mobile, Pangolier dodges Torrent/Boat combos easily. Rolling Thunder stuns Kunkka before he can cast anything. Cleave is less effective against a hero who jumps in and out of fights.

pairs.name: Venomancer
pairs.reason: Venomancer’s spells disables Blink Dagger and punishes grouped-up teamfighting. Kunkka lacks sustain and usually doesn’t build magic resistance items . Venomancer slows Kunkka and his allies, making it hard to chase or disengage.

pairs.name: Ember Spirit
pairs.reason: Ember dodges Torrent and Boat with Sleight and Remnant. He out-farms Kunkka, has high mobility, and pokes from a safe distance.Tidebringer rarely hits him, and he punishes Kunkka’s long cooldowns.

pairs.name: Elder Titan
pairs.reason: ET reduces armor, punishing Kunkka’s high-HP, low-armor build. Spirit + Stomp combo can cancel Kunkka’s setup and isolate him. He scales better in teamfights and destroys Kunkka.

pairs.name: Abaddon
pairs.reason: Lina can never combo and kill Abaddon with all her spells as long as Borrowed Time is off cooldown. Aphotic Shield and Mist Coil also protect his allies from dying to Lina's spells. Once Abaddon gets Blink Dagger, he can jump Lina and run her down with the movement speed slow through Curse of Avernus, and forces Lina to play defensively.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Lina struggles to fend off Anti Mage, who can easily Blink next to her and burst her down with Mana Void after draining her mana through his right clicks empowered with Mana Break. Anti Mage also has the potential to block and reflect Lina's Laguna Blade damage back to her with Counterspell. Counterspell also provides magic resistance to reduce a lot of Lina's burst damage from her spell combo.

pairs.name: Centaur Warrunner
pairs.reason: Centaur Warrunner's high HP from his Innate, strength gain, and item purchases prevents Lina from bursting him down with her spell combo. Once Centaur gets Blade Mail, he can reflect a lot of Lina's burst damage back to her in combination with Retaliate and threaten her life every time. Stampede also lets Centaur's entire team close the gap on a squishy Lina and burst her down.

pairs.name: Doom
pairs.reason: Doom completely shuts down Lina with his ultimate as she cannot throw any spells in its duration to fight back or fend off Doom with the Light Strike Array stun. Doom can easily run down a slow and squishy Lina during Scorched Earth and finish her off every time while his ultimate is active.

pairs.name: Ember Spirit
pairs.reason: Ember Spirit's Sleight of Fist lets him dodge Lina's Light Strike Array and Dragon Slave when timed correctly. With the Orb of Corrosion purchase in the laning stage, Ember Spirit can also harass and threaten Lina's life with the Sleight of Fist and Searing Chains combo. The Flame Guard barrier also lets Ember Spirit absorb a lot of Lina's burst damage from her spells, while he can also close the gap or get away with Fire Remnant.

pairs.name: Faceless Void
pairs.reason: Faceless Void's Time Walk lets him reverse the damage taken from Lina's entire spell combo if he doesn't get bursted down from full to zero. Faceless Void's Chronosphere also locks down a squishy Lina and makes for easy kills throughout the game. Time Dilation also prevents Lina from using her low cooldown spells multiple times in fights.

pairs.name: Huskar
pairs.reason: Huskar's Berserker's Blood passive keeps him healthy and provides magic resistance during the laning stage and prevents Lina from building a massive advantage with her long range harass from spells and right clicks. Huskar can also return the aggression on a squishy Lina with the gap close through Life Break, followed up with the Inner Fire silence and Burning Spears.

pairs.name: Invoker
pairs.reason: Lina relies on slowly poking and wearing down opposing mid laners with her long range spells and right clicks, which is countered by Invoker with the inbuilt HP regen provided by Quas. Lina also relies heavily on mana for her lane domination, which is heavily countered by the mana burn from EMP. Lina is also a squishy hero and is easily killed by Invoker's spell combo.

pairs.name: Kez
pairs.reason: Kez's high mobility lets him find easy kills on a squishy Lina who finds it incredibly difficult to fend him off with Light Strike Array because of the Talon Toss silence as well as Kez's high mobility. Kez's ultimate Raptor Dance also gives him magic damage immunity to nullify Lina's damage spells.

pairs.name: Lifestealer
pairs.reason: Lifestealer's Rage provides him debuff immunity and magic resistance to avoid the Light Strike Array stun as well as reduce the damage taken from Lina's spell combo. Lifestealer's Infest bomb and Open Wounds slow also lets him stay on top of a squishy Lina and poke her down with his right clicks.

pairs.name: Night Stalker
pairs.reason: Night Stalker's Crippling Fear silence under the Void movement speed slow prevents Lina from running away from him or fending him off with the Light Strike Array stun. Dark Ascension's massive vision and flying movement also helps Night Stalker find and get close to Lina every time, which is further enabled with the Blink Dagger purchase.

pairs.name: Nyx Assassin
pairs.reason: Nyx Assassin always has kill threat on a squishy Lina with Vendetta and follow up spell combo alongside Dagon. Lina's high mana pool works against her as it lets Nyx Assassin do even more damage to her with Mind Flare. Nyx Assassin can also use Lina's AoE damage spells to stun her with Spiked Carapace, particularly when she farms creep waves.

pairs.name: Oracle
pairs.reason: Oracle's Fate's Edict prevents all of Lina's burst damage from her spells and can waste her entire combo when timed correctly. False Promise also dispels the Light Strike Array stun and works well to prevent Lina from bursting anyone down with her spells and right clicks.

pairs.name: Puck
pairs.reason: Puck's high attack range and damage nukes gives her an even footing against Lina in the laning stage. Puck's Phase Shift also lets her dodge Lina's Light Strike Array and Dragon Slave when timed correctly. Illusory Orb and Waning Rift also let Puck close the gap on a squishy Lina to keep her leashed under Dream Coil and burst her down while she is silenced.

pairs.name: Silencer
pairs.reason: Silener's silence through Global Silence and Last Word can completely disrupt Lina's spell combo throughout the game and render her useless in teamfights. Arcane Curse also lets Silencer do a lot of slow and damage to Lina if she casts her spell combo while affected by the spell.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: Slark can easily time Dark Pact to dispel the Light Strike Array stun because of its cast time, which helps him use Shadow Dance before Lina can target him with Laguna Blade and right clicks. Slark's Pounce also lets him close the gap on a squishy Lina and keep her leashed to bring her down with his right clicks, or steal a ton of Essence Shift stacks at the very least.

pairs.name: Spectre
pairs.reason: Spectre's Shadow Step lets her instantly get on top of a squishy Lina and makes for easy pickoffs on her when accompanied by another hero. The matchup progresses further in Spectre's favor as the game goes on when she builds up her HP pool to prevent dying to Lina's spell combo as well as return a ton of damage through Dispersion.

pairs.name: Storm Spirit
pairs.reason: Storm Spirit's high attack range and Static Remnant gives him an even footing to contest creeps as well as harass Lina with the Static Slide facet. Past the laning stage, Storm Spirit's Ball Lightning gives him mobility to close the gap on a squishy Lina to burst her down as well as dodge the Light Strike Array stun.

pairs.name: Viper
pairs.reason: Viper's high attack range on top of Poison Attack stacks and Corrosive Skin let him threaten Lina's life in the laning stage and prevents her from building a massive advantage the way she does in most matchups. Once Viper reaches level 6, Viper Strike also adds to the kill threat on Lina. Corrosive Skin also provides magic resistance to reduce a lot of Lina's damage through her spells.

pairs.name: Tidehunter
pairs.reason: Blubber can dispel both Earth Spike and Hex without a cooldown essentially, as long as Tide is taking sufficient damage and can survie it. This makes Tide impossible to initiate on without a Break as upon dispelling the crowd control with Blubber he can instantly "turn the tide" with Ravage.

pairs.name: Spectre
pairs.reason: Shadow Step allows Spectre to consistently get on top of Lion and dirsupt him from efficiently using his Earth Spike and Hex. Spectral Dagger allows Spectre to track him down even in Glimmer Cape and Dispersion makes it hard for Lion to fight back with Finger of Death.

pairs.name: Rubick
pairs.reason: Rubick takes Lion's kit and turns it against him and his team, but better. Spell Steal increases the duration of both Earth Spike and Hex, while Arcane Supremacy increases the damage of Earth Spike and Finger of Death. Might and Magus provides additional Magic Resistance to Rubick making him suprisingly tanky versus Lion's exclusive magic damage kit.

pairs.name: Visage
pairs.reason: Gravekeeper's Cloak makes it hard for Lion to burst down Visage with Finger of Death. Visage tends to pressure towers early with his Familiars, which Lion struggles with due to his lack of strong wave clear. Most importantly, Visage can just go "Sic 'em, boys!" and unleash his Familiars on Lion as he lacks the innate damage block to mitigate their high frequency of attacks as he a ranged hero.

pairs.name: Lifestealer
pairs.reason: Rage prevents Lion from controlling Lifestealer with Earth Spike or Hex, while mitigating most of his damage. Infest can be used to save an ally from being bursted by Finger of Death or to heal back Lifestealer up and reset his resources to keep fighting.

pairs.name: Beastmaster
pairs.reason: Beastmaster’s summoned units make it difficult for Lion to commit to his spells, often forcing him to target the wrong unit. Beastmaster can also soak up Lion’s damage and use his summons to quickly eliminate Lion from the fight, limiting his impact

pairs.name: Phantom Assassin
pairs.reason: Lion is very squishy and can be burst down quickly by Phantom Assassin. Once PA gets BKB, Lion’s disables become almost useless.

pairs.name: Rubick
pairs.reason: Lion has strong disables, but Rubick can turn the tide by stealing key spells like Hex or Finger of Death. Rubick’s longer range and spell versatility give him an edge in drawn-out fights. Positioning and timing are crucial for Lion to avoid getting outplayed.

pairs.name: Gyrocopter
pairs.reason: Gyro’s AoE damage can quickly burst Lion down due to his low HP. Lion must pick his timings well to avoid getting caught in Flak Cannon and Call Down.

pairs.name: Visage
pairs.reason: Visage’s familiars interrupt Shackles and easily cancel any channeling. His burst damage deletes Shadow Shaman quickly, and he’s tanky enough to survive wards with Cloak and Gravekeeper’s Cloak.

pairs.name: Terrorblade
pairs.reason: Terrorblade's illusions easily kill Serpent Wards while he remains untouched. Shadow Shaman lacks the AoE tools to clear illusions, and he dies in a few hits if caught out.

pairs.name: Lone Druid
pairs.reason: Lone Druid’s bear can break Shackles or tank Serpent Wards while the Druid focuses down Shaman. The dual-target threat makes it hard to lock him down properly in fights.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: Too many illusions for Shadow Shaman to deal with. His single-target disables are ineffective against a flood of clones, and PL can easily slip past wards and isolate him.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
