pairs.reason: Naga overwhelms Shadow Shaman with illusions. Song of the Siren also resets teamfights, negating his wards or Shackles mid-fight.

pairs.name: Beastmaster
pairs.reason: Beastmaster’s summons cancel Shackles. Primal Roar can easily kill or disable Shadow Shaman before he casts anything. He also pushes harder and faster.

pairs.name: Ringmaster
pairs.reason: Ringmaster can outplay Shadow Shaman with mobility and overwhelming burst. He excels at killing squishy supports and can disengage from Serpent Wards quickly with his toolkit.

pairs.name: Wraith King
pairs.reason: Shadow Shaman’s long disables don’t matter much against a hero with Reincarnation. Once Wraith King revives, he can charge down Shaman with ease, especially when BKB is up.

pairs.name: Hoodwink
pairs.reason: Hoodwink keeps distance and punishes static casters. She can interrupt Shackles with Acorn Shot + Bushwhack and quickly reposition after dealing damage. Shadow Shaman can’t catch her alone.

pairs.name: Gyrocopter
pairs.reason: Gyrocopter thrives in chaos and area fights, while Shadow Shaman wants controlled skirmishes. His Rocket Barrage and Flak Cannon make short work of Shaman if he’s not protected by teammates.

pairs.name: Abaddon
pairs.reason: Abaddon can cast Aphotic Shield on any of his allies to immediately dispel Corrosive Haze and/or the stun and the slow components of Slithereen Crush. All of Slardar's debuffs are also removed if Abaddon's Borrowed Time triggers.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: Phantom Lancer's Doppelganger has a low cooldown and applies a basic dispel on PL, making it hard to keep Corrosive Haze on him. Phantom Lancer usually purchases Manta Style which provides another basic dispel to remove Corrosive Haze with. Besides Slithereen Crush, Slardar does not have another way to deal with illusions and has a low mana pool, which allows Phantom Lancer with Diffusal Blade to quickly build up illusions while draining Slardar's mana.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: Dark Pact purges off Corrosive Haze quickly and can pre-cast it to remove the Slithereen Crush stun duration, which removes Slardar's key tool for chasing and bursting. Shadow Dance makes Slark untargetable, so even if he’s low, Slardar can’t finish him off during that duration.

pairs.name: Chaos Knight
pairs.reason: Chaos Knight overwhelms Slardar with multiple illusions, making it hard for him to focus the real hero even with Corrosive Haze. Slardar’s single-target focus struggles against CK’s chaos and burst. CK also has high physical damage that melts Slardar before he can sustain in fights. Slardar’s armor reduction has little value when CK overwhelms him with illusion-based damage. Manta style and phantasm dispel corrosive haze.

pairs.name: Terrorblade
pairs.reason: Terrorblade is another illusion-based hero who shrugs off Slardar’s armor reduction thanks to high armor and multiple units. Once he gets Manta and Satanic, he easily outlasts Slardar in fights. Slardar has no way to clear illusions efficiently, which weakens his impact in late game. Terrorblade also punishes Slardar’s aggression with strong counter-initiation.

pairs.name: Dragon Knight
pairs.reason: Dragon Knight has incredibly high base armor and tankiness, which makes Corrosive Haze less effective. Slardar can’t burst him down fast enough before DK’s natural tanking and healing kick in. Dragon Knight can also outlast fights and push objectives, something Slardar doesn't handle well. In lane, DK sustains easily through any physical harassment Slardar attempts.

pairs.name: Troll Warlord
pairs.reason: Troll Warlord excels in prolonged fights, which is dangerous for Slardar, who depends on quick kills. Troll’s attack speed and lifesteal allow him to beat Slardar head-on after the initial stun. Once Troll ults, he becomes unkillable for Slardar, who lacks disarms or hard disables. Slardar’s armor reduction doesn't stop Troll from scaling through raw stats.

pairs.name: Naga Siren
pairs.reason: Naga Siren overwhelms Slardar with illusions that waste his bash and spread damage. Her Song of the Siren also resets fights, making Slardar’s aggressive dives less impactful. Slardar struggles to lock her down once she builds Manta or Heart. Illusions also soak up Slardar’s physical damage, rendering him inefficient.

pairs.name: Drow Ranger
pairs.reason: Drow Ranger punishes melee heroes like Slardar with high ranged damage and slow. If Slardar fails to jump her instantly, she can kite and kill him easily with her Gust silence and damage burst. Slardar also doesn’t scale as well into late game compared to her.

pairs.name: Muerta
pairs.reason: Muerta becomes untargetable by physical damage during Pierce the Veil, making Slardar's entire skillset useless. Slardar can’t bash or hit her during this phase, and Muerta can burst him with magical damage. Even before her ult, she kites Slardar easily with her range and movement tools. He gets no value out of his armor reduction against her.

pairs.name: Luna
pairs.reason: Luna outputs heavy magical and physical damage and scales better in teamfights. Her Lucent Beam and Eclipse burst Slardar down before he can even react. Slardar’s melee nature makes him vulnerable to her glaive bounces and AoE. Once farmed, Luna destroys him in both 1v1 and team scenarios.

pairs.name: Tidehunter
pairs.reason: Tidehunter naturally counters physical burst with Kraken Shell and extremely high durability. Slardar can’t reduce enough armor to kill him before Ravage turns the fight. Tide’s teamfight presence is more impactful, while Slardar offers mostly pickoff. In lane, Tide’s tankiness and spam make it hard for Slardar to apply pressure. Kraken shell when triggered also dispels corrosive haze

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Mana Break quickly burns Tidehunter's mana pool, preventing him from spamming his abilities, and Kraken Shell does not mitigate the bonus damage component. Blink allows Anti-Mage to enter combat quickly and safely after Ravage. A well-timed Counterspell can reflect Gush back at Tidehunter.

pairs.name: Ursa
pairs.reason: Fury Swipes will keep stacking on Tidehunter since it cannot be dispelled by Kraken Shell and its bonus damage cannot be reduced by Anchor Smash. Enrage dispels the slow from Gush, and if upgraded with Aghanim's Scepter, can even dispel Ravage's stun.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: Dark Pact dispels debuffs from Gush, Anchor Smash and even Ravage if timed correctly. Kraken Shell cannot restore attributes stolen by Essence Shift or dispel the leash if he gets Pounced.

pairs.name: Witch Doctor
pairs.reason: Maledict is highly effective against tanky heroes like Tidehunter and can help burst him down in lane. Additionally, Witch Doctor’s Death Ward deals pure damage, which cannot be mitigated by Kraken Shell

pairs.name: Outworld Devourer
pairs.reason: Outworld Devourer’s Arcane Orb deals pure damage, bypassing Kraken Shell. His ultimate can burst Tidehunter due to Tide’s relatively low mana pool, and Astral Imprisonment can save allies from Ravage, making him a tough matchup

pairs.name: Necrophos
pairs.reason: Necrophos excels at dealing magical damage to tanky heroes like Tidehunter. His Reaper’s Scythe can quickly finish Tide off, if he gets low on health.

pairs.name: Undying
pairs.reason: Undying’s Decay steals strength, making Tidehunter squishier during the laning phase. Additionally, Tidehunter struggles to deal with Tombstone and its zombies.

pairs.name: Lifestealer
pairs.reason: Feast lets Lifestealer deal heavy damage to Tidehunter while healing himself, making trades unfavorable. His Rage ability also counters Ravage, making Lifestealer a difficult matchup throughout the game.

pairs.name: Puck
pairs.reason: Puck can easily dodge your Paralyzing cask and Maledict as well as Silence you during Death Ward.

pairs.name: Templar Assassin
pairs.reason: Templar's Reflection uses instances to negate damage and all of Witch Doctors spells are instance damage. Witch Doctor also has low armor which Templar Assassin can reduce even further with Meld.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Anti-Mage can easily deflect your predictable Paralyzing Cask and set you up for a kill, in addition he can blink away from trouble or blink in pre-emptively with Counter Spell.

pairs.name: Medusa
pairs.reason: Her Mana Shield makes her hard to kill with Death Ward or Maledict. She also outlasts long fights where Witch Doctor is most dangerous.

pairs.name: Pangolier
pairs.reason: Constant mobility and spell immunity during Rolling Thunder make it hard for Witch Doctor to channel Death Ward or land Cask and Maledict effectively.
– When she activates Pierce the Veil, she becomes immune to physical damage, completely negating Death Ward. She can also burst Witch Doctor quickly.

pairs.name: Faceless Void
pairs.reason: Chronosphere completely disables Witch Doctor, often catching him before he can cast Death Ward. Void also excels at bursting supports.

pairs.name: Riki
pairs.reason: Can sneak up and silence Witch Doctor with Smoke Screen and Tricks of the Trade, preventing spellcasting. Hard to detect pre-dust/gem.

pairs.name: Morphling
pairs.reason: Can shift strength to survive Maledict and Death Ward. Once he gets his core items, he can burst Witch Doctor in seconds.

pairs.name: Sand King
pairs.reason: Blink + Burrowstrike cancels Death Ward easily. His Sandstorm forces Witch Doctor to buy detection. SK's magic damage bursts him fast.

pairs.name: Bristleback
pairs.reason: Death Ward and Maledict deal little due to his Bristleback passive and high tankiness. He excels in drawn-out fights.He can use blade mail to kill witch doctor during death ward channeling .

pairs.name: Puck
pairs.reason: Nearly impossible to hit with Paralyzing Cask or Maledict due to Phase Shift and high mobility. Puck can silence and burst you easily.

pairs.name: Wraith King
pairs.reason: Wraith King can survive trough Lich's damage with Reincarnation. He further provide this protection to his team with Aghanim's Scepter and can soak up Chain Frost bounces with his many Bone Guard skeletons.

pairs.name: Oracle
pairs.reason: Shadow Demon can dispel Frost Shield with Fortune's End and save an ally from Chain frost with his False Promise or Fate's Edict.

pairs.name: Shadow Demon
pairs.reason: Shadow Demon can dispel Frost Shield with Demonic Purge and save an ally from Chain frost with his Disruption. Even if an ally is caught out Disseminate can be used to return much of Lich's damage back to his team.

pairs.name: Ringmaster
pairs.reason: Ringmaster can save an ally with Escape Act from Lich's vast amounts of Magical damage or by interrupting Sinister Gaze.

pairs.name: Centaur Warrunner
pairs.reason: Stampede is amazing at disengaging Centaur's entire team from Chain Frost as it negates all the many slows that Lich's toolkit utilizes to keep his enemies close.

pairs.name: Outworld Devourer
pairs.reason: OD can save an ally with Astral Imprisonment from Lich's vast amounts of Magical damage or by interrupting Sinister Gaze.

pairs.name: Axe
pairs.reason: The taunt from Axe's Berseker's Call makes Riki attack him by force and not remain invisible through Cloak and Dagger, or use Blink Strike and Tricks of the Trade to do more damage or get away. Axe can also proc Counter Helix through the Smoke Screen silence once it reaches enough attack counters. Axe's high HP pool and tanky item purchases also makes it extremely difficult for Riki to ever burst him down, even after he gets Diffusal Blade.

pairs.name: Bounty Hunter
pairs.reason: Bounty Hunter's Track reveals Riki through his Cloak and Dagger invisibility, which is his main asset of roaming and setting up kills. Until he purchases a Manta Style or gets to level 25 for the Dispel talent on Tricks of the Trade, Riki has no way to take off Track and finds it extremely difficult to play around it. Bounty Hunter's high armor also makes him relatively tanky against Riki's physical damage.

pairs.name: Bristleback
pairs.reason: Bristleback takes reduced damage when getting hit from the back because of his passive Bristleback ability. This massively counters Riki as his Blink Strike lands him behind Bristleback for right clicks, and his Tricks of the Trade also strikes enemy units from behind in its AoE. Bristleback also releases Quill Spray or Viscous Nasal Goo from the Bristleback damage threshold, depending on the facet he selected, which reflects damage back to Riki or deters him from fighting because of the armor reduction.

pairs.name: Centaur Warrunner
pairs.reason: Centaur Warrunner's high HP gain and tanky item purchases make it extremely difficult for Riki to ever burst him down, even after he gets Diffusal Blade. Centaur's Retaliate still reflects damage inside the Smoke Screen silence to do damage back to Riki, unless he is hidden with Tricks of the Trade. If Centaur isn't the Smoke Screen target, he can use Stampede to get his teammate out of the AoE of Riki's spells and save them as Diffusal Blade does not slow movement speed during Centaur's ultimate.

pairs.name: Chaos Knight
pairs.reason: Chaos Knight and his Phantasm illusions can divide the damage of Riki's Trick of the Trade and tank it together because of their high HP pool. Once a squishy Riki comes out of Tricks of the Trade, Chaos Knight and his illusions easily burst him down during the Chaos Bolt stun and Reality Rift pull. The Chaos Strike procs on right clicks from Chaos Knight still provide lifesteal and heal him up inside the Smoke Screen silence.

pairs.name: Dragon Knight
pairs.reason: Dragon Knight's Dragon Blood innate provides him massive armor and HP regen with levels to go with his naturally high HP pool to tank Riki's physical damage. This makes it extremely difficult for Riki to ever burst him down, even after he gets Diffusal Blade. Dragon Knight is also not bothered too much by the Smoke Screen silence, as long as he is in Elder Dragon Form, and can simply stand his ground to fight against a squishy Riki.

pairs.name: Legion Commander
pairs.reason: Legion Commander's Duel forces Riki to attack him and not remain invisible through his Cloak and Dagger. Riki also right clicks Legion Commander from the front during Duel, which massively reduces his damage output and gives Legion Commander the upper hand in the fight to get easy Duel wins and accumulate damage throughout the game. Legion Commander's Moment of Courage also procs on right clicks inside the Smoke Screen silence.

pairs.name: Meepo
pairs.reason: Meepo's Earthbind root latches onto Riki even when he is invisible through Cloak and Dagger, revealing him and making him unable to cast Blink Strike and Tricks of the Trade. Meepo and his clones can chain Root a squishy Riki in this way and burst him down easily with Poof and right clicks. Meepo and his clone can also tank Tricks of the Trade together to not get bursted down by Riki inside the Smoke Screen AoE.

pairs.name: Nyx Assassin
pairs.reason: Nyx Assassin's Nyxth Sense innate reveals Riki through his Cloak and Dagger invisibility when the two heroes are close to each other. This puts Riki at a major disadvantage when Nyx Assassin scouts him while he is invisible himself through Vendetta. As such, Nyx Assassin can surprise and kill a squishy Riki with his Vendetta hit and follow up spell combo. A well timed Spiked Carapace can also stun Riki if he uses Blink Strike on Nyx Assassin, which doesn't let him follow up with Smoke Screen and Tricks of the Trade.

pairs.name: Slardar
pairs.reason: Slardar's Corrosive Haze reveals Riki through his Cloak and Dagger invisibility, which is his main asset of roaming and setting up kills. Until he purchases a Manta Style or gets to level 25 for the Dispel talent on Tricks of the Trade, Riki has no way to take off Corrosive Haze and finds it extremely difficult to play around it. Slardar's high HP pool also makes him relatively tanky against Riki's physical damage, and he can still proc Bash of the Deep inside the Smoke Screen silence.

pairs.name: Spectre
pairs.reason: Spectre's Spectral Dagger can hit Riki through his Cloak and Dagger invisibility, which reveals him but doesn't make him targetable. This makes it extremely difficult for Riki to hide or run away, and gives an easy opportunity to Spectre's team to Dust and kill him. Spectre can also proc Desolate on right clicks inside the Smoke Screen silence, while her Dispersion returns a lot of Riki's damage back to him to threaten his life, unless he is hidden during Tricks of the Trade.

pairs.name: Underlord
pairs.reason: Atrophy Aura reduces BASE attack damage and Riki loves stacking Agility as it scales with Backstab. Pit of Malice reveals invisible units making it a potent counter to his core mechanic Cloak and Dagger. Pit of Malice and Firestorm can be placed on top of Tricks of the Trade to instantly root and damage Riki as he exits it, also preventing him from using Blink Strike. Agility stacking means high armor making Firestorm quite effective against Riki's high armor but low HP pool.

pairs.name: Viper
pairs.reason: Viper's attack speed slow through Nethertoxin and Corrosive Skin, which isn't silenced inside Smoke Screen, makes it difficult for Riki to dish out his physical damage after he Blink Strikes on top of him. This makes Riki rely on Tricks of the Trade for damage, which is not enough on its own to finish off a tanky Viper. Viper's Viper Strike also breaks and reveals a squishy Riki through his Cloak and Dagger invisibility, which makes him susceptible to dying to Poison Attack stacks.

pairs.name: Zeus
pairs.reason: Zeus' Lightning Bolt provides true sight in a small area, and can latch onto an invisible Riki if he is close enough to the spot where Lightning Bolt was originally casted to do massive damage to him. This puts pressure on Riki to Blink Strike and silence Zeus inside Smoke Screen, which can possibly be avoided if Zeus jumps away quickly with Heavenly Jump before getting silenced. Once Zeus gets Aghanim's Scepter, his Nimbus becomes a global tool to reveal Riki alongside Thundergod's Wrath.

pairs.name: Alchemist
pairs.reason: The massive HP regen from Chemical Rage provides solid protection from being bursted during a Black Hole. Enigma's many Eidolons trigger Greevil's Greed and often become the focus of Alch for some massive easy gold. Malefice get's dispelled by both Chemical Rage and Berserk Potion.

pairs.name: Bristleback
pairs.reason: Bristleback can mitigate significant damage during Black Hole and Midnight Pulse and even kill off Enigma with Quill Spray procs before a full Black Hole channel is completed. Eidolons have relatively low armor and mostly provide extra Gold and XP for Bristleback.

pairs.name: Spectre
pairs.reason: Spectre's Dispersion makes her one of the better heroes to survie a Black Hole as Dispersion reduces ANY damage source incluing BH's Pure damage. Shadow Step and Haunt allow Spectre to focus Enigma and prevent him from executing a clean Black Hole.

pairs.name: Silencer
pairs.reason: Global Silence can interrupt Black Hole from anywhere on the map, forcing Enigma to either catch Silencer in it or not use it altogether until he is dead or Global Silence is on cooldown. Even if Enigma is under the effects of BKB or any other form of debuff immunity Global Silence would still interrupt BLack Hole's channel.

pairs.name: Rubick
pairs.reason: Spell Steal arms Rubick and his team with an empowered Black Hole. Arcane Supremacy amplifies the cast range and damage of Malefice, Midnight Pulse and Black Hole. Telekinesis can instantly interrupt Black Hole or be used to break Linken's along with Fade Bolt to steal it.

pairs.name: Warlock
pairs.reason: Chaotic Offering has a huge AOE and cast range that can reliably interrupt Black Hole, even during BKB or any other form of debuff immunity. Clipping Enigma with any of Warlock's basic spells -Fatal Bonds, Shadow Word, Upheaval before he gets to use Black Hole can disrupt his Blink initiation. His basic abilities are also effective at clearing Eidolons.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Anti Mage has an easy time jumping on a squishy and immobile Tinker with Blink and burn his mana with his Mana Break right clicks, which lets him follow up with Mana Void to burst him down because of his high mana pool. Anti Mage can also block and reflect Laser with Counterspell to avoid getting blinded. Defense Matrix also does Tinker little help against Anti Mage's right clicks into Mana Void burst. The Mana Void mini stun also stops the Rearm and Keen Conveyance channel.

pairs.name: Batrider
pairs.reason: Batrider has an easy time running down a squishy and immobile Tinker during Firefly while he is slowed by Sticky Napalm in the laning stage. Defense Matrix and the Laser blind does Tinker little help getting run down in this manner. Later in the game, Batrider's Blink Dagger into Flaming Lasso lets him drag Tinker to his team and burst him down without letting him teleport away with Keen Conveyance. Flamebreak also lets Batrider push Tinker closer to him and find him in tree lines.

pairs.name: Clockwerk
pairs.reason: Clockwerk's Rocket Flare gives him vision to find Tinker hiding in tree lines, which lets him follow up with his long range Hookshot to lock down Tinker and interrupt his Rearm and Keen Conveyance teleport. Battery Assault also prevents Tinker from Rearming or teleporting, while Defense Matrix does little against the mini stun inside Power Cogs. Clockwerk can also kick one of his Power Cogs from range to stop Tinker's channeling spells.

pairs.name: Doom
pairs.reason: Doom's ultimate Doom disables a squishy and immobile Tinker from using spells, which makes him completely useless as he relies heavily on his spells to get in and out of fights as well as do damage and survive. Doom can easily run down Tinker in the duration of his ultimate with the movement speed boost during Scorched Earth. The Infernal Blade mini stun also stops Tinker's channeling spells.

pairs.name: Earth Spirit
pairs.reason: Earth Spirit's Rolling Boulder lets him get on top of a squishy and immobile Tinker from range to follow up with the damage and control from the rest of his spells to burst him down. Earth Spirit is also invulnerable during his Roll, letting him avoid the March of the Machines damage. The Geomagnetic Grip silence also interrupts Tinker's channeling spells, including his Keen Conveyance teleport.

pairs.name: Invoker
pairs.reason: Tinker relies on staying in the back or hide in tree lines where enemy heroes cannot get to him during teamfights or while farming. But Invoker has an easy time finding Tinker with Tornado to dispel Defense Matrix and land his spell combo on the squishy hero. Invoker can also easily interrupt Tinker's Teleport and Rearm channel to ensure he cannot get away.

pairs.name: Kunkka
pairs.reason: Kunkka's X Marks the Spot into follow up spell combo from long range is a massive problem for Tinker throughout the game as he cannot Rearm or teleport away with Keen Conveyance when targeted by the spell. Even if Tinker's teleport completes, he comes right back to the X Mark. Torrent also provides vision in its AoE to find Tinker in tree lines.

pairs.name: Legion Commander
pairs.reason: Legion Commander's Blink Dagger into Duel lets her find a squishy Tinker in tree lines while he pushes out lanes alone with March of the Machines after his Keen Conveyance teleport. This makes for easy Duel wins for Legion Commander and snowball in the game with the accumulated damage. Press the Attack also dispels the blind from Laser.

pairs.name: Night Stalker
pairs.reason: Night Stalker's flying vision and movement during Dark Ascension lets him find a squishy and immobile Tinker in tree lines while he pushes out lanes alone with March of the Machines after his Keen Conveyance teleport. Once on top of Tinker, The Crippling Fear silence prevents him from using any spells, including teleporting away with Keen Conveyance, making for an easy kill for Night Stalker. The Void mini stun during night time also interrupts Tinker's channeling spells.

pairs.name: Nyx Assassin
pairs.reason: Nyx Assassin has an easy time finding a squishy Tinker in tree lines during his Vendetta invisibility while he pushes out lanes alone with March of the Machines after his Keen Conveyance teleport. This gives Nyx Assassin easy kills with the Vendetta hit followed by his spells combo. Nyx Assassin can also use Spiked Carapace during the Vendetta invisibility to use the AoE damage from March of the Machines to stun Tinker and stop his channeling spells.

pairs.name: Pangolier
pairs.reason: Pangolier has an easy time closing the gap on a squishy and immobile Tinker during Rolling Thunder and burst him down by chain stunning him to prevent him from Rearming or teleporting away with Keen Conveyance. Pangolier cares little about the Laser blind when doing damage with Swashbuckle, while the magic resistance while rolling prevents most of the damage from March of the Machines.

pairs.name: Pudge
pairs.reason: Pudge gets easy hooks on a stationary Tinker while he channels Rearm and Keen Conveyance in fights to bring him close and burst him down with a follow up Dismember and run down during Rot. The status resistance from Defense Matrix does little help against the slow from Rot. Pudge can also practically absorb all the damage from March of the Machines with his Meat Shield active.

pairs.name: Pugna
pairs.reason: Pugna's Nether Ward does massive damage to Tinker when he uses any spell in its AoE because of their high mana cost. Since Tinker uses his volley of spells multiple times in fights with Rearm, the Ward massively counters him and threatens his life if he continues to cast spells in its AoE. Pugna also cares little about the Laser blind, while his Life Drain channel keeps him healthy while standing in March of the Machines as Tinker has no stun or silence to stop it.

pairs.name: Silencer
pairs.reason: The silence from Silencer's Global Silence and Last Word are massive issues for Tinker throughout the game as he relies on his spells to get in and out of fights as well as do damage and survive. Arcane Curse also damages and slows Tinker for a lengthy duration if he keeps casting his volley of spells multiple times with Rearm when affected by the spell.

pairs.name: Skywrath Mage
pairs.reason: Skywrath Mage's long range instant silence with Ancient Seal renders Tinker completely useless in fights as he relies on his spells to get in and out of fights as well as do damage and survive. This lets Skywrath Mage follow up with his burst damage from spells to kill a squishy and immobile Tinker while he cannot do anything. Skywrath Mage can also target Tinker with his Mystic Flare burst even without Rod of Atos as he stands in place to channel his Rearm and Keen Conveyance teleport.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: Slark's high movement speed through his innate and the mobility through Pounce lets him find and get on top of a squishy Tinker while he pushes out lanes alone with March of the Machines after his Keen Conveyance teleport. This lets Slark get easy kills and build up Essence Shift stacks as he can dispel the Laser blind with Dark Pact, while keeping himself healthy inside March of the Machines with the HP regeneration during Shadow Dance. The Pounce leash also prevents Tinker from teleporting away with Keen Conveyance.

pairs.name: Spirit Breaker
pairs.reason: Spirit Breaker sets up easy kills on a squishy Tinker throughout the game with his Charge of Darkness as Tinker has no way of stopping its collision. This is particularly useful in the laning stage for Spirit Breaker to keep ganking Tinker and killing him over and over to slow down his game, while snowballing himself with the gold and experience. Charge of Darkness also follows Tinker where ever he Teleports with Keen Conveyance to get on top of him, and can always be stopped manually to avoid going into Tinker's base.

pairs.name: Storm Spirit
pairs.reason: Storm Spirit has a decent time in lane against Tinker as he can get last hits with Static Remnant despite the blind from Laser. Once Storm Spirit gets to level 6 and has Ball Lightning, he can easily close the gap on Tinker and burst him down during the Electric Vortex lockdown. Storm Spirit is also invulnerable during his Ball Lightning jump, which prevents all the damage from March of the Machines. The Electric Vortex pull also interrupts Tinker's channeling spells.

pairs.name: Zeus
pairs.reason: Zeus has a decent time in lane against Tinker as he can get last hits with Arc Lightning and Lightning Bolt despite the blind from Laser. Later in the game, Zeus' global Thundergod's Wrath finds and damages Tinker while he stays in tree lines or hides behind his team, letting Zeus follow up with the rest of his spells to close the gap and burst him down. Once Zeus gets Aghanim's Scepter, Nimbus becomes another global tool to damage Tinker and stop his channeling spells along with Lightning Bolt.

pairs.name: Storm Spirit
pairs.reason: While Storm may struggle against Sniper early on, he can dominate in the mid to late game using Ball Lightning and Electric Vortex to quickly close the gap and burst Sniper down.

pairs.name: Centaur Warrunner
pairs.reason: Centaur Warrunner is naturally tanky, and with Blade Mail and his passive Retaliate, he can reflect a lot of Sniper’s damage. As a frequent Blink Dagger buyer, he can close the distance easily and punish Sniper. His ultimate, Stampede, helps his team initiate or escape, making him an effective counter to Sniper.

pairs.name: Morphling
pairs.reason: Morphling can turn into Sniper and outdamage him with higher attack speed and agility when fully morphed. He can also chase and finish Sniper off using Waveform, making it hard for Sniper to escape or trade effectively.

pairs.name: Pudge
pairs.reason: Pudge can easily hook and solo kill Sniper in the early game due to Sniper’s low mobility. In the late game, Pudge can displace Sniper by hooking him out of position, making him a strong counter throughout the match.

pairs.name: Spectre
pairs.reason: Spectre can use Reality to jump directly onto Sniper, bypassing his range advantage. In the mid to late game, Spectre's tankiness and sustained damage make it easy for her to kill Sniper before he can escape or fight back.

pairs.name: Phantom Assassin
pairs.reason: Phantom Assassin can easily close the gap on Sniper and burst him down with high crit damage at any stage of the game. Sniper’s low mobility and fragility make him an easy target for PA’s quick pickoffs.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: Slark can easily kill Sniper by using Pounce to lock him down and Shadow Dance to stay elusive during the fight. Sniper’s lack of mobility makes him a prime target for Slark’s aggressive pickoffs.

pairs.name: Mars
pairs.reason: Mars is a natural Blink Dagger buyer, allowing him to quickly initiate on Sniper. With Arena of Blood and Spear of Mars, he can trap and pin Sniper, making him an easy kill due to his low mobility and defenses.

pairs.name: Earth Spirit
pairs.reason: Earth Spirit’s spells let him roll in quickly and silence or stun Sniper, making it easy to burst him down. His mobility and crowd control allow him to pick off Sniper during fights before he can react.

pairs.name: Primal Beast
pairs.reason: Primal Beast can use Trample to start, followed by Onslaught to close the gap, and then finish with Pulverize (ultimate) to disable and burst down Sniper. This combo makes it easy for Primal Beast to catch and kill Sniper despite his range advantage.

pairs.name: Lycan
pairs.reason: With his ultimate Shapeshift, Lycan gains increased movement speed and attack damage, allowing him to quickly close the gap and pick off Sniper before he can react.

pairs.name: Ancient Apparition
pairs.reason: Ice Blast prevents Necro from healing trough Sadist and Death Pulse, while having Ghost Shroud amplify it's damage as it reduces Magic Resistance. Necro has no innate mobility spells and is quite slow and stationery, making it difficult for him to disengage easily and wait out the duration of Ice Blast in safety.

pairs.name: Arc Warden
pairs.reason: Necro is strong and sturdy but slow and stationary making Spark Wraith and Flux amazing tools at wearing him down and keeping him at bay. Tempest Double allows Arc to continue fighting and splitpushing even if Reaper's Scythe manages to kill the main Arc, diminishing it's effectiveness. Shiva's Guard as well as Necro's level 20 talent reduces Barracuda's HP regen.

pairs.name: Shadow Demon
pairs.reason: Disruption is just a nightmare for Necro - any Illusions that it creates inherit Hearthstopper Aura as well as other auras like Radiance or Shiva, which Necro naturally builds into, as well as Sadist and Profane Potency to help them stay alive. Disruption can be used as a save from Reaper's Scythe as it has a fairly long connection time. Demonic Purge dispels Ghost Shroud and hinders Necro's already low mobility even further.

pairs.name: Doom
pairs.reason: Necro's main mechanic is healing trough Death Pulse, Death Seeker (Aghanim's Shard Upgrade) and Sadist stacks, which Doom completely prevents. Doom can Devour several creeps and use them against Necro - some of the more notable ones are: Satyr Banisher to Purge Ghost Shroud; Centaur Courser for Cloak Aura, which is a Magic Resistance AURA (basically Pipe but twice as better); Vhoul Assassin for Envenomed Weapon to almost entirely reduce Sadist's and general HP regen.

pairs.name: Oracle
pairs.reason: Oracle has not 1 but 2 saves from Reaper's Scythe - Fate's Edict, which provides 100% Magic Resistance and False Promise. Having 2 saves is already bad enough for Necro, but Fate's Edict specifically is a low cooldown basic ability with a relatively large cast range and low cast point. Fortune's End can dispel Ghost Shroud, while rendering Necro rooted and Purifying Flames can do some significant damage during Ghost Shroud.

pairs.name: Medusa
pairs.reason: Medusa's unique ability to use her Mana pool as her HP makes her a nightmare for Necro. Hearthstopper Aura does very little to her as she tends to build Mana items instead of HP and there's rarely a good opportunity to cast Reaper's Scythe on her because if she's already out of mana and half HP she's pretty much dead already.

pairs.name: Tidehunter
pairs.reason: Tide shrugs off Fatal Bonds and Upheaval with Kraken Shell. He wins teamfights with Ravage before Warlock can impact the fight, and Golems can’t pierce his tankiness. He scales better in 5v5s.

pairs.name: Bounty Hunter
pairs.reason: Bounty thrives on hunting supports like Warlock, who lacks escape or armor. Track ensures Warlock gets deleted first in fights, and his constant harassment keeps Warlock from safely warding or channeling.

pairs.name: Elder Titan
pairs.reason: ET negates Warlock’s sustain by reducing magic resistance. His spirit combo and Echo Stomp can zone Warlock and stop his channeled abilities. Bonds are useless if Warlock dies before casting.

pairs.name: Morphling
pairs.reason: Morphling's mobility and sustain shrug off Bonds and Upheaval. He quickly kills Warlock in the backline and survives Mystic Flare-level bursts. Warlock has no way to lock Morphling down.

pairs.name: Bristleback
pairs.reason: Bristle thrives in long fights and shrugs off Warlock's harassment. Fatal Bonds doesn't deter him, and Golems do little unless the whole team commits. He’s too tanky for Warlock to influence meaningfully.

pairs.name: Underlord
pairs.reason: Underlord punishes grouped-up heroes, and Warlock’s entire spell kit relies on clustering. Pit of Malice and Firestorm zone Warlock out of teamfights, while Dark Rift can nullify Offering follow-up.

pairs.name: Shadow Fiend
pairs.reason: Shadow Fiend’s AoE and quick right-click damage punish Warlock’s slow casting and low armor. He can burst Warlock before Offering lands. If SF gets BKB, Warlock becomes helpless during engagements.

pairs.name: Sand King
pairs.reason: Sand King can blink-stun Warlock before he casts. His Epicenter + Caustic combo melts supports grouped under Fatal Bonds. Warlock also struggles to position safely against invis or blink initiation.

pairs.name: Keeper of the Light
pairs.reason: Keeper’s blinding light and high mobility make it hard for Warlock to land Upheaval. He can interrupt channeling with Will-o-Wisp and push lanes faster than Warlock can defend.

pairs.name: Phoenix
pairs.reason: Phoenix’s Fire Spirits reduce right-click effectiveness of Golems. Supernova zones Warlock out and punishes his low attack speed. Warlock can’t cancel Supernova unless massively ahead.

pairs.name: Medusa
pairs.reason: Mana Shield allows Medusa to survive Beastmaster's Primal Roar and to counter initiate with Stone Gaze. Split Shot, Mystic Snake and Gorgon's Grasp all affect multiple targets and are naturally effective at clearing Call of the Wild Boar and Call of the Wild Hawk summons. Primal Road triggers Cold Blooded making Medusa even more survivable.

pairs.name: Dawnbreaker
pairs.reason: Both Starbreaker and Celestial hammer are both effective at clearing Call of the Wild Boar and Call of the Wild Hawk summons due to their AOE property. More importantly Solar Guardian provides a global save, and counter initiation for Primal Roared ally anywhere on the map.

pairs.name: Sand King
pairs.reason: Sand King's kit is entirely AOE making it easy for him to clear Call of the Wild Boar and Call of the Wild Hawk. More importantly, Caustic Finale turns Beastmaster's summons against him as even a single Stinger can affect multiple summons that upon death nuke Beastmaster for massive damage.

pairs.name: Ember Spirit
pairs.reason: Ember's kit is entirely AOE making it easy for him to clear Call of the Wild Boar and Call of the Wild Hawk. The multiple summons allow Ember to stay invulnerable for longer during Sleight of Fist. Flameguard provides him protection from Beastmaster's heavy Magic Damage and he can dodge a lot of damage from Wild Axes and Drums of Slom with Sleight of Fist and Fire Remnant.

pairs.name: Bristleback
pairs.reason: Bristleback's heavy AOE kit makes it easy for him to clear Call of the Wild Boar and Call of the Wild Hawk with Quill Spray and Hairball. Beastmaster can take a lot of towers early and Bristleback can simply park his body infront of a tower and turn his Bristleback towards a pushing Beastmaster to delay or stop the push altogether.

pairs.name: Elder Titan
pairs.reason: Elder Titan’s Spirit clears the zoo with bonus damage, and Echo Stomp controls the entire army. His aura reduces armor and magic resistance, punishing Beastmaster’s summons and frontline presence heavily.

pairs.name: Gyrocopter
pairs.reason: Gyro punishes summons with Flak Cannon and Call Down. He clears pushes fast and scales better in teamfights. Beastmaster can’t burst Gyro easily, and the longer the fight goes, the worse it becomes for Beastmaster.

pairs.name: Kunkka
pairs.reason: Kunkka’s Torrent and Boat stall pushes and disrupt the zoo. Cleave from Tidebringer eliminates summons quickly. Kunkka also scales into a tanky frontliner that shrugs off Primal Roar and zone control.

pairs.name: Tidehunter
pairs.reason: Anchor Smash massively reduces damage from Beastmaster’s units. Kraken Shell removes Primal Roar, making it nearly useless. Beastmaster cannot push through Ravage and the teamfight dominance Tide brings.

pairs.name: Lina
pairs.reason: Lina’s Dragon Slave and Light Strike Array instantly clear summons. Laguna Blade bursts Beastmaster if he overcommits. Her range and spell damage make it very hard for him to establish a siege safely.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Anti Mage's Blink together with Mana Break on right clicks lets him get on top of Queen of Pain and burn her mana. This makes Queen of Pain Blink defensively every time if she doesn't want to get bursted by Mana Void because of her high mana pool. Anti Mage can also easily block and reflect Shadow Strike with Counterspell, leaving only Scream of Pain and Sonic Wave as her real damage sources. Anti Mage's magic resistance through Counterspell also reduce a lot of Queen of Pain's spell damage.

pairs.name: Bloodseeker
pairs.reason: Bloodseeker's Rupture keeps Queen of Pain in place and prevents her from using Blink to get away if she wants to avoid taking a ton of damage. This lets Bloodseeker follow up with the Blood Rite silence and damage on a squishy and immobile Queen of Pain and burst her down with his right clicks.

pairs.name: Centaur Warrunner
pairs.reason: Centaur Warrunner's Return Retaliate returns a ton of Queen of Pain's burst damage back to her, threatening her life if she uses her spell combo on a tanky Centaur. Once Centaur gets Blade Mail, this reflection damage is even greater and practically prevents Queen of Pain from ever targeting him with her burst damage without the fear of dying herself. Stampede also enables Centaur's entire to close the gap on a squishy Queen of Pain.

pairs.name: Disruptor
pairs.reason: Disruptor's Glimpse completely counters Queen of Pain's mobility through Blink, as long as he has vision of her after she has Blinked in or out of fights. Disruptor can gain vision with Thunder Strike beforehand, and prevents Queen of Pain from Blinking in its duration. The Static Storm silence inside Kinetic Field also lets Disruptor control a squishy Queen of Pain and set up a kill on her.

pairs.name: Doom
pairs.reason: Doom's ultimate Doom silences Queen of Pain and completely shuts down her mobility through Blink. This lets Doom run down a squishy Queen of Pain during Scorched Earth every time when his ultimate is off cooldown. Doom's high HP pool also keeps him relatively safe from dying to Queen of Pain's high damage spells.

pairs.name: Earth Spirit
pairs.reason: Earth Spirit's Rolling Boulder lets him get on top of a squishy Queen of Pain and stun her at the same time to follow up with his control and damage through the rest of his spells to set up kills on her. The low cooldown on Rolling Boulder also matches the cooldown of Blink to match Queen of Pain's mobility. Earth Spirit's high HP pool also keeps him relatively safe from dying to Queen of Pain's high damage spells.

pairs.name: Faceless Void
pairs.reason: Faceless Void's Time Walk can completely reverse the damage taken from Queen of Pain's burst damage spell combo while closing the gap or getting away from her. Chronosphere also lets Faceless Void lock down a squishy Queen of Pain and burst her down with his right clicks. Time Dilation also massively counters Queen of Pain's low cooldown spells, and doesn't let her use them multiple times in fights. Blink's cooldown hurts Queen of Pain in particular as she cannot get out of fights if she Blinks in.

pairs.name: Grimstroke
pairs.reason: Grimstroke's silence through Phantom's Embrace is a massive problem for Queen of Pain as she has to stand and right click it down every time to use her damage and mobility spells. This sets up a follow up Ink Swell stun to not let Queen of Pain Blink away and set up a kill on her. Soulbind is also prevents Queen of Pain from Blinking if she gets leashed to one of her allies.

pairs.name: Kunkka
pairs.reason: Kunkka's Tidebringer lets him match Queen of Pain's Shadow Strike harass in lane to keep up with her and not get zoned out. Later in the game, Kunkka's X Marks the Spot into Ghostship and Torrent combo makes short work of a squishy Queen of Pain as her Blink is only wasted if she casts it before getting pulled back by Kunkka. Kunkka's high HP pool also keeps him relatively safe from dying to Queen of Pain's burst damage, and the Blade Mail purchase reflects a lot of her damage back to her to threaten her life.

pairs.name: Legion Commander
pairs.reason: Legion Commander's Duel initiation after a Blink Dagger purchase lets her get on top of a squishy Queen of Pain and get easy Duel wins to accumulate damage throughout the game. This makes Queen of Pain play around her team and significantly reduces her farming speed and solo pickoff threat. Press the Attack also lets Legion Commander dispel Shadow Strike.

pairs.name: Lina
pairs.reason: Lina's burst damage nukes and high attack range gives her a favorable matchup in lane against Queen of Pain. Lina has an easy time stunning Queen of Pain with Light Strike Array and right clicking her when she walks up to use Shadow Strike. Past the laning stage, Lina's burst damage with her spells makes short work of Queen of Pain when she Blinks into fights.

pairs.name: Meepo
pairs.reason: Meepo's Earthbind roots Queen of Pain in place and prevents her from getting away through Blink to avoid the chain control from the rest of Meepo's clones. This lets Meepo follow up with Poof and right clicks from his clones to burst down a squishy Queen of Pain. The matchup gets even more difficult for Queen of Pain once Meepo gets Blink Dagger and Scythe of Vyse.

pairs.name: Night Stalker
pairs.reason: Night Stalker's flying movement and massive vision during Dark Ascension lets him find and get on top of a squishy Queen of Pain and burst her down inside the Crippling Fear silence to prevent her from Blinking away. The matchup gets even more difficult for Queen of Pain once Night Stalker gets Blink Dagger. Night Stalker's high HP pool also keeps him relatively safe from dying to Queen of Pain's high damage spells.

pairs.name: Nyx Assassin
pairs.reason: Nyx Assassin's Vendetta invisibility lets him find a squishy Queen of Pain and burst her down with the damage and control from his spell combo throughout the game. Nyx Assassin Spiked Carapace also works well against Queen of Pain's AoE damage spells to reflect her damage and control her. The matchup gets even more difficult for Queen of Pain once Nyx Assassin gets Dagon and more levels in Mind Flare as well as Vendetta.

pairs.name: Puck
pairs.reason: Puck's Phase Shift lets her dodge Queen of Pain's Shadow Strike and Scream of Pain in lane to prevent her from gaining the upper hand with her poke damage. Later in the game, Puck's Dream Coil leashes Queen of Pain in a small area and prevents her from Blinking away until she breaks the link to stun herself and take damage. Puck's follow up control and damage through Illusory Orb and Waning Rift easily lets her burst down a squishy Queen of Pain.

pairs.name: Riki
pairs.reason: Riki's Blink Strike into Smoke Screen lets him get on top of a squishy Queen of Pain and silence her to prevent her from Blinking Away and burst her down with his right clicks and Tricks of the Trade. The matchup gets even worse for Queen of Pain once Riki becomes invisible through Cloak and Dagger and purchases a Diffusal Blade, which lets him easily keep Queen of Pain inside the Smoke Screen AoE to burst her down.

pairs.name: Rubick
pairs.reason: Queen of Pain has four active spells, which can all get stolen by Rubick with his Spell Steal. Stealing Blink from Queen of Pain gives Rubick massive mobility alongside his Blink Dagger purchase, while stealing Sonic Wave or Scream of Pain gives him a massive AoE damage nuke to dish out even more damage than her with his Arcane Supremacy buff.

pairs.name: Silencer
pairs.reason: Silencer's Global Silence and Last Word can silence a squishy Queen of Pain and prevent her from Blinking away, setting up easy kills on her. Arcane Curse also hinders Queen of Pain from spamming her low cooldown spells as it does more damage and slow with more spells she uses while affected by Silencer's spell. The double silence on Global Silence from Silencer's Reverberating Silence also makes it difficult for Queen of Pain to dispel it with a Black King Bar or Eul's Scepter.

pairs.name: Skywrath Mage
pairs.reason: Skywrath Mage's Ancient Seal silence prevents a squishy Queen of Pain from Blinking away and sets up easy kills on her with the burst damage from the rest of his spells. Queen of Pain is also susceptible to dying after Blinking close to Skywrath Mage as he can swiftly turn the fight on her with the burst damage from his spell combo. The magic damage barrier from the Shield of the Scion facet also helps absorbs a lot of the Scream of Pain and Shadow Strike damage.

pairs.name: Void Spirit
pairs.reason: Void Spirit's Dissimilate lets him dodge Queen of Pain's Shadow Strike and Scream of Pain in lane to prevent her from gaining the upper hand with her poke damage. The damage barrier from the Sanctuary facet for Resonant Pulse also helps absorb a lot of Queen of Pain's spell damage. Later in the game, Void Spirit's mobility through Astral Step lets him get on top of a squishy Queen of Pain and follow up with his damage and control spells to burst her down easily.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: Venomancer struggles against Phantom Lancer due to his illusions overwhelming Plague Wards. His poison damage is spread thin across duplicates. PL can dispel slows with Doppelganger and easily avoid Gale. Venomancer can’t stop PL from farming or taking over long fights.

pairs.name: Arc Warden
pairs.reason: Arc Warden outranges Venomancer and uses his clone to kill Plague Wards safely. His magnetic field allows allies to ignore poison chip damage. Venomancer cannot approach Arc Warden without being punished by spark wraiths and flux. He loses map control and poke wars.

pairs.name: Brewmaster
pairs.reason: Brewmaster dispels all of Venomancer’s damage-over-time effects with Primal Split. During the split, he removes Plague Wards and disables Venomancer’s positioning. Gale and Nova become useless once dispelled. Brewmaster’s utility and tankiness outlasts Venomancer’s slow burn.

pairs.name: Storm Spirit
pairs.reason: Storm Spirit zips in and out of fights, ignoring all of Venomancer’s slow-based control. He can burst Venomancer before poison becomes a threat. Venomancer lacks disables to lock Storm down. Once behind, he can’t recover against Storm’s map pressure.

pairs.name: Tinker
pairs.reason: Tinker has the range and burst to kill Venomancer without getting close. Venomancer’s slow poison damage is too slow to pressure Tinker’s farming pace. Tinker’s mobility keeps him out of reach.

pairs.name: Shadow Demon
pairs.reason: Shadow Demon can purge Poison Sting and Gale from his allies, nullifying Venomancer’s control. His illusions from Disruption can tank wards and push waves. Venomancer’s chip damage is ineffective when SD can save allies at critical moments. He completely removes Venomancer’s influence in key fights.

pairs.name: Naga Siren
pairs.reason: Naga Siren overwhelms Venomancer with illusions that absorb his poison damage. Her Song of the Siren resets fights and renders Poison Nova useless. Venomancer’s chip damage can’t handle her high armor and magic resistance. He becomes a liability once she gets farm.

pairs.name: Sniper
pairs.reason: Sniper outranges Venomancer and kills Plague Wards from a distance. He is rarely in range to be hit by Gale or Nova. Venomancer struggles to close the gap without getting punished. In fights, Sniper stays safe while Venomancer slowly melts.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Anti-Mage dispels Gale and slows with Manta Style and ignores wards with Blink. Venomancer’s lack of disables makes it impossible to stop AM from farming. His low mobility is punished hard by Mana Void. Anti-Mage scales out of control while Venomancer stalls.

pairs.name: Morphling
pairs.reason: Morphling easily shrugs off poison with his attribute shifting and high sustain. Venomancer can’t burst him before Morph’s regen takes over. Morphling also clears Plague Wards with waveforms. His mobility and late-game strength make Venomancer fall off hard.

pairs.name: Night Stalker
pairs.reason: Crippling Fear can silence Faceless Void for a long time, preventing him from using his Time Walk and Chronosphere.

pairs.name: Abaddon
pairs.reason: Mist Coil and Aphotic Shield enable Abaddon to keep an ally alive during Chronosphere. Borrowed Time prevents Faceless Void from killing Abaddon during his Chronosphere.

pairs.name: Kunkka
pairs.reason: Ghostship can stun Faceless Void and give damage reduction to allies that are trapped during Chronosphere. Torrent can stun Faceless Void from outside Chronosphere. X Marks the Spot can bring back Faceless Void if he escapes using Time Walk.

pairs.name: Wraith King
pairs.reason: Void often wastes Chrono on WK’s first life. Reincarnation punishes Void’s long cooldown commitment and forces defensive repositioning.

pairs.name: Enigma
pairs.reason: Black Hole pierces BKB and can catch Void before or after Chrono. Enigma also punishes grouped-up fights,

pairs.name: Medusa
pairs.reason: Medusa’s tankiness and Stone Gaze punish Void for standing still during Chrono. She can outlast his burst and counter-initiate easily.

pairs.name: Silencer
pairs.reason: Global Silence interrupts Time Walk, Chrono, and BKB timings. Faceless Void needs precise fights, which Silencer disrupts.

pairs.name: Winter Wyvern
pairs.reason: Cold Embrace saves Chrono targets. Winter’s ultimate also punishes grouped teammates, especially after Void drops a bad Chronosphere.

pairs.name: Enchantress
pairs.reason: Strong laner that bullies Void early with ranged harass. Her untouchable reduces Void’s right-click effectiveness, and she’s hard to burst down alone.

pairs.name: Lifestealer
pairs.reason: Rage makes Lifestealer immune to magic damage during Chrono’s duration. If he Infests a creep or hero, Void has to waste time in chrono to reach lifestealer.

pairs.name: Disruptor
pairs.reason: Glimpse and Static Storm are direct counters. Disruptor can trap Void post-Time Walk and silence him before Chrono, denying initiation.

pairs.name: Necrophos
pairs.reason: Necro’s Heartstopper Aura and Reaper’s Scythe punish low-HP Void. In extended fights, Void becomes an easy target without BKB or help.

pairs.name: Underlord
pairs.reason: Atrophy Aura reduces WK's attack damage, which is almost all of his total damage output. Underlord can control him multiple times with Pit of Malice, as he lacks innate dispel. Fiend's Gate allows him to bring in the numbers on WK if he ever gets caught out anywhere on the map in order to get trough his second life via Reincarnation.

pairs.name: Tidehunter
pairs.reason: Anchor Smash reduces WK's attack damage significantly, which is almost all of his total damage output. Blubber can dispel Wraithfire Blast after a single Mortal Strike as the game goes on. Gush reduces armor, which WK already struggles with and Dead in the Water is hard for WK to deal with due to his low base attack speed. Ravage can be timed as Reincarnation is about to revive WK to instantly disable him.

pairs.name: Phoenix
pairs.reason: WK's total damage output comes mostly from his attacks and Phoenix can make them both miss with Blinding Sun or reduce their frequency with Fire Spirits. Supernova can be hard for WK to deal with as he is a melee hero and also lacks good base attack speed or built in debuff immunity.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: WK's total damage output comes mostly from his attacks, which he cannot take advantage of during Slark's main defensive tools: Shadow Dance and Depth Shroud (Aghanim's Shard upgrade). Dark Pact can dispel Wraithfire Blast and Reincarnation's Wraith form still provides Slark with Essence Shift stacks.

pairs.name: Lifestealer
pairs.reason: Rage/Unfettered can be used to dodge/dispel Wraithfire Blast. Feast + Open Wounds outheal Vampiric Spirit and in a 1 on 1 fight, which WK is supposedly "king" of LS tends to win as he outdamages and outheals WK. Infest can disarm trough Debuff Immunity once upgraded with Aghanim's Scepter, removing most of WK's damage output for it's duration.

pairs.name: Windranger
pairs.reason: Windranger is a strong counter, as Windrun evades both your attacks and your skeletons’ damage. With Diffusal Blade combined with her ultimate, she can burn your mana and prevent Reincarnation.

pairs.name: Ancient Apparition
pairs.reason: Ice Blast prevents you from healing from Spirit Siphon and Exorcism which is the most reliant way of Death Prophet to survive during teamfights.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Your high mana pool and frequent mana usage will make you a prime target for Anti Mage with his Mana Void.

pairs.name: Doom
pairs.reason: Doom is going to stop you from casting spells which will make you useless during teamfights unless you have already casted Exorcism before that. You cannot heal during Doom.

pairs.name: Terrorblade
pairs.reason: ChatGPT said: Terrorblade can use Sunder to swap health with Death Prophet and finish her off in team fights. His illusions create high sustained damage, overwhelming her defenses. Metamorphosis increases his attack power, making it harder for Death Prophet to survive prolonged fights. If Terrorblade controls the tempo, he can burst her before she uses Exorcism effectively

pairs.name: Lycan
pairs.reason: Lycan can easily bait Exorcism and disengage or engage using his ultimate, Shapeshift, allowing him to chase down and finish Death Prophet quickly, exploiting her cooldowns and limited mobility during fights.

pairs.name: Elder Titan
pairs.reason: Elder Titan can Echo Stomp to lock down Death Prophet, allowing his team to set up kills or interrupt her while chasing. Natural Order strips her armor and magic resistance, making her much easier to kill.
Shadow Demon can use Demonic Purge to slow Death Prophet’s movement and disrupt her with Disruption if she’s chasing allies, making him both a strong counter and a valuable save.

pairs.name: Undying
pairs.reason: Undying can use Tombstone to spawn zombies on Death Prophet, while his ultimate Flesh Golem boosts his tankiness and damage. His healing and strength-stealing abilities let him sustain and fight effectively against Death Prophet.

pairs.name: Bristleback
pairs.reason: Bristleback can sustain against Death Prophet’s aggression. If Death Prophet tries to commit, Bristleback can spam Quill Spray and use Viscous Nasal Goo to wear her down, then turn the fight in his favor.

pairs.name: Venomancer
pairs.reason: Venomancer can slow Death Prophet using his Venomous Gale, Poison Sting, and Plague Ward attacks, limiting her impact by reducing her movement speed and making it harder for her to fight effectively.

pairs.name: Axe
pairs.reason: Phantom Strike's extra attack speed will cause Phantom Assassin to trigger Counter Helix more often, which can be fatal for Phantom Assassin in the early game. Jumping on Axe with Phantom Strike is not a good idea for Phantom Assassin at all as it makes her a seriously easy target for a counter-initiation with Berserker's Call and Blade Mail. Most of Axe's abilities pierce Black King Bar, allowing him to lock down Phantom Assassin at any time. Berserker's Call greatly reduces Phantom Assassin's ability to crit hard against Axe, and may cause her to kill herself when used with Blade Mail. Berserker's Call can also affect Phantom Assassin even if she has Black King Bar active as Berserker's Call can fully pierce spell immunity, making Berserker's Call one of the best abilities in the game against heroes like Phantom Assassin who wants to kill opponents quickly without being interrupted. Culling Blade can often kill Phantom Assassin before she can do anything due to her low health and strength gain. And every time Culling Blade successfully kills Phantom Assassin or any of her teammates, Axe gains permanent armor from it, which in combination with armour items that Axe often purchases like Blade Mail, Crimson Guard, Assault Cuirass and Shiva's Guard can make Phantom Assassin's attacks only tickle Axe.

pairs.name: Troll Warlord
pairs.reason: Whirling Axes (Melee) makes it hard for Phantom Assassin to land a Coup de Grace. Troll Warlord often buys Silver Edge and Monkey King Bar, the items that greatly help against Phantom Assassin's Blur ability. Battle Trance completely negates Phantom Assassin's large damage output, preventing Troll Warlord from dying easily. The lifesteal also allows Troll Warlord to restore much of his health.

pairs.name: Windranger
pairs.reason: Phantom Assassin's Blur is useless against Windranger as she commonly buys items that require Javelin like Maelstrom, Monkey King Bar or Bloodthorn, and other than Stifling Dagger, Phantom Assassin has nothing else that can bypass Windrun. Additionally, Phantom Assassin doesn't like building Monkey King Bar because her crits are reliant on attack damage. Focus Fire can still deal considerable damage despite Blur's evasion due to the increased attack speed.

pairs.name: Pangolier
pairs.reason: Phantom Assassin struggles against Pangolier because his Rolling Thunder constantly disarms her, making it impossible for her to deal right-click damage. He is tanky, mobile, and can kite her easily in fights. Pangolier's Diffusal Blade also burns her mana, stopping her from escaping with Phantom Strike.

pairs.name: Pudge
pairs.reason: Pudge counters Phantom Assassin by tanking through her burst and locking her down with Dismember, which goes through Black King Bar. He can easily build Blade Mail or Ghost Scepter, punishing her in direct fights.

pairs.name: Bristleback
pairs.reason: Phantom Assassin's single-target burst is ineffective against Bristleback's Quill Spray and Goo spam. His back damage reduction and consistent AoE pressure overwhelm her in prolonged engagements. Bristleback simply doesn't die to critical strikes alone. Phantom Assassin's Break Fan of knives is now her aghanim's which is flat 4200 gold Phantom Assassin need other items before she can buy aghanim so it delays her kill window the game while bristle can dominate.

pairs.name: Earth Spirit
pairs.reason: Earth Spirit disables Phantom Assassin with silences and slows, making it hard for her to stick to targets. He is tanky and mobile, and his early-game aggression delays her item timings. His Geomagnetic Grip silences her before she can burst him down.

pairs.name: Doom
pairs.reason: Phantom Assassin cannot function under Doom, as it disables all her active abilities and prevents escape or burst. Doom can also build Scythe of Vyse or Shiva's Guard, reducing her mobility and crit damage. She’s heavily reliant on spells to fight and flee, which Doom nullifies completely.

pairs.name: Queen of Pain
pairs.reason: Queen of Pain kites Phantom Assassin with her blink and magic damage. She deals significant burst before Phantom Assassin can get close. Her high mobility makes her difficult to target, and she farms faster in the early game.

pairs.name: Timbersaw
pairs.reason: Phantom Assassin’s physical burst has little effect on Timbersaw, who stacks reactive armor quickly and deals pure damage in return. She cannot burst him before he turns the fight. Timbersaw also clears waves faster and pressures lanes, limiting her farm.

pairs.name: Tiny
pairs.reason: Tiny’s burst damage deletes Phantom Assassin before she can react. His Avalanche-Toss combo is deadly during her squishy early-game phase. He also builds Silver Edge to disable her Blur, and his tree cleave punishes her in melee range.

pairs.name: Dawnbreaker
pairs.reason: Dawnbreaker’s Starbreaker disables Phantom Assassin and deals heavy physical damage. Solar Guardian allows her to join fights and heal allies, making it hard for Phantom Assassin to get solo pickoffs. Dawnbreaker is naturally tanky and doesn’t die to one crit.

pairs.name: Primal Beast
pairs.reason: Primal Beast punishes Pugna’s squishy nature with high physical burst. Pugna struggles to cast when caught by Onslaught and Trample. Nether Ward has little impact on Primal’s low mana use spells. Pugna can’t disengage or defend himself once locked down.

pairs.name: Chen
pairs.reason: Chen overwhelms Pugna’s push tempo with stronger creeps and global healing. Pugna’s spells are inefficient against Chen’s army. Divine Favor and Hand of God outheal Life Drain. Pugna’s early push is easily stalled by creeps and sustain.

pairs.name: Huskar
pairs.reason: Huskar jumps onto Pugna and punishes his low armor and HP. Life Break into Burning Spears bypasses Pugna’s healing attempts. Decrepify helps slightly, but Huskar’s magic resistance scales fast. Huskar snowballs through fights where Pugna is forced to play passively.

pairs.name: Marci
pairs.reason: Marci closes the gap quickly and disables Pugna before he can escape. Her burst punishes Pugna’s long cast times and low defense. Decrepify doesn’t stop physical damage if Marci builds nullifier. Pugna can’t keep up with Marci’s skirmish pace.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Anti-Mage with right clicks (Mana Break) can finishes him with Mana Void easily. Decrepify cannot stop Anti-Mage from blinking around fights. Pugna’s reliance on spellcasting becomes a liability. He can’t kite Anti-Mage effectively and is a prime target.

pairs.name: Pudge
pairs.reason: Pudge easily hooks Pugna out of position and punishes him before he can react. Decrepify delays death but doesn’t stop Pudge’s high HP tanking. Pugna’s low strength scaling makes him easy pickings for Pudge. Nether Ward rarely threatens Pudge’s simple combo.

pairs.name: Riki
pairs.reason: Riki silences Pugna and kills him quickly with backstab damage. Smoke Screen shuts down casting and ruins Pugna’s teamfight impact. He can’t position well against invisibility and blink strikes. Pugna has no natural way to deal with Riki’s stealth.

pairs.name: Nyx Assassin
pairs.reason: Nyx Assassin hard counters Pugna with Mana Burn and Carapace reflecting Nether Blast. Pugna constantly triggers Carapace and stuns himself. Nyx scouts and bursts Pugna in fog before he can respond. Pugna’s heavy spell reliance becomes a huge risk.

pairs.name: Shadow Fiend
pairs.reason: Shadow Fiend out-ranges and outbursts Pugna in lane and teamfights. Decrepify can help mitigate right-clicks but SF can go magic or physical. Pugna can’t survive the combo if caught with Requiem. Nether Ward has limited effect on SF’s burst timing.

pairs.name: Kez
pairs.reason: Kez disables Pugna with fast rotation and punishes his static laning. He breaks positioning and forces Pugna into panic Decrepify or retreat. His burst combo happens before Pugna can react. Kez nullifies squishy spellcasters with fast map pressure.

pairs.name: Huskar
pairs.reason: Huskar's burn damage from Burning Spear is incredibly strong against Templar Assassin as it completely cancels out her Refraction from the burning over time which results in making her very vulnerable to ganks and harassments, and in turn forcing her out of the lane. Huskar often buys Heaven's Halberd.

pairs.name: Viper
pairs.reason: The damage over time from Viper's Poison Attack and Viper Strike rapidly wear down Refraction charges, allowing Templar Assassin to be damaged. Additionally, Corrosive Skin causes her attacks to apply damage overtime on her as well.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: Phantom Lancer's illusions destroy Refraction charges very quickly. Diffusal Blade, his core item, drains Templar Assassin's small mana pool, rendering her unable to save herself with Meld.

pairs.name: Naga Siren
pairs.reason: Naga’s illusions burn through Refraction instantly, removing TA's key defense. Templar Assassin struggles to clear illusions efficiently and gets overwhelmed in prolonged fights. Song of the Siren can reset fights or catch TA before she gets a kill.

pairs.name: Batrider
pairs.reason: Sticky Napalm ruins her mobility and melts Refraction charges rapidly. Flaming Lasso completely removes her from fights, especially pre-BKB. Batrider also breaks Meld positioning and traps with Firefly vision.

pairs.name: Brewmaster
pairs.reason: Primal Split can dispel Refraction and control Templar Assassin with cyclone. Brew's tankiness and utility make it difficult for her to burst him down. He excels in chaotic fights that disrupt Templar Assassin’s flow and force her into unfavorable targets.

pairs.name: Terrorblade
pairs.reason: Templar Assassin cannot burst him through Sunder, and he outscales her in the late game. Terrorblade’s illusions shred Refraction and tank a lot of her damage. She struggles once he has Manta + Skadi, as she can’t isolate him easily.

pairs.name: Phoenix
pairs.reason: Supernova completely halts Templar Assassin's right-click potential if not destroyed in time. Phoenix's AoE burn removes Refraction quickly. Slow and disarm from Fire Spirits reduce her burst and chase potential.

pairs.name: Sand King
pairs.reason: Burrowstrike + Sandstorm combo instantly removes Refraction, making her vulnerable. Sand King has great waveclear and stops Templar Assassin’s mid-push momentum. Epicenter prevents her from blinking or diving squishy supports.

pairs.name: Troll Warlord
pairs.reason: Troll can perma-root Templar Assassin and ignore her burst once he has BKB. His attack speed also shreds through Refraction very quickly. In a manfight, she loses unless she kills him before he ults.

pairs.name: Treant Protector
pairs.reason: Living Armor mitigates Templar Assassin’s burst during ganks and slows tower pushes. Overgrowth roots her through BKB, ruining her backline dives. He delays the game, which is not favorable for her tempo playstyle.

pairs.name: Arc Warden
pairs.reason: Magnetic Field makes it hard for Templar Assassin to hit targets reliably. Double heroes (main + Tempest) confuse her targeting and bait Refraction cooldowns. Arc Warden can also kite and outscale her with his clone and ranged poke

pairs.name: Naga Siren
pairs.reason: Naga Siren’s illusions overwhelm Viper’s single-target damage style. He can’t clear illusions quickly, and they burn his mana. Song of the Siren resets fights where Viper tries to initiate. She scales harder into late game and dominates after laning.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: Phantom Lancer creates too many illusions for Viper to handle. Viper’s slows do little once PL gets Diffusal and Manta. He can’t clear illusions fast enough and gets overwhelmed. PL shrugs off poison damage with high sustain.

pairs.name: Terrorblade
pairs.reason: Terrorblade resists Viper's early pressure due to high armor and Conjure Image. He outscales Viper and punishes his lack of burst. Viper can’t stop Sunder and gets destroyed in later fights. TB's illusions also act as meat shields against Viper's output.

pairs.name: Arc Warden
pairs.reason: Arc Warden outranges Viper with Spark Wraith zoning and Tempest Double. He controls space safely while Viper struggles to close the gap. His clone soaks Viper's abilities and allows for free harassment. Arc Warden wins the map with split pressure.

pairs.name: Chaos Knight
pairs.reason: Chaos Knight overpowers Viper with illusions and high burst damage. Viper’s slow single-target spells don’t impact CK’s phantoms. He forces Viper to buy items like Mjollnir that delay timing. CK punishes Viper's immobility and paper armor.

pairs.name: Tinker
pairs.reason: Tinker spams lasers from fog where Viper can’t retaliate. He outscales Viper completely with high magic burst and mobility. Viper has no tools to stop rearming or teleportation. Once Blink is online, Tinker dominates the tempo.

pairs.name: Brewmaster
pairs.reason: Brewmaster splits before Viper can kill him and dispels poison effects. Viper’s DOTs are useless against the Primal Split. He offers no way to stop Brewmaster from controlling fights. Brew’s utility and scaling outmatch Viper’s direct style.

pairs.name: Lycan
pairs.reason: Lycan summons overwhelm Viper’s single-target approach. Viper can’t kite or burst Lycan before he closes the gap. His ultimate runs through slows and forces Viper out of fights. Lycan wins lane with sustain and summons if Viper can’t zone early.

pairs.name: Dark Seer
pairs.reason: Dark Seer surges through Viper’s slows and sets up big AoE fights. Viper’s single-target focus is weak into illusions and Vacuum combos. Ion Shell punishes Viper in lane and ruins his supports. In teamfights, Dark Seer forces Viper to play reactively.

pairs.name: Chen
pairs.reason: Chen's summons and heals overwhelm Viper’s damage-over-time style. He baits spells on creeps and sustains through fights. Viper struggles to lane if Chen rotates early. In the midgame, Viper’s poison is outclassed by Chen’s army and utility.

pairs.name: Dark Seer
pairs.reason: Wall of Replica and Normal Punch (Aghanim's Scepter Upgrade) can create multiple Illusions of Luna to do devastating amounts of damage to her own team as she tends to build heavy stat items to improve her own Manta Illusions' damage and durability. The Illusions DS creates inherit both Moon Glaives and Lunar Blessing. Surge is amazing at disengaging from Eclipse or closing the gap on Luna.

pairs.name: Juggernaut
pairs.reason: Both Blade Fury and Omnislash are direct counters to Eclipse, offering Juggernaut spell immunity and invulnerabilty. Therefore, Luna will need assistance in taking down Juggernaut as going solo will not be successful. Because of her low range, Luna cannot easily destroy Healing Ward.

pairs.name: Shadow Demon
pairs.reason: Demonic Purge takes off Luna's superior mobility, removing the need for chasing her and allowing your team to reposition in team fights or escape when at low HP. If Shadow Demon has Aghanim's Scepter it will also take away glaive bounces and extra damage from Luna's passive. And Luna's commonly items Manta Style and Black King Bar does not work dispell to Demonic Purge Luna's illusions created by Disruption are very valuable with their Moon Glaives. These will effectively counter her pushing attempts and are painfully effective in team fights. Disruption can be used to save an ally from Eclipse. For the same reasons, Shadow Demon makes a very powerful ally for Luna when they are in the same team.

pairs.name: Chen
pairs.reason: Chen's creeps soak up a large portion of Luna’s glaive bounces and Eclipse beams. His army and sustain delay Luna’s timing to take objectives. Chen out-pushes early and counters Luna’s 5-man group-up with map pressure.

pairs.name: Underlord
pairs.reason: Atrophy Aura reduces Luna’s right-click damage drastically, especially during midgame. Pit of Malice roots her in Eclipse or to forces her to use BKB . Underlord's tankiness and aura-based playstyle slow down Luna’s tempo.

pairs.name: Medusa
pairs.reason: Medusa’s Mana Shield absorbs most of Luna’s magical and physical burst. Medusa out-scales Luna in ultra-late-game and holds high ground much better. During fights medusa can turn with stone gaze.

pairs.name: Dark Willow
pairs.reason: Brambles and Cursed Crown interrupt Luna’s positioning and channeled fights. Shadow Realm and Bedlam allow Willow to out-trade and kite Luna in lane, Terrorize can be used to reset or setup on luna.

pairs.name: Bristleback
pairs.reason: Luna’s glaives hit Bristle from behind, charging up Quills. She can't kill him fast enough, and her magic damage is ineffective vs his tankiness. Bristle punishes close-range heroes like Luna with constant harass.

pairs.name: Bane
pairs.reason: Fiend’s Grip pierces BKB and completely disables Luna during fights. Nightmare saves his cores from Eclipse or Lucent Beam burst. Bane has the tools to lock Luna down and render her damage useless.

pairs.name: Wraith King
pairs.reason: Luna blows cooldowns on his first life, only for him to respawn and re-engage. She lacks burst to kill both Wraith King and his team unless farmed significantly. WK makes her glaives and Eclipse unreliable due to many skeletons.

pairs.name: Necrophos
pairs.reason: Heartstopper Aura and Reaper's Scythe go right through Dragon Knight's armor.

pairs.name: Ursa
pairs.reason: Fury Swipes can tear Dragon knight down as it stacks infinitely.

pairs.name: Outworld Devourer
pairs.reason: Arcane Orb's constant pure damage output is devastating to Dragon Knight. Dragon Knight's relatively low mana pool leads to heavy damage from Sanity's Eclipse, which also bypasses his armor.

pairs.name: Viper
pairs.reason: Dragon Knight struggles against Viper because Viper directly counters what makes DK strong—his tankiness and sustain. Viper’s Nethertoxin disables Dragon Blood, so DK loses his armor and HP regen, making him much easier to harass and kill in lane. Poison Attack stacks slow and damage over time, wearing down DK even under his tower. Viper’s range and lane dominance make it hard for DK to farm or trade effectively. Overall, Viper shuts down DK’s durability and lane presence, forcing him into a passive, underfarmed position early on.

pairs.name: Arc Warden
pairs.reason: Arc can kite him endlessly with ranged attacks and slows. DK relies on getting close to deal damage, especially in Elder Dragon Form, but Arc’s Magnetic Field makes it hard for DK to hit buildings or heroes. The double Spark Wraiths and constant poke from Tempest Double chip away at DK over time, even through his tankiness. Arc can also farm faster and outscale DK in the late game, where his damage output and split push become overwhelming.

pairs.name: Ringmaster
pairs.reason: Ringmaster counters Dragon Knight by dealing max HP damage with Impalement Arts, bypassing his armor and regen. Wheel of Wonder punishes DK’s melee nature by pulling him in and bursting him if he faces it. Escape Act makes it hard for DK to finish targets. Ringmaster’s control and damage completely disrupt DK’s frontline impact.

pairs.name: Batrider
pairs.reason: Batrider is good against Dragon Knight because Sticky Napalm stacks reduce DK’s turn rate and stack damage over time, which DK can't shrug off early. Firefly lets Batrider bypass DK’s armor by dealing pure damage over terrain. Flaming Lasso pulls DK out of position, disrupting his tanky frontline role. Batrider's constant harassment and mobility make it hard for DK to farm or fight back effectively.

pairs.name: Crystal Maiden
pairs.reason: Crystal Maiden is good against Dragon Knight because her mana regeneration aura helps allies spam spells to break through his tankiness. Her Frostbite roots DK in place, making it hard for him to close gaps or escape. Crystal Nova slows his already low mobility, and her ultimate deals high magic damage that ignores his armor. Early game, her control and burst can zone him out before he gets tanky.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: Slark is good against Dragon Knight because he builds up Essence Shift stacks during long fights, gradually weakening DK’s strength while boosting his own. DK’s low burst damage and slow attacks make it hard to punish Slark before he escapes. Slark can dispel Dragon Tail stun and Corrosive Breath with Dark Pact, avoiding control and damage. His mobility lets him kite DK, heal with Shadow Dance, and re-engage on his terms.

pairs.name: Witch Doctor
pairs.reason: Witch Doctor is good against Dragon Knight because his Maledict amplifies damage based on lost health, which works well against DK’s high HP pool. Paralyzing Cask can interrupt DK’s channeled actions and stall his initiation. Death Ward deals high physical damage over time, punishing DK even through his armor if he’s stunned. Witch Doctor's sustained damage and control make it hard for DK to frontline effectively in fights.

pairs.name: Timbersaw
pairs.reason: Whirling Death, Timber Chain, and Chakram deal pure or magic damage that ignores DK’s high armor. Whirling Death also reduces DK’s strength, lowering his HP and weakening his tankiness. Timbersaw thrives in extended fights, where DK’s low burst can't threaten him, while Timbersaw can shred DK over time. DK’s melee nature and reliance on physical durability make him an easy target for Timber

pairs.name: Lone Druid
