pairs.reason: Spirit Bear can tank Dragon Knight’s attacks and harass him safely from a distance. The bear’s ranged attacks and mobility make it hard for DK to trade effectively. Lone Druid’s high physical damage can quickly bring down Dragon Knight’s towers and structures, bypassing DK’s frontline presence. Additionally, Lone Druid can split push and force DK to respond, limiting his impact in team fights.

pairs.name: Axe
pairs.reason: Axe's Culling Blade can kill a hero protected by Dazzle's Shallow Grave if the target's HP is below the Culling Blade threshold. Shallow Grave prevents a hero from dying by damage, but Culling Blade is an instant kill that bypasses death prevention effects like Grave. As long as the target's HP is low enough, Axe will execute them even under Grave.

pairs.name: Ancient Apparition
pairs.reason: Ice Blast prevents all healing, disabling Shallow Grave's sustain and Shadow Wave’s healing. The debuff lingers, making it dangerous for low-HP targets even after retreating. If a hero under Shallow Grave drops below the Ice Blast kill threshold, they will die as soon as Grave ends.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: He can dispel Shadow Poison with Doppelganger. His illusions burn Dazzle’s mana quickly with defusal blade making him unable to cast spells or use Shallow Grave. Phantom Lancer can kite Dazzle and pressure him constantly rendering him useless in fights without mana.

pairs.name: Slardar
pairs.reason: He can jump on Dazzle in teamfights and chain-stun him with Slithereen Crush and Bash of the Deep. Due to Dazzle’s squishy nature he is an easy pickoff. Taking him out first ensures he can’t use Shallow Grave or save his team during fights.

pairs.name: Weaver
pairs.reason: He can kite Poison Touch during laning and in teamfights .Dazzle relies on Poison Touch to harass and without it he struggles. Weaver’s mobility and damage make it easy to pick off Dazzle who has low HP and armor. Even as a support Weaver can outscale Dazzle with levels from Hive Mind and have more mid-game impact.

pairs.name: Sand King
pairs.reason: He can burst Dazzle or his allies quickly with his magic damage, making it hard for Dazzle to react or cast Shallow Grave in time.Dazzle’s heal is ineffective against Sand King’s high burst damage.During chaotic teamfights, it’s difficult for Dazzle to position properly and save teammates.

pairs.name: Tidehunter
pairs.reason: His high durability makes him hard for Dazzle to harass or zone out in lane. Kraken Shell dispels Poison Touch reducing Dazzle’s laning impact. Ravage can instantly disable Dazzle in teamfights preventing him from using Shallow Grave or healing. Tide’s strong teamfight presence outclasses Dazzle’s support capabilities.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: He can dispel Poison Touch and Weave using Dark Pact. Slark’s mobility allows him to kite and fight Dazzle and his allies easily. He can gain Essence Shift stacks from targets affected by Shallow Grave, giving him more agility during fights. Dazzle’s spells are less effective against Slark’s sustain.

pairs.name: Abaddon
pairs.reason: He can dispel Poison Touch or Weave using Aphotic Shield. He also outheals and out-sustains Dazzle in fights. As a frontline healer and dispeller, Abaddon provides more utility and durability for his team. His Borrowed Time makes him hard to kill, reducing Dazzle’s impact.

pairs.name: Razor
pairs.reason: His high movement speed and ability to stay on top of enemies make it hard to escape. If a target affected by Static Link is under Shallow Grave, Razor can still drain maximum damage and quickly turn fights in his favor. Razor’s constant pressure reduces Dazzle’s effectiveness in teamfights.

pairs.name: Beastmaster
pairs.reason: Clockwerk’s Battery Assault targets a single enemy, allowing Beastmaster’s summoned boars and hawks to absorb the damage. Additionally, Beastmaster’s summons make it difficult for Clockwerk to land his Hookshot , as he might end up targeting the summons instead of Beastmaster himself.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: Phantom Lancer can easily escape Clockwerk’s Cogs using Doppelganger, and his illusions absorb Battery Assault damage. As a natural Diffusal Blade buyer, Phantom Lancer can quickly burn Clockwerk’s mana, rendering him ineffective.

pairs.name: Juggernaut
pairs.reason: Juggernaut can easily bypass Battery Assault and Power Cogs by using Blade Fury, allowing him to quickly turn the fight around on Clockwerk.

pairs.name: Terrorblade
pairs.reason: Terrorblade’s illusions can tank Battery Assault, and his high attack speed allows him to quickly destroy Power Cogs. Even if Clockwerk isolates Terrorblade, he can use Sunder to turn the fight and kill Clockwerk instead.

pairs.name: Visage
pairs.reason: Visage is naturally tanky, and his familiars help soak up Battery Assault damage. Both Visage and his familiars can quickly destroy Power Cogs with their attacks. Clockwerk can only initiate and lock down heroes, lacking burst damage, so Visage can easily turn fights around and punish Clockwerk.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Anti-Mage’s Blink and built-in magic resistance make him hard to lock down. Even if Clockwerk hooks him, Anti-Mage can use Manta Style and Blink to escape or turn the fight around against Clockwerk.

pairs.name: Queen of Pain
pairs.reason: Queen of Pain can easily escape Clockwerk’s spells using Blink and kite him effectively. She can slow Clockwerk’s movement speed with Shadow Strike and then finish him off quickly with Sonic Wave.

pairs.name: Ancient Apparition
pairs.reason: AA's ult - Ice Blast completely negates Leshrac's sustain in fights, crippling him significantly and forces him to flee the fight altogether or risk getting bursted. He can keep his distance in order to use his spell making it difficult for Leshrac to reach him.

pairs.name: Medusa
pairs.reason: Medusa's unique Mana Shield counts as a damage absorb, which does not proc any Lifesteal or Spelllifesteal effects. Leshrac naturally has a high mana pool trough his base stats and natural itemization, which Medusa can further abuse to sustain herself trough Mystic Snake.

pairs.name: Drow Ranger
pairs.reason: Drow Ranger's Aghanim's Scepter is one of the strongest healing reduction abilities in DOTA and greatly diminishes Leshrac's sustain. She has high attack range to keep her distance and a consistent slow to kite Leshrac, making it difficult for him to get on top of her.

pairs.name: Doom
pairs.reason: Doom's ult - Doom completely negates Leshrac's sustain in fights, crippling him significantly and forces him to flee the fight altogether or risk getting bursted. He's a natural Shiva builder and can Devour a Vhoul Assassin, which makes him greatly effective even outside of Doom.

pairs.name: Lifestealer
pairs.reason: Lifestealer has multiple ways of mitigating or completely avoiding Leshrac's damage trough his Rage/Unfettered and Infest. His abudance of sustain trough Feast and Open Wounds can easily result in a situation where Leshrac runs out of Mana before LS runs out of HP.

pairs.name: Ember Spirit
pairs.reason: Ember's flexible itemization allows him to go for all 4 healing reduction items (Shiva, Skadi, Vessel, Orb of Corrosion) and a Mageslayer completely crippling Leshrac's sustain and damage output. His mobility is borderline ridiculous and makes it hard for Lesh to stay on top of him.

pairs.name: Undying
pairs.reason: Undying excels in long fights, where Leshrac normally thrives but Tombstone shifts that advantage. Decay reduces Leshrac’s effective HP pool, weakening his early presence. Leshrac struggles to kill Tombstone with right-clicks, and his team gets zoned out. In lane, Undying can easily out-sustain and harass Leshrac.

pairs.name: Queen of Pain
pairs.reason: QoP's high mobility lets her blink out of Pulse Nova and split Earth range. She can dodge Leshrac’s skill shots and harass him hard in lane with Shadow Strike. Leshrac has no silence or hard lockdown, making him an easy target post-laning.

pairs.name: Elder Titan
pairs.reason: Natural Order removes Leshrac’s base magic resistance and armor, making him paper-thin. Spirit + Stomp combo disables Leshrac. In teamfights, Leshrac often gets deleted by Echo Stomp + Earth Splitter before he can output damage. ET’s aura destroys Leshrac’s mid-game tankiness that he depends on.

pairs.name: Batrider
pairs.reason: Batrider has an easy time getting close to an immobile Nature's Prophet with Sticky Napalm stacks and Firefly, which also breaks the Sprout trees to maintain vision and keep on top of him. Nature's Prophet also struggles to Teleport away because of the long duration Flaming Lasso lockdown. Flamebreak also breaks Sprout trees when a unit that is pushed collides with a tree.

pairs.name: Broodmother
pairs.reason: Nature's Prophet can never trap or hold back Broodmother or her Spiderlings with Sprout while they are in the AoE of one of her Webs. Broodmother also has an easy time running at a squishy and immobile Nature's Prophet and burst him down before he can Teleport away. However, Broodmother has to be careful about the damage from Sprout and Wrath of Nature as it can kill most of her Spider army.

pairs.name: Dawnbreaker
pairs.reason: Dawnbreaker's Celestial Hammer gives her mobility to get on top of a squishy and immobile Nature's Prophet while breaking his Sprout trees to maintain vision of him. Dawnbreaker can also use one of her teammates to use Solar Guardian to get close to Nature's Prophet while saving her ally caught inside Sprout. Dawnbreaker's high damage through her spells and right clicks also helps deal with Treants throughout the game.

pairs.name: Doom
pairs.reason: Doom easily counters the Treants from Nature's Prophet with just a single level in Devour to get rid of them instantly. Level 1 Devour works on Level 4 Treants, and can instantly kill the strong Treant from the Ironwood Treant facet. Doom also has an easy time of running at a squishy and immobile Nature's Prophet during Scorched Earth and kill him every time Doom is off cooldown.

pairs.name: Earthshaker
pairs.reason: Earthshaker's spell combo makes short work of a squishy Nature's Prophet in every fight, as Echo Slam makes use of the Treant summons to do even more damage. Once Earthshaker gets Aghanim's Scepter, he also has a natural way of getting out of the Sprout trees every time with Enchant Totem.

pairs.name: Elder Titan
pairs.reason: Elder Titan's Astral Spirit makes use of the Treant summons from Nature's Prophet to give him even more damage and movement speed upon returning. This lets him run at Nature's Prophet as well as deal with his Treants with the mobility and damage. Elder Titan also has multiple long distance lockdown spells in Earth Splitter and Echo Stomp through Astral Spirit to stop the Teleportation of Nature's Prophet.

pairs.name: Ember Spirit
pairs.reason: Despite being a melee hero, Ember Spirit does most of his damage from a long distance with the Sleight of Fish and Searing Chains combo to maintain the upper hand on a squishy Nature's Prophet. The mobility from Fire Remnant also lets Ember Spirit break Sprout trees and get on top of a squishy Nature's Prophet to burst him down.

pairs.name: Faceless Void
pairs.reason: Faceless Void's Chronosphere lets him lock down and kill a squishy Nature's Prophet every time while he cannot fight back or defend himself. Nature's Prophet also struggles to get away from Faceless Void or hold him back with Sprout and Faceless Void can easily get outside or around the trees with Time Walk.

pairs.name: Invoker
pairs.reason: Invoker has multiple ways of stopping the Nature's Prophet Teleportation channel to ensure he does not get to join or get away from fights. Nature's Prophet also likes to play away from his team and split push lanes, which makes him an easy target for Invoker to find with Ghost Walk and finish off with his spell combo.

pairs.name: Kez
pairs.reason: Kez's high mobility lets him find easy kills on a squishy Nature's Prophet since he has no defensive tools to kite or get away from him. The Talon Toss silence also ensures Nature's Prophet cannot complete his Teleportation. Kez is also hard to deter with Sprout as he can chop down one of the trees with Grappling Claw to either escape or maintain the chase on Nature's Prophet.

pairs.name: Lina
pairs.reason: Lina's massive damage through her spell combo makes short work of a squishy Nature's Prophet to give her easy kills throughout the game. Light Strike Array also breaks trees, allowing Lina to get out of Sprout or find Nature's Prophet if he tries to hide himself and Teleport away. Lina's high damage through her spells and right clicks also helps deal with the strong Treant from the Ironwood Treant facet.

pairs.name: Meepo
pairs.reason: Meepo's high burst damage through right clicks and multiple Poofs from his clones gets him easy kills on a squishy Nature's Prophet throughout the game. Meepo also has plenty of Earthbind casts through his clones to stop the Teleportation of Nature's Prophet. Nature's Prophet also doesn't have a ton of damage or lockdown to burst down Meepo or control his clones when fighting back.

pairs.name: Monkey King
pairs.reason: Monkey King's mobility with Tree Dance and Primal Spring lets him find and jump a squishy Nature's Prophet, who struggles to get away with Sprout because of Tree Dance. The Boundless Strike stun also helps stop the Teleportation from Nature's Prophet and burst him down before he gets away. The armor gain from Wukong's Command also negates a lot of physical damage dished out by Nature's Prophet.

pairs.name: Muerta
pairs.reason: Muerta's Dead Shot lets her break a tree, which gives her an easy escape from Sprout while fearing Nature's Prophet with the ricochet targeted towards him. Muerta can also use Pierce the Veil to burst down Nature's Prophet while not letting him do any right click damage. The Calling silence also stops Nature's Prophet from Teleporting away.

pairs.name: Naga Siren
pairs.reason: Naga Siren has an easy time of running at a squishy and immobile Nature's Prophet to lock him down Ensnare and burst him down with her illusions. The Song of the Siren and Ensnare also prevent Nature's Prophet from Teleporting away. Naga Siren also counters the split push from Nature's Prophet and his Treants with her own split push through Mirror Image illusions, which lets her push multiple lanes at once.

pairs.name: Pangolier
pairs.reason: Pangolier's massive damage and lockdown with his spells makes short work of a squishy and immobile Nature's Prophet and gives him easy kills. Rolling Thunder breaks trees in its path, letting Pangolier get in and out of Sprout to maintain the chase on Nature's Prophet. The mobility from Swashbuckle and Shield Crash also help deal with Sprout and kill Nature's Prophet and his Treants at the same time.

pairs.name: Pudge
pairs.reason: Pudge gets easy Meat Hooks on a squishy and immobile Nature's Prophet when he hides himself inside Sprout, or tries to stand and throw right clicks. A follow up Dismember and the run down during Rot lets Pudge finish him off as he has no natural ability to get away from Pudge. Pudge can also Hook and instantly kill the stronger Treant summoned by Nature's Prophet with his Ironwood Treant facet, taking away a lot of his damage.

pairs.name: Queen of Pain
pairs.reason: Queen of Pain gets to whittle away the HP of Nature's Prophet with Shadow Strike in lane to maintain kill threat on him at all times. Later in the game, Queen of Pain's Blink lets her close the gap on a squishy Nature's Prophet and burst him down together with his strong Treant from the Ironwood Treant facet with her AoE burst damage through Sonic Wave and Scream of Pain. Blink also lets Queen of Pain easily get in and out of Sprout. The Dagon purchase also helps against both Nature's Prophet and his Treants.

pairs.name: Spectre
pairs.reason: Spectre has an easy time getting on top of a squishy and immobile Nature's Prophet with Shadow Step and running him down under the slow from Spectral Dagger. The phased movement on the Spectral Dagger path allows Spectre to move through Sprout trees to not allow Nature's Prophet to get away from her or slow her down.

pairs.name: Spirit Breaker
pairs.reason: Spirit Breaker counters the split push strategy of Nature's Prophet with his global Charge of Darkness to find and kill him every time he shows on the map to clear creep waves. The lockdown from Nether Strike and Greater Bash easily stops Nature's Prophet from Teleporting away. Charge of Darkness also allows Spirit Breaker to get away when trapped inside the Sprout trees.

pairs.name: Storm Spirit
pairs.reason: Storm Spirits mobility through Ball Lightning lets him get on top of a squishy and immobile Nature's Prophet and burst him down with his spells and right clicks during the Electric Vortex lockdown. Ball Lightning also breaks trees, which allows Storm Spirit to get in and out of Sprout to maintain the chase on Nature's Prophet. The catch from Ball Lightning also helps deal with the split push from Nature's Prophet and his Treants.

pairs.name: Timbersaw
pairs.reason: All of Timbersaw's active abilities cut trees, which makes the Nature's Prophet Sprout completely ineffective against him. Timbersaw can use the Sprout trees to deal even more damage with Whirling Death by cutting more trees in its AoE. Timbersaw's burst damage with his spells easily kills a squishy Nature's Prophet before he can get away with Teleportation.

pairs.name: Tinker
pairs.reason: Tinker counters the split push from Nature's Prophet and his Treants by getting to lanes with Keen Conveyance and killing creep waves safely with March of the Machines. Tinker's Defense Matrix also absorbs a lot of the damage dealt by Nature's Prophet with his right clicks and Wrath of Nature, effectively nullifying his burst potential. Nature's Prophet also has no way of stopping Rearm and the Keen Conveyance teleportation.

pairs.name: Underlord
pairs.reason: Underlord's Fiend's Gate deals with the split push from Nature's Prophet by getting on top of him every time he shows on the lane to clear creep waves. The root from Pit of Malice stops Nature's Prophet from getting away with Teleportation. Underlord also deals plenty of damage with Firestorm and his right clicks to deal with the strong Treant from the Ironwood Treant facet.

pairs.name: Visage
pairs.reason: Visage and his Familiars have an easy time running at a squishy and immobile Nature's Prophet during the slow from Grave Chill to kill him every time. The Familiars have flying movement, which lets them get in and out of Sprout to maintain vision of Nature's Prophet, and their Stone Form stuns him to stop him from Teleporting away. Nature's Prophet also has no good way of getting through the Gravekeeper's Cloak layers.

pairs.name: Batrider
pairs.reason: Flaming Lasso pierces Debuff Immunity capable of stunning an repositioning LS even during his Rage. Flamebreak can be used to kite LS and Firefly allows Batrider to move over impassable terrain like cliffs to prevent him from hitting you.

pairs.name: Bane
pairs.reason: Fiend's Grip pierces debuff immunity making it great at controlling LS during his Rage. Enfeeble greatly reduces his rightclick damage, which is his main source of damage and forces him to get even closer in order to use Infest or Open Wounds. Nightmare is effective at controlling or isolating him in a fight and Brain Sap can damage him during Rage.

pairs.name: Enigma
pairs.reason: Black Hole pierces Rage's Debuff Immunity and does not get mitigated by Unfettered's Status Resistance nor does it get dispelled as it is a channel, giving Enigma a reliable way of locking down LS. Midnight Pulse also pierces Rage's Debuff Immunity and does not get mitigated by Status Resistance. In lane Eidolons are amazing at securing last hits and more importantly denies due ot LS's low base attack damage.

pairs.name: Slardar
pairs.reason: Corrosive Haze and Bash of the Deep pierce Debuff Immunity and can be applied during Rage. Rage provides massive amounts of Magic Resistance and LS's main defensive tools, which don't work well versus Slardar's highly physical damage and Debuff Immunity piercing kit. LS struggles in lane versus Slardar, just like most melee heroes.

pairs.name: Bristleback
pairs.reason: Rage provides Magical Resistance and Debuff Immunity/Status Resistance, neither of which do well against Quill Spray and Bristleback Procs. In lane, LS struggles to make use of the excess mana that Quill Spray and Viscous Nasal Goo can provide and to control the wave due to Quill Spray doing AOE damage and naturally pushing the wave in.

pairs.name: Faceless Void
pairs.reason: Void can initiate with Chronosphere, locking Lifestealer down and rendering his Rage ineffective during its duration. This setup allows his team to follow up with disables. Additionally, his Time Lapse helps him mitigate damage and escape from Lifestealer's attacks.

pairs.name: Morphling
pairs.reason: Morphling is a strong counter to Lifestealer because he can replicate Lifestealer’s basic spells. This allows Morphling to use Lifestealer’s own abilities against him, turning his strengths into weaknesses. Additionally, Morphling’s high mobility and burst damage make it difficult for Lifestealer to trade effectively

pairs.name: Razor
pairs.reason: Razor’s Static Link is a hard counter to Lifestealer, as it goes through Rage and continuously steals his attack damage. Razor’s high movement speed allows him to chase Lifestealer, maintain the link, and often secure the kill

pairs.name: Bloodseeker
pairs.reason: Rupture makes it more difficult to get value out of Surge as the hasted movement speed now comes with a damage cost. Sanguiovore helps sustain Bloodseeker in lane against Ion Shell harass. Bloodseeker's Illusions do not inhherit Thirst, making him a weak Illusion hero that does not spawn a LVL 30 META TB with Wall of Replica or Normal Punch.

pairs.name: Oracle
pairs.reason: Fortune's End can dispel both Ion Shell and Surge, while providing valuable lockdown versus any Surged Targets. Fortune's End is particularly effective at shutting down Dark Seer's lane completely as it is one of the few level 1 dispels, that's AOE on top of that and Ion Shell is DS's main laning tool.

pairs.name: Ursa
pairs.reason: Most of Ursa's abilities are active appart from Fury Swipes, which is his main damage steroid that Wall of Replica and Normal Punch (Aghanim's Scepter Upgrade) Illusions do not inherit. Despite being a melee hero Ursa can focus down any Ion Shelled creeps in lane with Overpower and Fury Swipes to mitigate getting harassed and DS generally finds himself struggling greatly when facing Ursa in lane.

pairs.name: Windranger
pairs.reason: All of WR's abilities are active making her a poor target for Wall of Replica and Normal Punch (Aghanim's Scepter Upgrade) Illusions as they do not have any strong passives to inherit. WR can focus down any Ion Shelled creeps in lane and push out the wave with Power Shot to prevent getting harassed and DS generally finds himself struggling greatly when facing her in lane. Shackle Shot is amazing at locking down Surged opponents due to it's long duration.

pairs.name: Sven
pairs.reason: Sven's main damage steroids are Greater Cleave and God's Strength, which Wall of Replica and Normal Punch (Aghanim's Scepter Upgrade) Illusions do not inherit, otherwise Sven would build Manta every game. Despite being a melee hero Sven can naturally push out the wave with Greater Cleave to prevent getting overly harassed by Ion Shell and can lock down any Surged targets with Storm Hammer. Storm Hammer's Aghanim's Scepter Upgrade allows Sven to dispel both Ion Shell and Surge, negating half of DS's kit.

pairs.name: Faceless Void
pairs.reason: Faceless Void counters Dark Seer because Time Walk negates Ion Shell damage and restores his health during fights. Time Dilation increases the cooldown of Dark Seer's abilities, slowing him and reducing his impact. Additionally, Void’s Chronosphere can catch Dark Seer before he can use his utility spells.

pairs.name: Weaver
pairs.reason: Weaver can dodge Ion Shell damage with Shukuchi and freely reposition. His high mobility and harassment make laning difficult for Dark Seer. Time Lapse also allows Weaver to undo Dark Seer’s burst or disable attempts, making him hard to kill.

pairs.name: Sven
pairs.reason: Sven can easily kill creeps affected by Ion Shell with his cleave and burst damage. He can also quickly clear illusions created by Wall of Replica, making Dark Seer’s ultimate less effective in fights.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: Clinkz struggles against Phantom Lancer because PL buys Manta and Diffusal Blade, making it hard to identify the real one. This often leaves Clinkz out of mana, allowing Phantom Lancer to kill him easily.

pairs.name: Naga Siren
pairs.reason: Naga buys Manta and uses Ensnare to lock down Clinkz, making it difficult for him to catch the real Naga, leaving him vulnerable to being killed by naga or her allies.

pairs.name: Chaos Knight
pairs.reason: Chaos Knight buys Manta, allowing him to quickly turn and burst Clinkz if he tries to initiate, making it risky for Clinkz to engage.

pairs.name: Wraith King
pairs.reason: Wraith King doesn’t mind if Clinkz bursts through his first life because he can follow up with Wraithfire Blast, and Clinkz will be slowed by Reincarnation, making it hard for him to escape.

pairs.name: Meepo
pairs.reason: Meepo can net Clinkz even when he's invisible, revealing his position. Meepo can then chain more nets and burst Clinkz down quickly with Poof.

pairs.name: Morphling
pairs.reason: Morphling can morph into Strength to survive Clinkz’s burst if Clinkz tries to turn on him. Morphling’s high damage and mobility with Waveform let him either fight back effectively or escape Clinkz’s initiation.

pairs.name: Arc Warden
pairs.reason: Arc Warden can easily dodge Clinkz’s right-clicks using Magnetic Field. Essence Flux and Spark Wraith help Arc Warden deal damage and catch Clinkz if he tries to escape.

pairs.name: Lycan
pairs.reason: Lycan can chase down Clinkz easily thanks to his high movement speed during Shapeshift. With just a Dust or Gem, Lycan can reveal and kill Clinkz mid to late game.

pairs.name: Earth Spirit
pairs.reason: Earth Spirit’s Rolling Boulder and Silence effectively lock down Clinkz, preventing his escape. Additionally, Magnetize deals damage over time, making it even harder for Clinkz to get away alive.

pairs.name: Slardar
pairs.reason: Slardar’s Corrosive Haze reveals Clinkz and reduces his armor, making Clinkz much easier to kill. This makes Slardar an effective counter against Clinkz.

pairs.name: Shadow Demon
pairs.reason: Shadow Demon completely counters Guardian Angel by purging it with Demonic Purge. His Disruption removes targets before Omniknight can save them. He breaks Omniknight’s utility and saves.

pairs.name: Primal Beast
pairs.reason: Primal Beast punishes immobile supports like Omniknight with Onslaught and Trample. He can quickly close gaps and burst Omniknight before he casts spells. Omniknight’s abilities don’t prevent Primal’s magical damage or crowd control. He struggles to save allies from Pulverize.

pairs.name: Ancient Apparition
pairs.reason: Ancient Apparition counters Omniknight’s healing and sustain with Ice Blast. When Ice Blast is active, Purification and Guardian Angel become useless. AA’s long-range poke prevents Omniknight from positioning safely. He denies the core aspect of Omniknight’s defensive play.

pairs.name: Doom
pairs.reason: Doom silences Omniknight completely, disabling his healing and saving abilities. A Doomed Omniknight becomes useless in fights. Doom also breaks Guardian Angel .Omniknight has no way to deal with Doom’s direct suppression.

pairs.name: Medusa
pairs.reason: Medusa shrugs off Guardian Angel due to her Split Shot with Aghanim’s Scepter as she can target other enemies. Medusa’s tankiness also makes Omniknight’s healing less impactful. She outscales his team’s sustain in long fights

pairs.name: Enchantress
pairs.reason: Enchantress punishes Omniknight’s lack of burst damage and slows him with Untouchable. Her pure damage ignores Guardian Angel entirely. Omniknight’s sustain is too slow to outpace her Impetus attacks. He also cannot stop her from kiting his teammates.

pairs.name: Winter Wyvern
pairs.reason: Winter Wyvern’s Winter’s Curse turns Omniknight’s buffs against his team. Her Arctic Burn ignores his physical resistance. Wyvern also counters grouping strategies that Omniknight prefers. She can delay fights until Omniknight’s cooldowns are wasted.

pairs.name: Elder Titan
pairs.reason: Elder Titan removes Omniknight’s defensive value with Natural Order, reducing armor and magic resistance. Omniknight can’t protect allies from Earth Splitter’s burst. He also struggles to maintain formation under Astral Spirit harassment. Elder Titan breaks down Omniknight’s durability.

pairs.name: Witch Doctor
pairs.reason: Witch Doctor punishes extended fights with Death Ward, which Guardian Angel cannot fully negate. Maledict also amplifies burst damage over time. Omniknight’s healing is delayed and ineffective under this pressure. He lacks mobility to escape the Death Ward zone.

pairs.name: Outworld Devourer
pairs.reason: Outworld Destroyer can Astral Imprison Omniknight or his allies to delay or prevent Guardian Angel. Sanity’s Eclipse bursts Omniknight’s low-intelligence frame easily. His pure damage and scaling overpower Omniknight’s heals. Omniknight contributes little once Astral resets fights.

pairs.name: Marci
pairs.reason: Enchantress is bad against Marci because Marci can quickly close the gap and burst her down with high physical damage through unleash, ignoring Untouchable through Sidekick’s bonus damage and her rapid mobility. Enchantress struggles to kite Marci once she's on top of her.

pairs.name: Chen
pairs.reason: Against Chen, Enchantress can get outpaced in pushing and map control. Chen’s large creep army outscales Enchantress' Enchant, and his team-healing can nullify her chip damage from Impetus during mid to late-game pushes. Penitence also removes untouchable since it buff chen allies attack speed.Chen can also persuade enchantress creeps

pairs.name: Ursa
pairs.reason: Ursa counters Enchantress due to his Fury Swipes stacking damage, which bypasses Untouchable’s attack speed slow. Once Ursa gets on top of her, she can’t sustain through the damage, and her mobility isn’t enough to escape his chase potential.

pairs.name: Phantom Assassin
pairs.reason: Phantom Assassin is a major threat to Enchantress because she can instantly burst her down with high crit damage. Enchantress’ lack of hard disables or strong armor makes her vulnerable to PA’s quick kills, especially if PA has desolater.

pairs.name: Underlord
pairs.reason: Underlord is strong against Enchantress because his high AoE damage and sustain can deal with her creeps and chip damage. His Pit of Malice roots her in place, making it hard for her to kite, and his aura reduces her right-click damage significantly.

pairs.name: Pudge
pairs.reason: Pudge is a bad matchup for Enchantress because a single well-placed Hook can isolate and burst her. His Rot deals consistent magic damage that bypasses Untouchable, and once he grabs her with Dismember, she has little way to escape.

pairs.name: Crystal Maiden
pairs.reason: Crystal Maiden counters Enchantress in lane with high magic damage and disables. Enchantress can’t kite if she’s rooted by Frostbite, and her naturally low magic resistance makes her vulnerable to Crystal Maiden’s full spell combo, especially in early fights. Crystal Maiden can also kill enchantress creeps with frostbite

pairs.name: Morphling
pairs.reason: Morphling can survive Enchantress’ harass with Attribute Shift and can later outscale her with high burst damage. Enchantress lacks instant disable to prevent Morphling from switching to full agility or escaping, making it hard to finish him off.

pairs.name: Earth Spirit
pairs.reason: Earth Spirit is dangerous for Enchantress due to his silences and stuns, which interrupt her healing and movement. His burst damage combo comes fast, and if he catches her off guard, she can die before she gets a chance to kite or sustain.

pairs.name: Sand King
pairs.reason: Sand King is effective against Enchantress because of his magic burst through Caustic Finale and Epicenter. Enchantress’ healing isn’t fast enough to offset Sand King’s AoE damage, and her lack of mobility makes it easy for him to catch her with Burrowstrike.

pairs.name: Ancient Apparition
pairs.reason: Ice Blast is one of, if not the best spell against Huskar as he is the only hero in DOTA that does not have a Mana pool and utilizes HP to cast his spells and items. It prevents his Berserker's Bloodhealing and the lack of mobility in Huskar's kit makes it difficult for him to disengage easily and wait out the duration safely. Even if he just gets clipped by Ice Blast's debuff he usually dies to Armlet as he generally runs around at already low HP.

pairs.name: Necrophos
pairs.reason: Huskar loves playing on low HP to get maximum benefit from his Berserker's Blood, making him a perfect target for Reaper's Scythe. Ghost Shroud prevents Huskar from atacking Necro, and level 20 talent essentially negates Huskar's level 20 talent for extra HP regen.

pairs.name: Bloodseeker
pairs.reason: Huskar loves playing on low HP to get maximum benefit from his Berserker's Blood, making him constantly visible to Bloodseeker due to Thirst. This usually prevents him from sneaking a solo Rosh or to safely flash farm as fast as possible with as little HP as possible. Rupture does damage during Life Break.

pairs.name: Viper
pairs.reason: Viper can hold his own in lane versus Huskar as he outranges him and can trade back damage with Corrosive Skin. Viper can essentially end the lane upon reaching level 6 and acquiring Viper Strike as it prevents Huskar from utilizing Berserker's Blood. Viper can itemize for a quick Blink Dagger to always get the jump on Huskar.

pairs.name: Shadow Demon
pairs.reason: Shadow Demon can save his allies with Disruption in the early game, as well as disabling Huskar with it. More importantly, as the game goes on he can pick up and Aghanim's Scepter and Break Huskar for up to 10 seconds with Demonic Purge.

pairs.name: Doom
pairs.reason: Doom's Doom is one of the best spells against Huskar as he is the only hero in DOTA that does not have a Mana pool and utilizes HP to cast his spells and items. It prevents his Berserker's Blood healing and the lack of mobility in Huskar's kit makes it difficult for him to disengage easily and wait out the duration safely.

pairs.name: Phantom Assassin
pairs.reason: Huskar relies on sustained damage, but PA's Blur gives high evasion, making it hard for him to land hits. Her high burst damage from Coup de Grace can kill Huskar before he lifesteals back. Once PA gets BKB and Satanic, she becomes nearly impossible for Huskar to deal with. Halberd isn't enough to stop her physical burst.

pairs.name: Windranger
pairs.reason: Windranger kites Huskar effortlessly using Windrun to evade his attacks. Focus Fire melts through his low armor even when he has high HP from Berserker’s Blood. She builds Maelstrom or Gleipnir, which synergizes well against her mobility. Her Shackleshot can disable him long enough for allies to follow up.

pairs.name: Chaos Knight
pairs.reason: Chaos Knight's reality illusions overwhelm Huskar, who lacks good AoE to deal with them. CK's burst damage from Chaos Bolt and crits can kill Huskar before he can lifesteal or disarm. Armlet toggling becomes ineffective against the chaos of multiple illusions. CK scales better and thrives in mid-to-late game where Huskar falls off.

pairs.name: Troll Warlord
pairs.reason: Troll outlasts Huskar in fights thanks to Fervor attack speed stacking. Battle Trance saves Troll when Huskar brings him low, allowing him to lifesteal back and win duels. Troll builds Satanic and MKB, countering both disarm and evasion strategies. In late game, Troll becomes tankier and deals more DPS than Huskar can handle.

pairs.name: Naga Siren
pairs.reason: Nightstalker's lack of AOE damage makes it difficult for him to deal with Mirror Image Illusions - this allows Naga to manfight him and to keep the waves pushed, giving her and her team the upper hand. Both Ensnare and Song of the Siren can be used to lockdown or kite Nightstalker during Dark Ascension.

pairs.name: Arc Warden
pairs.reason: NS loves isolating a single target and Tempest Double allows Arc to have reliable backup to fight back. Flux and Spark Wraith slow, which greatly help with kiting NS while Magnetic Field provides evasion for Arc and his team. Arc Warden’s strong split-pushing forces Night Stalker to spread thin as he is slow at clearing waves, and Spark Wraith provides vision, diminishing Night Stalker’s ability to fly and hide over cliffs and terrain during Dark Ascension.

pairs.name: Bloodseeker
pairs.reason: Rupture limits NS's mobility from Hunter in the Night as he is forced to pay in blood to make use of his enhanced movement speed as well as flying over terrain during Dark Ascension. Thirst and Blood Rite can provide vision on NS as he tries to juke and hide over trees and cliffs in order to disengeage a fight when he gets low on health.

pairs.name: Chaos Knight
pairs.reason: Nightstalker's lack of AOE damage makes it impossible for him to deal with Phantasm Illusions in a straight up fight, considering they have built in sustain with Chaos Strike. Chaos Bolt has enough of a cast range to outrange Crippling Fear and Reality Rift can be used to pull NS away from his target of focus.

pairs.name: Wraith King
pairs.reason: WK doesn't really have any high impact active spells, considering he can have up to 3 passives, making him probably the worst hero in DOTA to be affected by Crippling Fear. Wraithfire Blast has enough of a cast range to outrange Crippling Fear and Vampiric Spirit supplies him with sufficient sustain to 1v1 NS. Boneguard can be a problem for NS as he lacks the AOE to clear the skeletons quickly, allowing WK to split push lanes, giving him and his team the upper hand.

pairs.name: Meepo
pairs.reason: Nightstalker's lack of AOE damage makes it impossible for him to deal with multiple Meepos in a straight up fight, considering they have built in sustain with Ransack. Earthbind has enough of a cast range to outrange Crippling Fear and can lock down NS multiple times while Poof allows Meepo to never have to face Night Stalker alone.

pairs.name: Alchemist
pairs.reason: Greevil's Greed makes Broodmother’s spiderlings far more valuable to Alchemist making it important that he does farm them as opposed to other heroes where the spider's bounties are negligible. Acid Spray will be potentially avoidable but it is still hard trying to kill him knowing he can use it. Alchemist naturally will be buying Radiance which will further be a problem for your spiderlings.

pairs.name: Axe
pairs.reason: Berserker's Call forces Broodmother and her spiderlings to attack, allowing for large amounts of pure damage to be done through Counter Helix.

pairs.name: Earthshaker
pairs.reason: Aftershock in combination with Enchant Totem prevents Broodmother from continuing to attack Earthshaker without being repeatedly stunned. Echo Slam is greatly amplified by Spiderlings, often instantly killing Broodmother, her swarm, and anyone else unfortunate enough to be nearby.

pairs.name: Naga Siren
pairs.reason: Naga Siren can easily clear Broodmother’s spiderlings using her illusions and Riptide, denying Brood map control and gold. She can use Song of the Siren to reset or set up fights, giving her team time to focus Broodmother or reposition. Her illusions also make it difficult for Brood to isolate the real Naga, especially in the mid to late game.

pairs.name: Dark Seer
pairs.reason: Dark Seer can use Ion Shell on one of Broodmother’s spiderlings to quickly clear out the rest, making it difficult for Brood to maintain her swarm. In chaotic teamfights, it's especially hard for Broodmother to micro her spiderlings away from Ion Shell damage. Vacuum helps control Broodmother’s movement and can group her with her spiders, amplifying AoE damage from allies.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: Phantom Lancer naturally counters Broodmother by overwhelming her with illusions, making it hard for her to focus the real PL. His illusions easily clean up spiderlings with Spirit Lance and basic attacks, denying Broodmother farm and map control. In extended fights, Broodmother struggles to isolate PL due to his constant repositioning and illusion spam.

pairs.name: Troll Warlord
pairs.reason: Troll Warlord can easily deal with Broodmother’s spiderlings using Whirling Axes (Melee) and his fast attack speed, clearing them quickly for extra gold and experience. In direct fights, Battle Trance allows Troll to survive Brood’s burst and turn the fight around with sustained damage. His strong laning presence and ability to take early objectives also limit Broodmother’s space to farm and push. Overall, Troll’s durability, AoE clearing, and 1v1 potential make him a strong counter to Broodmother.

pairs.name: Lina
pairs.reason: Lina can clear Broodmother’s spiderlings with ease using Dragon Slave and Light Strike Array, especially during the laning phase. Her long-range nukes keep Brood at bay, preventing her from snowballing or taking over the map. As the game progresses, Laguna Blade gives Lina the burst needed to finish off Broodmother before she can escape or heal.

pairs.name: Queen of Pain
pairs.reason: Queen of Pain excels against Broodmother with her high mobility and burst magic damage. She can easily clear spiderlings using Scream of Pain, denying Broodmother farm and slowing her momentum. With Blink, QoP avoids Brood’s slows and terrain control, making it hard for Broodmother to lock her down. Sonic Wave allows QoP to burst Brood quickly in fights, especially before she builds tanky items.

pairs.name: Crystal Maiden
pairs.reason: Broodmother has no stuns, making her vulnerable to Crystal Maiden’s disables like Frostbite, which can root her prevent escape. Crystal Maiden’s Crystal Nova slows Broodmother’s movement and attack speed, reducing her effectiveness in fights. Her Freezing Field ultimate deals heavy area damage, damaging both Broodmother and her spiderlings, which helps control Brood’s swarm during teamfights.

pairs.name: Abaddon
pairs.reason: Aphotic Shield is a low cooldown ability that can dispel Track and almost matches Tracks's cooldown, making it significantly more difficult for BH to play to his core strengths. Borrowed Time can be activated during Shadow Walk's stun to dispel it and can further dispel Track by itself.

pairs.name: Oracle
pairs.reason: Fortune's End is a low cooldown ability that can dispel Track and almost matches Tracks's cooldown, making it significantly more difficult for BH to play to his core strengths. Additionally, Fortune's End can reveal BH during Shadow Walk . Fate's Edict prevents BH from attacking, hindering his ability to apply Jinada. False Promise adds another layer of protection with a save and an extra dispel for any Tracked targets.

pairs.name: Legion Commander
pairs.reason: Press the Attack is a low cooldown ability that can dispel Track, crippling's BH vision advantage. Duel is effective at locking BH down and killing him as he has an above average BAT increasing the frequency of Moment of Courage procs.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: Dark Pact is a low cooldown ability that can dispel Track and almost matches Tracks's cooldown, giving Slark a reliable way of dealing with it. Pounce can leash BH during Shadow Walk, although without providing vision of him. Shadow Dance and Depth Shroud prevent Slark and any of his allies from being targeted by Shuriken Toss or it's bounces even while Tracked.

pairs.name: Tidehunter
pairs.reason: Blubber provides Tide with a constant dispel from both Track and Shadow Walk's stun as long as he is receiving enough incoming damage and has the HP to support it. Dead in the Water provides vision of BH during Shadow Walk and both Anchor Smash and Ravage can affect him during Shadow Walk.

pairs.name: Zeus
pairs.reason: Zeus can easily reveal Bounty Hunter using Lightning Bolt or Thundergod’s Wrath, exposing him even when invisible. His innate vision and burst damage make it hard for Bounty Hunter to roam or escape unseen. True sight from Zeus’s abilities is key to countering Bounty’s invisibility and disrupting his ganks.

pairs.name: Nyx Assassin
pairs.reason: Nyx Assassin can detect Bounty Hunter using Nyx Assassin’s innate ability Nyxth Sense , gaining an advantage in the vision game. Nyx’s high mobility and burst damage from Vendetta, Impale, and Dagon let him quickly kite and kill Bounty before he can react.

pairs.name: Faceless Void
pairs.reason: Chronosphere completely shuts Weaver down, catching him before he can Time Lapse. Void’s time-lock bashes are hard to dodge during fights. Weaver cannot fight into Void once BKB and items are up. His lack of hard disable makes Void scale freely.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: Weaver can’t handle Phantom Lancer’s illusions without AoE damage. He gets overwhelmed by Diffusal Blade and mana burn. Time Lapse often targets the wrong illusion, making survival unreliable. PL dominates long fights where Weaver loses control.

pairs.name: Morphling
pairs.reason: Morphling outscales Weaver and can morph into him for mobility. Weaver has no way to burst Morphling before he shifts to strength. Morphling’s sustain and magic burst punish Weaver's low HP. In late game, Morphling wins almost every duel.

pairs.name: Puck
pairs.reason: Puck’s silence and Dream Coil both counter Weaver’s escape tools. Weaver struggles to hit moving targets with Puck’s evasive playstyle. Puck also scales better into midgame utility. Coil forces Weaver into risky fights without his ult.

pairs.name: Rubick
pairs.reason: Rubick can steal Time Lapse or Shukuchi and turn them against Weaver. His lift disables Weaver long enough to kill him. Rubick builds survivability and utility faster. A good Rubick makes Weaver’s mobility a liability.

pairs.name: Visage
pairs.reason: Visage punishes Weaver’s low HP with burst from familiars. Soul Assumption stacks quickly from Weaver’s pokes. Gravekeeper's Cloak reduces poke damage significantly. Weaver also struggles to kill familiars without cleave or AoE.

pairs.name: Riki
pairs.reason: Riki silences Weaver with Smoke Screen, making Time Lapse unusable. His mobility is hard to track, and Diffusal Blade removes Weaver’s mana. Riki punishes poor positioning and weak detection. He wins lane with constant harass and slows.

pairs.name: Nyx Assassin
pairs.reason: Nyx lands Impale and Mana Burn reliably on Weaver. Carapace punishes Shukuchi usage. Nyx has built-in detection with Vendetta and nullifies Weaver’s split pushing. He can kill Weaver before he reacts.

pairs.name: Drow Ranger
pairs.reason: Drow slows Weaver with Frost Arrows, limiting his escape. Gust silences and prevents both Shukuchi and Time Lapse. She outdamages him once Dragon Lance is online. Weaver has difficulty closing the distance without Blink or BKB.

pairs.name: Dark Willow
pairs.reason: Dark Willow roots and stuns Weaver, forcing out Time Lapse early. Shadow Realm avoids his auto attacks. Cursed Crown and Brambles combo into disables. Her control denies Weaver free movement in chaotic fights.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Blink allows Anti-Mage to both, escape from Jakiro and to hunt down Jakiro, who has no way to escape without items. Counterspell protects Anti-Mage against Jakiro's mostly-magical damage. Both Mana Void and Mana Burn is very hazardous for Jakiro because of his high mana.

pairs.name: Clockwerk
pairs.reason: Battery Assault prevents Jakiro from casting spells as all his spells have very long cast times. Jakiro is also an easy target for Clockwerk's Hookshot + Power Cogs combo, as he has little mobility and no escape without items. Alternatively, if the enemy Clockwerk traps one of his own allies or Jakiro's allies in the cogs, it gives Jakiro an ideal setup to punish Clockwerk and his ally or to save Jakiro's ally.

pairs.name: Rubick
pairs.reason: Fade Bolt can hinder Jakiro's early pushing power by clearing creep waves. All of Jakiro's spells are great for Rubick to Spell Steal. Ice Path is a great spell for Rubick so steal, since Rubick has no cast time on stolen abilities, making Rubick's version of Ice Path much more reliable than Jakiro's. Macropyre is a great way for Rubick to deal immense amount of damage.

pairs.name: Morphling
pairs.reason: Morphling has high mobility with Waveform and can escape Macropyre and Ice Path easily. He shifts into high Strength during Jakiro’s slow damage over time from Dual Breath and Liquid Fire. He can also Morph into Jakiro and use his spells effectively. Jakiro’s lack of burst damage makes it hard to punish Morphling early.

pairs.name: Pangolier
pairs.reason: Pangolier’s Rolling Thunder interrupts Jakiro’s long cast animations. Jakiro has no mobility and gets chain-stunned easily by Shield Crash and Rolling Thunder. Dual Breath and Ice Path are hard to land on a rolling Pangolier.

pairs.name: Tidehunter
pairs.reason: Tidehunter shrugs off Jakiro’s spell with high natural HP regen and Kraken Shell dispell. Ravage disrupts Jakiro's spell casting and team fight setup. Jakiro cannot zone Tide effectively in lane due to Anchor Smash reducing his damage. Jakiro's slow damage output can't threaten Tide post-laning phase.

pairs.name: Tinker
pairs.reason: Tinker rearms and keeps his distance, while Jakiro lacks gap-closing and burst. March of the Machines clears waves faster than Jakiro can push. Ice Path and Macropyre don’t reach Tinker once he starts blinking and hiding.

pairs.name: Batrider
pairs.reason: Batrider dominates Jakiro in lane with Sticky Napalm stacking. Jakiro’s slow cast times make him vulnerable to Lasso initiation. Flamebreak and Firefly kill him quickly as he lacks escape tools.

pairs.name: Legion Commander
pairs.reason: Legion easily duels Jakiro due to his immobility and low armor. Jakiro’s slow cast time makes it hard to react to Duel. Even if Jakiro survives, his damage-over-time spells won’t stop Legion’s single-target burst. Legion builds BKB/Scetper early, ignoring Jakiro’s control spells.

pairs.name: Huskar
pairs.reason: Huskar’s high magic resistance from Berserker’s Blood makes him resist all of Jakiro’s magic damage. He jumps Jakiro with Life Break and melts him in seconds. Jakiro cannot disengage once Huskar is on top of him. Ice Path is too slow to interrupt his aggressive plays.

pairs.name: Pudge
pairs.reason: Pudge has various ways of saving his teammates from Batrider's spells. He can Meat Hook his allies away from Firefly or Batrider himself during Flaming Lasso to drag his ally back to safety. He can also pick up an Aghanim's Shard and use Dismember on an ally to cancel the Flaming Lasso altogether or prevent Flamebreak's burn duration.

pairs.name: Abaddon
pairs.reason: Aphotic Shield is a low cooldown Strong Dispel, which can dispel both Flaming Lasso as well as remove Sticky Napalm Stacks consistently. Borrowed Time can be used DURING Flaming Lasso to dispel it.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: Dark Pact is a low cooldown Strong Dispel, which can dispel Flaming Lasso, Flamebreak's DOT as well as remove Sticky Napalm Stacks consistently. Pounce provides a reliable lockdown for Batrider to mitigate his mobility and Shadow Dance and Depth Shroud prevent Flaming Lasso from being cast on anyone under their effects.

pairs.name: Oracle
pairs.reason: False Promise is a Strong Dispel and can dispel Flaming Lasso as well as Sticky Napalm and Flamebreak's DOT. Fortune's End provides additional dispel for Stick Napalm and Flamebreak as well as a root to control Batrider. Even if both of them are on cooldown Fate's Edict still provides protection from Batrider's exclusively magic damage kit..

pairs.name: Ursa
pairs.reason: By itself Ursa's Enrage provides sufficient Status Resistance and Damage reduction on its own to mitigate Flaming Lasso's effects. Aghanim's Scepter however allows Ursa to Enrage DURING Flaming Lasso and outright kill Batrider. Earthshock can be used to traverse terrain and stick on Batrider during his Firefly.

pairs.name: Legion Commander
pairs.reason: Press the Attack is a Strong Dispel and can dispel Flaming Lasso as well as Sticky Napalm and Flamebreak's DOT. Duel provides substantial lockdown for an elusive Batrider and can be used as counter initiation to his Flaming Lasso.

pairs.name: Tidehunter
pairs.reason: Kraken Shell removes Sticky Napalm stacks and dispels Flaming Lasso quickly. Tide is tanky enough to frontline and make Batrider’s pickoff attempts meaningless with Ravage follow-up during dives.

pairs.name: Viper
pairs.reason: Batrider suffers against ranged magic harass, and Nethertoxin punishes his tendency to stay in one spot. Viper zones him out of lane and teamfights with longer range and persistent damage.

pairs.name: Enigma
pairs.reason: Batrider needs to dive into fights, but Black Hole punishes him for doing so. Midnight Pulse also melts his HP rapidly. Enigma’s control can outscale Bat's early tempo if he farms well.

pairs.name: Phoenix
pairs.reason: Phoenix stays far away from Sticky Napalm stacks and zones Bat with Sun Ray. Supernova disrupts Bat’s dives, forcing him to retreat or commit fully into a losing fight. Phoenix also heals Lasso targets.

pairs.name: Alchemist
pairs.reason: Chen's core mechanic is having an army of creeps to aid him in battle - Alchemist's core mechanic is killing creeps as they yield extra gold. This leaves Chen in an awkward spot as every engagement with Alch could just spiral his netwroth out of control. Alchemist's strong early game allows him to deal with Chen's early game pressure better than most heroes as he can drop an Acid Spray in front of a tower to hinder Chen's push.

pairs.name: Earthshaker
pairs.reason: Earthshaker is strong against Chen. His Echo Slam deals massive damage based on the number of enemy units, making Chen’s controlled creeps a liability in teamfights. Fissure and Enchant Totem help control Chen and isolate his heroes or creeps. Earthshaker can punish Chen’s grouped pushes by blinking in and wiping out both creeps and heroes. Overall, Chen’s strength in numbers plays directly into Earthshaker’s AoE burst, making Earthshaker a solid counter.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: His illusions make it difficult for Chen to control or kill him quickly. Phantom Lancer’s high mobility and confusing presence force Chen to waste creeps and spells.Chen’s single-target abilities struggle to keep up with Phantom Lancer’s illusion spam and escape potential.

pairs.name: Sven
pairs.reason: His Great Cleave allows him to deal massive area damage, quickly wiping out Chen’s summoned units. Storm Hammer provides reliable lockdown on Chen or his creeps, preventing escape or control. With proper positioning, Sven can dominate teamfights by removing Chen’s army and focusing Chen himself.

pairs.name: Tiny
pairs.reason: His burst damage and stun can quickly kill Chen’s controlled creeps and heroes. Tiny’s Avalanche and Toss combo disrupt Chen’s positioning and cancel creep attacks. He can clear Chen’s creep army fast with Tree Grab and AoE damage. Tiny’s burst and mobility make it hard for Chen to execute his early push and control strategy.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: His Blink lets him dodge Chen’s disables and reposition in fights. Anti-Mage’s Mana Break burns Chen’s mana, limiting his ability to cast spells and control creeps. With Mana Void, Anti-Mage punishes Chen’s high mana usage and low mobility. Anti-Mage’s farming speed and late-game scaling make it difficult for Chen to keep up or control the map.

pairs.name: Sand King
pairs.reason: His Burrowstrike provides a reliable stun to interrupt Chen’s spells and creep control. Sand King’s Sand Storm lets him avoid damage while poking Chen and his creeps. Epicenter can quickly clear Chen’s army and deal huge AoE damage in teamfights. Overall, Sand King’s mobility and AoE control counter Chen’s pushing and creep-based strategies effectively.

pairs.name: Keeper of the Light
pairs.reason: His Blinding Light can disrupt Chen’s creep attacks by forcing creeps to miss their targets. Keeper’s strong mana regeneration and spammable spells allow him to out-sustain Chen in lane. Illuminate and Spirit Form deal high AoE damage, quickly clearing Chen’s creep army. Keeper’s control and damage make it difficult for Chen to maintain pressure or push effectively.

pairs.name: Dawnbreaker
pairs.reason: Her high burst damage and mobility allow her to quickly kill Chen’s creeps and heroes. Dawnbreaker’s Starbreaker can cleave through Chen’s summoned units, reducing his pushing power. Her Solar Guardian ultimate provides global presence to counter Chen’s map control and rotations.

pairs.name: Morphling
pairs.reason: His high mobility and Waveform let him dodge Chen’s disables and engage or escape easily. Morphling’s burst damage can quickly kill Chen’s controlled creeps and heroes. He can replicate Chen or key creeps with Morph, confusing Chen’s team and turning his own units against him.Morphling’s strong late-game scaling outmatches Chen’s early push and utility.

pairs.name: Abaddon
pairs.reason: Abaddon provides healing and sustain and barriers, which do wonders versus Spectre as she struggles to output significant damage proactively and lacks burst. Aphotic Shield dispels Spectral Dagger and his Aghanim's Scepter further amplifies his impact as it makes him heal in an AOE.

pairs.name: Underlord
pairs.reason: Underlord is able to abuse Spectre when she's at her weakest - in the laning stage. He can constanly harass and pressure her in addition to reducing her rightclick damage in order to deny her creeps. His global ult helps keep up with Spectre's global presence.

pairs.name: Undying
pairs.reason: Undying is able to abuse Spectre when she's at her weakest - in the laning stage. He can constantly harass and pressure her with Decay and Rightclicks in order to disrupt her ability to secure sufficient resources in the lane, offsetting her entire game.

pairs.name: Wraith King
pairs.reason: Wraith King's innate sustain allows him to man fight Spectre as by herself she doesn't output amazing damage and the Dispersion damage she relies on is offset by WK's Lifesteal. Silver Edge, which provides Break is a naturally great pickup for WK. He's got 2 lives.

pairs.name: Dark Seer
pairs.reason: Dark Seer is able shut Spectre down in lane due to Ion Shell and offset her game entirely. What's worse is that even if Spectre ever gets to that late game where she thrives, Dark Seer is able to make multiple Illusions of her and use Spectre's strength against her and her team as Wall of Replica and Normal Punch (Aghanim's Scepter Upgrade) Illusions inherit Desolate.

pairs.name: Oracle
pairs.reason: Oracle provides healing and sustain, which do wonders versus Spectre as she struggles to output significant damage proactively and lacks burst. Fortune's End dispels Spectral Dagger, Fate's Edict prevents Spectre from attacking and his ult - False Promise is an all purpose save button.

pairs.name: Io
pairs.reason: Healing, sustain and durability do wonders versus Spectre as she struggles to output significant damage proactively and lacks burst. Io supplies his team with plenty of that. On top of that he can use his ult - Relocate as a last rest save.

pairs.name: Necrophos
pairs.reason: Necro can sustain himself and easily pressure Spectre in lane with Death Pulse. Worse than that he can also sustain his allies due to his AOE heals. Ghost Shroud prevents Spectre from attacking him and Dispersion does neither reduce nor reflect any damage from Hearthstopper Aura.

pairs.name: Ember Spirit
pairs.reason: Ember Spirit's early game prowess and proneness to roaming with ease as early as minute 6 makes Spectre and easy target for him. Often times Spectre would have to relinquish her lane, even if it is going well, in order to not show on the map until she's strong enough to fight back.

pairs.name: Lifestealer
pairs.reason: Lifestealer is one of Spectre's hardest counters as his kit counters Spectre at EVERY stage of the game. LS is so good against her that even if he is an ENTIRE item behind he still easily wins out. His abundance of lifesteal combined with his debuff immunity and actual immunity from Infest is too much for Spectre to handle.

pairs.name: Witch Doctor
pairs.reason: Witch Doctor provides his team with much needed AOE heal to mitigate Spectre's Dipsersion and Radiance damage. He has a natural save against her with Aghanim's Shard, which is a staple item for him and a Maledict into Death Ward combo is usually enough to get her killed in the early-mid game.

pairs.name: Meepo
pairs.reason: Simply put, as strong as Spectre can get she is 1 body and Meepo can be 5. Meepo generally builds stats items to becomes quite tanky and has multiple ways of sustaing himself between Ransack and both Aghanim's Shard and Scepter. On top of that he can root Spectre indefinitely with multiple Earthbinds.

pairs.name: Pudge
pairs.reason: A core Pudge can decimate a Spectre both in lane and in game. In lane, his base damage is about 50% higher than Spectre's, making last hitting difficult. Due to Rot + Aghanim's Scepter being enough damage for Pudge that leaves him the rest of his inventory slots for sustain and tank items. Often Spectre finds herself rundown by Pudge.

pairs.name: Enchantress
pairs.reason: Enchatress provides consistent harass in lane with both her Impetus, rightclicks and a creep from Enchant. Her ult - Untouchable makes it almost impossible for Spectre to land a hit on her before she gets some Attack Speed items and Enchantress Nature's Attendants provide healing and sustain for her and her team.

pairs.name: Slardar
pairs.reason: Slardar can completely crush a Spectre in lane due to his abundance of damage and crowd control and forces her to leave lane as he hits level 6. His ult - Corrosive Haze serves as a reliable debuff and provides vision of Spectre troughout the game substracting up to 3000 gold of value from Spectre in terms of armor.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: Slark's Essence Shift steals stats directly from Spectre and does't get mitigated by Dispresion in any way. Slark's various sources of sustain (Barracuda, Shadow Dance, Depth Shroud - Aghanim's Shard Upgrade) and Dark Pact being a low-cooldown dispel for Spectral Dagger gives Slark all the tool he needs to deal with Spectre.

pairs.name: Doom
pairs.reason: Doom is able to prevent Spectre from receiving any heals by using his ult - Doom on her, effectively removing her from the fight. In lane, he is able to reliably pressure her with all 3 of his basic spells if he finds a suitable neutral creep. Additionally, as the game goes on Doom can enhance his ult with Break.

pairs.name: Shadow Demon
pairs.reason: Shadow Demon can Break with his ult - Demonic Purge, once he picks up Aghanim's Scepter. Half of Spectre's Spells are passives and most of her damage comes exactly from those 2 passives so Break effects inhibit her more than any other hero in DOTA. Additionally, he can save teammates with Disruption from Spectre's global initiation and create Spectre Illusions of his own that inherit Desolate.

pairs.name: Viper
pairs.reason: Viper has a reliable short cool down Break with his ult - Viper Strike. Half of Spectre's Spells are passives and most of her damage comes exactly from those 2 passives so Break effects inhibit her more than any other hero in DOTA. In lane, Viper is able to harass and pressure her significantly with Poison Touch.

pairs.name: Shadow Shaman
pairs.reason: Shadow Shaman can Break Spectre with his Hex once he enhances it with his talent. Half of Spectre's Spells are passives and most of her damage comes exactly from those 2 passives so Break effects inhibit her more than any other hero in DOTA. He naturally builds Blink Dagger and can setup for his team on Spectre.

pairs.name: Primal Beast
pairs.reason: Primal Beast has a spammable Break once he gets to his Aghanim's Scepter. Half of Spectre's Spells are passives and most of her damage comes exactly from those 2 passives so Break effects inhibit her more than any other hero in DOTA. On top of that he likes to apply pressure early AND he itemizes quite tanky.

pairs.name: Phantom Assassin
pairs.reason: Phantom Assassin can pick up and Aghs Shard as early as the 15 minute mark to give her a low-cooldown AOE Break. Half of Spectre's Spells are passives and most of her damage comes exactly from those 2 passives so Break effects inhibit her more than any other hero in DOTA. Her insane burst damage in combination with Break can utterly delete a Spectre.

pairs.name: Hoodwink
pairs.reason: Hoowink can Break with her ult - Sharpshooter and is not uncommon for a Spectre to be comboed to death by a single Hoodwink even if she's support. Half of Spectre's Spells are passives and most of her damage comes exactly from those 2 passives so Break effects inhibit her more than any other hero in DOTA.

pairs.name: Leshrac
pairs.reason: Leshrac deals massive amounts of AOE damage without having to itemize for it - this allows him to itemize for sustain and tankiness in order to buy himself time to unleash that damage. For most of the game Spectre struggles to output enough damage to go trough his sustain alone and often find herself being rundown by Leshrac.

pairs.name: Brewmaster
pairs.reason: Simply put Spectre is unable to do enough damage to kill Brewmaster during his ult - Primal Split, forcing her to kite instead of fight in an attempt to wait it out. In lane, Brewmaster is able to greatly pressure Spectre with just his basic spells and force her to leave lane early.

pairs.name: Dazzle
pairs.reason: Dazzle's entire kit works too well against Spectre. His Poison touch can easily get the lane out of control and boot Spectre out of lane early, even from the support position. His Grave provides a save for his teamates and Shadow Wave is an AOE heal, which Spectres generally struggle against.

pairs.name: Broodmother
pairs.reason: Broodmother's fast-paced and push-oriented gameplay, when paired against Spectre's weak early game, can easily result in Spectre and her team being set back so much that a comeback is highly improbable. She simply lacks the tools to deal with heavy early aggression. She also has built in sustain and high kill threat on Spectre in the early game.

pairs.name: Chen
pairs.reason: Chen's fast-paced and push-oriented gameplay, when paired against Spectre's weak early game, can easily result in Spectre and her team being set back so much that a comeback is highly improbable. She simply lacks the tools to deal with heavy early aggression. In lane, Chen can completely crush a Spectre with his creeps and provides an extra layer of healing for his team.

pairs.name: Beastmaster
pairs.reason: Beastmater's fast-paced and push-oriented gameplay, when paired against Spectre's weak early game, can easily result in Spectre and her team being set back so much that a comeback is highly improbable. She simply lacks the tools to deal with heavy early aggression. In lane, he can easily pressure her with his Summons and Wild Axes.

She simply lacks the tools to deal with heavy early aggression. In lane, he can easily pressure her with summons and just his high stats.

pairs.reason: Lycan's fast-paced and push-oriented gameplay, when paired against Spectre's weak early game, can easily result in Spectre and her team being set back so much that a comeback is highly improbable. She simply lacks the tools to deal with heavy early aggression. In lane, he can completely crush her with his Spirit Bear being so high stated.

pairs.name: Visage
pairs.reason: Visage's fast-paced and push-oriented gameplay, when paired against Spectre's weak early game, can easily result in Spectre and her team being set back so much that a comeback is highly improbable. She simply lacks the tools to deal with heavy early aggression. In lane, he can easily pressure her with Soul Assumption and rightclicks.

pairs.name: Tinker
pairs.reason: Tinker provides healing, sustain and barriers, which do wonders versus Spectre as she struggles to output significant damage proactively and lacks burst. March of the Machines can heal in an AOE, Defense Matrix provides a Barrier and Status Resist and Laser prevents Spectre from landing attacks. His innate - Eureka! allows him to spam Greaves and Holy Locket in a fight.

pairs.name: Omniknight
pairs.reason: Healing, sustain and durability do wonders versus Spectre as she struggles to output significant damage proactively and lacks burst. Omniknight supplies his team with plenty of that. Even his Aghanim's Scepter makes his ult - Guardian Angel global, to help match Spectre's global pressence.

pairs.name: Juggernaut
pairs.reason: Juggernaut is one of the strongest early game carries that doesn't mind grouping up to take objectives early and that's Spectre's weakest point of the game. She simply lacks the tools to deal with early aggression. His Healing Ward provides massive AOE sustain, Omnislash can outright kill Spectre, Blade Fury dispels Spectral Dagger and later in the game Blade Dance starts healing him.

pairs.name: Huskar
pairs.reason: Huskar's fast-paced and push-oriented gameplay, when paired against Spectre's weak early game, can easily result in Spectre and her team being set back so much that a comeback is highly improbable. She simply lacks the tools to deal with heavy early aggression. He has amazing sustain, increased Magic Resistance and is able to dispel Spectral Dagger with Life Break.

pairs.name: Troll Warlord
pairs.reason: Troll has amazing rightclick and consistent damage scaling from his base abilities alone - this allows him to itemize for sustain and mobility so he give himself the best opportunity to land all that damage. He can chain root Spectre into a 1v1 she can rarely win as Troll's Battle Trance additionally provides him with massive lifesteal and the inability to die to damage.

pairs.name: Dawnbreaker
pairs.reason: Dawnbreaker is a nightmare for Spectre to lane into as DB is able s to apply immense pressure with his Star Breaker and Celestial Hammer spells alone, while sustaining herself with Luminosity. More importantly Solar Guardian is able to match Spectre's global pressene perfectly as it provides AOE healing and Crowd Control on top of being global.

pairs.name: Timbersaw
pairs.reason: Timbersaw can completely boot a Spectre out of lane even before leveling up his ult as he does overwhelming damage via Whirling Death and Timber Chain, while having plenty of sustain from Reactive Armor. Throughout the game Spectre struggles to comfortably go on Timber as that just gives him an opportunity to cast his spells efficiently.

pairs.name: Pudge
pairs.reason: Pudge Support can pickup an early Aghanim's Shard in order to save his allies from Frost Blast - Dismembered allies do not heal but also do not have their health reduced in any way allowing them to wait out the Frost Blast debuff duration in safety. Meat Hook is effective at pulling teammates away from Cold Feet's stun radius.

pairs.name: Storm Spirit
pairs.reason: Storm's mobility allows him to easily get on top of AA and has enough damage to kill him reliably. Ball of Lightning allows him to easily dodge Ice Blast and get away from Cold Feet in order to dispel it. Ball of Lihgtning can also disjoint any Chilling Touch hits and makes retreating back to safety easy for Storm.

pairs.name: Lycan
pairs.reason: Lycan's mobility allows him to easily get on top of AA and has enough damage to kill him reliably. Shapeshift essentially provides him with Haste making it difficult for AA to connect his Ice Blast and easy for Lycan to leave Cold Feet's stun radius. Summon Wolves on their own are able to apply enough pressure for AA and force him to kite them.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: AA's quite mana intensive due to the low cooldowns of his spells, which makes him a great target for Mana Void. Blink is amazing for both closing the gap and dodging/disengaging Ice Blast or Cold Feet. Counterspell can block/reflect Cold Feet and provides Magic Resistance to significantly mitigate AA's exclusive magic damage output.

pairs.name: Medusa
pairs.reason: Medusa's Mana Shield is essentially her HP bar, which makes her the perfect counter to Ice Blast as it does not affect mana regeneration in any way, completely rendering the impact of the spell to only a fraction of it. Manta and Butterly are staple items for Medusa, with which she can Dispel Cold Feet and Evade Chilling Touch hits.

pairs.name: Weaver
pairs.reason: Shukuchi allows Weaver to easily get on top of AA or to disengage from Cold Feet or Ice Blast. Time Lapse is able to restore HP during Ice Blast as it does not function as a heal and can be further upgraded with Aghanim's Scepter to save allies. Additionally, Time Lapse can dispel Cold Feet and Shukuchi can disjoint the occasional Chilling Touch hit.

pairs.name: Night Stalker
pairs.reason: Night Stalker counters Ancient Apparition with his high mobility and silence, limiting AA’s ability to cast Ice Blast and other spells.

pairs.name: Brewmaster
pairs.reason: Brewmaster is good against Ancient Apparition because his Primal Split can dodge Ice Blast and avoid its healing prevention. His strong stuns and disables can lock down AA before he casts spells.

pairs.name: Arc Warden
pairs.reason: Tempest Double allows Arc to fight even when Doomed, diminishing Doom's impact. His Magnetic Field provides evasion for him and his team making Infernal Blade clunky to use due to Doom's increased attack range. Arc's split pushing and kiting potential make it hard for Doom to control him, effectively countering Doom's single-target, ultimate-dependant playstyle.

pairs.name: Meepo
pairs.reason: Divided we Stand allows Meepo to keep most of his impact even when Doomed. Most importantly, Megameepo (Aghanim's Scepeter Upgrade) allows Meepo Prime to save any of his Meepo's from Doom and completely prevent the Doomed Meepo from receiving any damage for its duration from any source other than Doom. This greatly complicates Doom's gameplay as post Aghanim's Scepeter he is forced to Doom Meepo Prime, who can just stay back and Poof himself onto the Doomed Meepo to save him.

pairs.name: Medusa
pairs.reason: Mana Shield does not take into account any Armor or Magic Resistance, making it the perfect counter to Doom's Pure Damage. Cold Blooded (Aghanim's Shard Upgrade) when combined with Aghanim's Scepeter allows Dusa to stun Doom upon casting Doom and naturally create distance. Doom lacks Mana Burn and the Attack Speed to justify a Diffusal/Disperser and struggles greatly to get trough Dusa's Manapool.

pairs.name: Lone Druid
pairs.reason: If you Doom the Spirit Bear LD can just resummon it if it happens to die, if you Doom LD then the Spirit Bear runs rampant. True Form's transformation time does not get interrupted by Doom and is not considered a heal, providing its HP bonus despite Doom's healing negation.

pairs.name: Rubick
pairs.reason: Spell Steal allows Rubick to cast a significantly improved version of Doom as it increases its duration and damage greatly, while reducing its cooldown. Telekinesis once improved with Aghanim's Shard can be used as a pseudo save for any Doomed targets and reposition them to safety.

pairs.name: Night Stalker
pairs.reason: Night Stalker thrives in darkness, gaining increased vision, movement speed, and silence, which makes it harder for Doom to control or escape him. Night Stalker’s tankiness and ability to chase down targets during nighttime make it difficult for Doom to survive or get his full combo off effectively.

pairs.name: Batrider
pairs.reason: Batrider’s Flaming Lasso can catch Doom early in fights and lock him down before Doom can react. Batrider’s burst damage and mobility let him focus Doom quickly, preventing Doom from using his ultimate effectively. If Doom gets caught first, he can be killed before turning the fight around. So against Batrider, Doom needs to be careful with positioning and timing to avoid getting disabled and burst down early.

pairs.name: Wraith King
pairs.reason: Wraith King’s Reincarnation gives him a built-in second life, which makes him naturally resilient against Doom. Even if Doom uses his ultimate to silence and disable Wraith King, when Wraith King dies, he comes back with full health and mana, allowing him to fight back. This makes it harder for Doom to lock him down and kill him outright

pairs.name: Tusk
pairs.reason: Tusk can be a great save against Doom’s ultimate because of his Snowball ability. When an ally is doomed and about to get focused, Tusk can quickly roll in with Snowball, grab that ally and others, and give them a moment of invulnerability inside the snowball. This can disrupt Doom’s damage and disable, giving the doomed ally a chance to survive or escape once the Snowball ends. So Tusk’s save potential really helps counter Doom’s lockdown in team fights.

pairs.name: Lina
pairs.reason: Lina can definitely punish Doom if she catches him off guard from the backlines. Her high burst damage with abilities like Laguna Blade can quickly melt Doom before he gets a chance to use his ultimate or tank up. Since Doom isn’t very mobile, if Lina positions well and jumps on him early, she can take him out of the fight fast. So Lina’s burst and range make her a real threat to Doom.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: Ursa has no sustained AoE to deal with illusions, it becomes worse since Phantom Lancer can create more illusions in a matter of seconds. Diffusal Blade can be used to drain Ursa mana. This is a standard item for Phantom Lancer in every match. Doppelganger applies basic dispel on Phantom Lancer, which will remove the slow from Earthshock. It also resets fights with more illusions, making hard for Ursa to hit the real Phantom Lancer. Manta Style creates two more illusions and also applies a basic dispel, further complicating the problem for Ursa to deal with.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: Enrage cannot restore attributes stolen by Essence Shift and will reduce his physical damage output. Even if Ursa initiates with Earthshock, Slark can Pounce away or use Dark Pact after Ursa's initiation to avoid Fury Swipes' damage until Earthshock's slow is gone. Shadow Dance provides a save against the initiation of Ursa.

pairs.name: Chaos Knight
pairs.reason: Ursa has no way to clear illusions quickly, making him vulnerable to Chaos Bolt and Phantasm combo. Reality Rift can quickly relocate or reinitiate on Ursa once the duration of Enrage is over. Phantasm can be used to dispel Earthshock's slow. Manta Style is another item that counter Ursa greatly. Ursa has low mobility, once jumped on by Reality Rift, Ursa struggles to escape. Doom

pairs.name: Troll Warlord
pairs.reason: Troll Warlord can be a tough matchup for Ursa. Whirling Axes apply miss chance, making it difficult for Ursa to land attacks and build Fury Swipes stacks. If Ursa initiates first, Troll can activate Battle Trance and potentially outlast Ursa in a drawn-out manfight.
