pairs.name: Winter Wyvern
pairs.reason: Cold Embrace completely negates Ursa’s physical damage while healing the target, shutting down his burst potential. Winter’s Curse can also turn Ursa’s high attack speed and damage against his own team, often causing him to burst down an ally

pairs.name: Disruptor
pairs.reason: Disruptor is a strong control hero against Ursa. Kinetic Field can trap Ursa and prevent him from chasing or escaping. More importantly, Static Storm silences Ursa, preventing him from activating Enrage, which makes him highly vulnerable during its duration.

pairs.name: Drow Ranger
pairs.reason: Drow Ranger counters Ursa by kiting him with Frost Arrows and silencing him with Gust, preventing him from using Enrage. Her high physical damage from range makes it difficult for Ursa to close the gap and survive long enough to fight back

pairs.name: Clockwerk
pairs.reason: Spirit Breaker can never connect the Charge of Darkness on Clockwerk as long as he has Power Cogs off cooldown, as he can easily put them down before Spirit Breaker reaches him to push him away. Clockwerk's Battery Assault, Power Cogs, and Hookshot lockdown all stop Spirit Breaker from Charging away from him as well. The mana burn from Power Cogs also massively affects Spirit Breaker because of his low mana pool, and can render him unable to use his entire spell combo.

pairs.name: Dark Willow
pairs.reason: Dark Willow's Bramble Maze massively counters Spirit Breaker's Charge of Darkness as it stops the Charge mid way if any of the Brambles fall in the Charge path. This makes it extremely difficult for Spirit Breaker to Charge in and out of fights as long as Dark Willow puts down her Bramble Maze. Dark Willow can also pop Shadow Realm before Spirit Breaker's Charge connects on her to stop him from following up with Nether Strike or his Greater Bash right clicks. Cursed Crown and Terrorize also let Dark Willow interrupt Charge of Darkness.

pairs.name: Ember Spirit
pairs.reason: Ember Spirit has an easy time dodging the Charge of Darkness collision by timing his Sleight of Fist on a cluster of units when Charge is about to connect on him. If Ember Spirit doesn't have units for Sleight of Fist around him, he can still use Sleight of Fist into Searing Chains on Spirit Breaker from range to stop the Charge mid way to stop him from getting in and out of fights. Flame Guard also absorbs damage from Spirit Breaker's spells and Greater Bash procs while jumping to Fire Remnants keeps Ember Spirit safe from ever dying.

pairs.name: Enigma
pairs.reason: Enigma's instant stun from Malefice lets him easily stop Spirit Breaker from Charging at him, or away from fights, by interrupting the spell. Spirit Breaker also has a difficult time interrupting Black Hole through Charge of Darkness or Nether Strike without getting caught in the AoE himself. Enigma's Eidolons also have high magic resistance, which keeps them safe from dying to the Charge collision.

pairs.name: Invoker
pairs.reason: Invoker has multiple ways of stopping Spirit Breaker's Charge to ensure he does not connect with his spell. Spirit Breaker can practically never cast his ultimate when affected by Cold Snap as it gets interrupted by damage instances. The slow from Ice Wall also doesn't let Spirit Breaker Charge away or into fights. Invoker's Tornado also dispels Bulldoze, which is Spirit Breaker's main survival tool.

pairs.name: Medusa
pairs.reason: Medusa's mana pool, which is effectively her HP pool, doesn't take a massive hit from Spirit Breaker's Charge of Darkness into Nether Strike combo, and keeps her safe from ever being threatened by the lockdown. Medusa can also pop Stone Gaze while Spirit Breaker is Charging towards her, which slows him down and turns him to stone if he gets too close. Once Medusa gets Aghanim's Shard, Spirit Breaker can never Charge at her as doing so will reflect a Mystic Snake towards him, which turns him to stone and interrupts the Charge.

pairs.name: Morphling
pairs.reason: Morphling loves to Morph into Spirit Breaker to use his Bulldoze for the status resistance in fights, which makes him practically impossible to get bursted down. The Morphed Charge of Darkness also gives Morphling an initiation and lockdown tool to get on top of an enemy hero and burst them down with his massive damage through spells and right clicks. Morphling can also time his Waveform and use it in Spirit Breaker's Charge direction when it is about to connect to avoid getting stunned.

pairs.name: Puck
pairs.reason: Despite her squishy nature, Puck remains safe from Spirit Breaker's ganks in the laning stage as a well timed Phase Shift lets her dodge the collision lockdown and damage. Puck can easily follow up with the Waning Rift silence to stop Spirit Breaker's Nether Strike usage, and create distance between herself and him by Jaunting to her Illusory Orb. Puck's Dream Coil also leashes Spirit Breaker and stops him from Charging in and out of fights, although he can break the link for a low duration stun by using Bulldoze.

pairs.name: Rubick
pairs.reason: Rubick's instant lift from Telekinesis lets him easily stop Spirit Breaker from Charging at him, or away from fights, by interrupting the spell. Rubick can also land Spirit Breaker away from himself to avoid Nether Strike as well because of its low cast range. Rubick also loves to Steal Charge of Darkness to get himself a mobility and initiation tool that also lets him farm creeps along with Fade Bolt.

pairs.name: Shadow Demon
pairs.reason: Shadow Demon's instant banish from Disruption lets him easily stop Spirit Breaker from Charging at him, or away from fights, by interrupting the spell. Shadow Demon's Demonic Purge also dispels Bulldoze, and massively slows down Spirit Breaker's movement speed during his Charge to practically keep him stuck in place.

pairs.name: Storm Spirit
pairs.reason: Storm Spirit's Ball Lightning lets him easily dodge the Charge of Darkness lockdown and damage by timing his spell in Spirit Breaker's Charge direction when it is about to connect. Storm Spirit can just as easily Ball Lightning away afterwards to create distance between himself and Spirit Breaker, or use his burst damage and lockdown to turn the fight.

pairs.name: Underlord
pairs.reason: Pit of Malice is amazing at interrupting Spirit Breaker's Charge, which is his core spell and additionally prevents him from using his Nether Strike for the root's duration, crippling his presence in fights significantly. The Status Resistance from Bulldoze greatly compresses the damage from Firestorm within it's reduced duration but does not reduce the total amount, making it less of a damage over time interaction and more into a nuke.

pairs.name: Arc Warden
pairs.reason: Arc kites Gyro with Spark Wraiths and constant slow. His Tempest Double safely harasses from range, while Gyro can't reach or burst him before being chipped down.

pairs.name: Lifestealer
pairs.reason: Lifestealer shrugs off Gyro’s magic damage with Rage. He can also infest and burst Gyro in fights, taking advantage of Gyro’s low armor and lack of hard disables.

pairs.name: Viper
pairs.reason: Viper’s Nethertoxin shuts down Flak Cannon by disabling passives. His poison and Break effects reduce Gyro’s ability to sustain or kite.

pairs.name: Ancient Apparition
pairs.reason: Ice Blast nullifies Gyro’s healing from Satanic and other regen sources. AA's long-range harass also punishes Gyro’s slow early movement.

pairs.name: Razor
pairs.reason: Razor drains Gyro’s damage mid-fight with Static Link, making Flak Cannon almost useless. Razor also tanks through magical burst and out-sustains in lane.

pairs.name: Juggernaut
pairs.reason: Juggernaut can Blade Fury through all of Gyro’s early-game magic. Omnislash cuts down Gyro, who has no strong escape or disable to stop it.

pairs.name: Keeper of the Light
pairs.reason: Blinding Light causes Gyro’s Flak Cannon attacks to miss. KotL’s high mobility and magic burst disrupt Gyro’s teamfight contribution.

pairs.name: Venomancer
pairs.reason: Venomancer kites Gyro with slows .Poison Nova combined with other spells from venomancer allies pressure and makes Gyro’s low HP pool a liability in prolonged fights.

pairs.name: Shadow Demon
pairs.reason: Disruption saves Gyro’s targets from Rocket Barrage or Homing Missile. He can also create illusions that scale better than Gyro in some cases.

pairs.name: Dragon Knight
pairs.reason: DK's Frost Dragon facet reduces Chemical Rage's healing substantially, which is Alch's main defensive tool. Additionally, he can reduce his overall damage output greatly with Breather Fire and Frost Dragon and provides reliable lockdown with Dragon Tail. His strong early game allows him to match Alch's strong early game better than most heroes.

pairs.name: Pudge
pairs.reason: Aghanim's Scepter and Shiva's Guard are staple items for Pudge and reduce Chemical Rage's healing, which is Alch's main defensive tool. Pudge is able to provide a strong permament slow on Alch preventing him from both attacking and retreating and has a reliable lockdown with Dismember.

pairs.name: Ancient Apparition
pairs.reason: AA's Ice Blast negates Chemical Rage's healing completely, which is Alch's main defensive tool. This usually forces Alch to flee from the fight entirely and wait it out. Additionally, his facet Bone Chill reduces strenght, which further impacts his overall potency.

pairs.name: Drow Ranger
pairs.reason: Drow Rangers's Aghanim's Scpeter reduces Chemical Rage's healing significantly, which is Alch's main defensive tool. She is able to provide a strong consistent slow on Alch preventing him from both attacking and retreating and does more than enough damage to kill him.

pairs.name: Doom
pairs.reason: Doom's Doom negates Chemical Rage's healing completely, which is Alch's main defensive tool. This usually forces Alch to flee from the fight entirely and wait it out. He can Devour a Vhoul Assassin neutral to almost entirely decrease Chemical Rage's sustain outside of Doom.

pairs.name: Necrophos
pairs.reason: Alch's damage is exclusively physical and Necro's Ghost Shroud completely negates it. Reaper's Scythe is a powerful tool to burst him and his Hearthstopper Aura can further reduce Chemical Rage's healing substantially, which is Alch's main defensive tool.

pairs.name: Abaddon
pairs.reason: Abaddon's Apothic Shield can dispel Alch's Unstable Concoction's stun as well as Abyssal Blade's. His innate Withering Mist can reduce Chemical Rage's healing, which is Alch's main defensive tool. He provides sustain for his team to extend the fight past Chemical Rage's duration.

pairs.name: Juggernaut
pairs.reason: In a man fight Alch simply loses to Jugg. Omnislash can provides a reliable burst to outright kill Alch even during Chemical Rage. He can use Blade Flurry to soak Alch's Unstable Concoction and Healing Ward to sustain his team and extend the fight past Chemical Rage's duration.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Anti Mage can easily close the gap on Invoker with Blink and burst him down by burning his mana and finishing him off with Mana Void. The mana burn also means Invoker may not have enough mana to use key defensive spells. Anti Mage can also Blink away from Invoker's spell combo and reflect Cold Snap or Rod of Atos easily.

pairs.name: Broodmother
pairs.reason: Broodmother is a very fast hero and is hard to keep in place to burst down with Invoker's spell combo. Invoker is also a slow hero without active Wex orbs and high levels in Ghost Walk, which makes him vulnerable to get run down by Spiderlings under the Orchid silence, which is a common purchase for Broodmother. The Necrotic Webs facet also reduces the HP regen from active Quas orbs.

pairs.name: Centaur Warrunner
pairs.reason: Centaur's Stampede can easily help his entire time close the gap on a slow and squishy Invoker and burst him down before he can react with his spells. Centaur is also a very high HP hero, and with Blade Mail on top of Retaliate, Invoker can easily die if he throws his spell combo on Centaur.

pairs.name: Doom
pairs.reason: Doom completely shuts down Invoker with his ultimate as he cannot throw any spells in its duration or heal himself with active Quas orbs. Doom can easily run down a slow and squishy Invoker during Scorched Earth and finish him off every time while his ultimate is active.

pairs.name: Faceless Void
pairs.reason: Faceless Void's Time Dilation causes a lot of damage over time and slows down Invoker when he has used his spell combo and most of his spells are on cooldown. This makes it easier for Faceless Void to run him down, even without committing Chronosphere or Time Zone every time. Time Walk also completely counters Invoker's spell combo as Faceless Void can easily gain back all his HP while getting away.

pairs.name: Juggernaut
pairs.reason: Juggernaut's Blade Fury grants him debuff immunity and high magic resistance to take very little damage from Invoker's spell combo, as most of his spells do magic damage and do not pierce spell immunity. Invoker also doesn't have good ways to get away from Omnislash and is susceptible to dying every time when targeted with the ultimate.

pairs.name: Kez
pairs.reason: Kez has a number of mobility spells to close the gap on a slow and squishy Invoker and follow up with his damage spells and silence to kill Invoker every time. Kez's ultimate Raptor Dance also gives him magic damage immunity to nullify most of Invoker's damage spells, and is very hard to lockdown for Invoker's spell combo.

pairs.name: Kunkka
pairs.reason: Kunkka has an easy way to harass Invoker with Tidebringer as he has low HP, armor, and movement speed to dodge the damage. This makes Invoker have more active Quas orbs to stay healthy and low right click damage to contest last hits. Once Kunkka reaches level 6, he always has kill threat on Invoker with his spell combo and right clicks.

pairs.name: Lifestealer
pairs.reason: Lifestealer's Rage grants him debuff immunity and high magic resistance to take very little damage from Invoker's spell combo, as most of his spells do magic damage and do not pierce spell immunity. Lifestealer also has kill threat on a slow and squishy Invoker during Open Wounds as he can dodge Invoker's defensive spells and not let him get away.

pairs.name: Night Stalker
pairs.reason: Night Stalker has massive kill threat on Invoker once he has Blink Dagger to get on top of Invoker and silence him with Crippling Fear. Night Stalker also has flying movement during Dark Ascension as well as high movement and attack speed from his passive to find and stay on top of a slow and squishy Invoker and kill him every time with his massive night vision.

pairs.name: Nyx Assassin
pairs.reason: Nyx Assassin always has kill threat on a squishy Invoker with Vendetta and follow up spell combo alongside Dagon. Invoker's high mana pool works against him as it lets Nyx Assassin do even more damage to him with Mind Flare. Nyx Assassin can also use Invoker's AoE damage spells to stun him with Spiked Carapace. The Nyxth Sense innate also lets him spot Invoker when he's invisible during Ghost Walk.

pairs.name: Pugna
pairs.reason: Pugna's Nether Ward returns massive damage to Invoker every time he casts a spell in its AoE as most of his spells have a high mana cost. Pugna can also threaten Invoker with Life Drain as long as interrupt spells like Cold Snap and Tornado are on cooldown. Life Drain also provides vision on Invoker while he is invisible during Ghost Walk.

pairs.name: Queen of Pain
pairs.reason: Queen of Pain's harass through spells and right clicks in the laning stage makes Invoker keep active Quas orbs for HP regen to stay healthy in the lane, which causes him to do less damage on right clicks to contest last hits. Queen of Pain can easily dodge EMP and the rest of Invoker's spell combo with Blink, which leads to her always having the upper hand in the matchup.

pairs.name: Riki
pairs.reason: Riki's Blink Strike lets him close the gap on a slow and squishy Invoker and do massive backstab damage. Blink Strike along with Tricks of the Trade also let Riki dodge Invoker's EMP and the rest of his spell combo to keep the upper hand in the matchup. Later in the game, Invoker is always an easy kill for Riki with Diffusal Blade, Blink Strike, and Smoke Screen.

pairs.name: Silencer
pairs.reason: Silener's silence through Global Silence and Last Word can completely disrupt Invoker's spell combo throughout the game and render him useless in teamfights. Arcane Curse also lets Silencer do a lot of slow and damage to Invoker if he casts his spell combo while affected by the spell.

pairs.name: Templar Assassin
pairs.reason: Templar Assassin's high damage through Refraction charges always gives her the upper hand in last hits during the laning stage. Psi Blades spill damage also lets her do a lot of damage to Invoker because of his low HP and armor. Invoker's kill threat on Templar Assassin is also significantly reduced by the defensive Refraction barrier charges, which absorb most of the damage instances.

pairs.name: Viper
pairs.reason: Viper has an easy time of applying Poison Attack on a slow and squishy Invoker in the laning stage, which makes him keep active Quas orbs in the lane to stay healthy and leads to not having bonus damage on right clicks to contest last hits. Viper's Corrosive Skin also gives him magic resistance to take much less damage from Invoker's spell combo.

pairs.name: Visage
pairs.reason: Visage has an easy time of running down a slow and squishy Invoker with Familiars under the effect of Grave Chill and Orchid, and follow up with Soul Assumption to do massive damage. Visage can also absorb a lot of damage from Invoker's spell combo with his Gravekeeper's Cloak layers, and later on with Aghanim's Shard, he can completely dodge all the Invoker spells.

pairs.name: Void Spirit
pairs.reason: Void Spirit's Astral Step lets him get on top of Invoker and follow up with his high damage spell combo to kill a squishy Invoker. Spells like Dissimilate and Astral Step also let Void Spirit completely dodge Invoker's entire spell combo. The Sanctuary facet also gives him an all damage barrier to absorb some of the damage from Invoker's spells and right clicks.

pairs.name: Weaver
pairs.reason: Weaver's high mobility with Shukuchi makes it very difficult for Invoker to keep him in place for his spell combo and burst him down. The high mobility also lets Weaver close the gap on Invoker and threaten his life with the high damage right clicks. Time Lapse also lets Weaver completely reverse all the burst damage dealt by Invoker.

pairs.name: Zeus
pairs.reason: Zeus' harass through spells in the laning stage makes Invoker keep active Quas orbs for HP regen to stay healthy in the lane, which causes him to do less damage on right clicks to contest last hits. Queen of Pain can easily dodge EMP and the rest of Invoker's spell combo with Heavenly Jump, which leads to him always having the upper hand in the matchup. Zeus also has ways to find Invoker when he is invisible during Ghost Walk.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: Silencer has no AoE or illusions control, so he gets overwhelmed by PL’s duplicates. PL can easily dodge Arcane Curse and nullify Silencer’s single-target impact. Global Silence doesn’t stop PL’s scaling or survivability.

pairs.name: Tidehunter
pairs.reason: Tidehunter is naturally tanky and can purge Global Silence with Kraken Shell. He shrugs off Silencer’s harass and dominates the teamfight post-silence. Tide doesn't rely on constant spell casting, weakening Silencer’s kit.

pairs.name: Abaddon
pairs.reason: Abaddon dispels Global Silence with Aphotic Shield and his ultimate, Borrowed Time, triggers despite silence. He removes Arcane Curse from himself or allies easily. Silencer has no way to stop Abaddon’s sustain-based playstyle.

pairs.name: Naga Siren
pairs.reason: Silencer struggles heavily against illusions and Naga’s Song of the Siren resets fights, making Global Silence ineffective. Naga also has natural magic resistance and multiple targets to soak Glaives. In the late game, Silencer becomes irrelevant due to illusion spam.

pairs.name: Chen
pairs.reason: Chen doesn’t rely on spell combos in fights, so Global Silence has limited impact. His army of creeps ignores Arcane Curse, Silencer lacks wave clear and can’t pressure Chen’s push strategy.

pairs.name: Arc Warden
pairs.reason: Arc Warden plays at extreme range with clone split push, avoiding teamfights where Global Silence is effective. Spark Wraiths and Magnetic Field protect him from Silencer’s harassment. Silencer can’t easily catch or reach him, and the Tempest Double absorbs silences.

Silencer has no AoE tools to clear spiderlings, making Broodmother dominate the lane and jungle. She’s unaffected by most of Silencer’s harass and controls the map with mobility. Brood can end the game before Silencer gets online.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: Slark thrives in prolonged fights and can purge Arcane Curse and Global Silence with Dark Pact. He benefits from attacking repeatedly, reducing Silencer’s INT with Essence Shift. Silencer has no reliable lockdown to stop him from snowballing.

pairs.name: Lycan
pairs.reason: Silencer has no tools to deal with units or summons, so Lycan's wolves overrun him easily. Lycan doesn’t rely on spells much, rendering Global Silence ineffective. He pushes fast and forces fights before Silencer can scale.

pairs.name: Templar Assassin
pairs.reason: Refraction blocks most of the damage dealt with Arcane Orb and Sanity's Eclipse if used correctly, and is difficult for Outworld Destroyer to deal with. If Astral Imprisonment is on cooldown, then an Outworld Destroyer slowed by Psionic Trap is an easy kill for Templar Assassin, especially during the laning stage.

pairs.name: Sniper
pairs.reason: As Outworld Destroyer has short cast ranges, a short attack range, and no gap-closing abilities, Sniper can kite and harass Outworld Destroyer in lane with his long range and zone him out in fights. The continuous area damage from Shrapnel also prevents Astral-Blink escapes. However, in the late game, Outworld Destroyer's massive damage can overwhelm Sniper once he obtains Blink Dagger, Force Staff etc. to close the gap.

pairs.name: Nyx Assassin
pairs.reason: Outworld Destroyer's high intelligence makes him a good target for Mind Flare. If timed correctly, Spiked Carapace will return the full damage from Sanity's Eclipse back to Outworld Destroyer. Even a reflected Arcane Orb can deal significant damage and make him vulnerable to a follow-up from Nyx Assassin. Spiked Carapace is also the perfect tool against Astral Imprisonment: if used on Nyx, he can reflect the damage back as he comes out of the prison by casting the ability while imprisoned.

pairs.name: Arc Warden
pairs.reason: Arc Warden’s clone creates map pressure Outworld Devourer can’t match, and his magic damage bypasses Astral Imprisonment. Spark Wraiths and Magnetic Field make Outworld Devourer miss attacks and waste time, while Tempest Double can bait Sanity’s Eclipse. Outworld Devourer has poor wave clear, making it hard to respond to constant split pushing.

pairs.name: Broodmother
pairs.reason: Broodmother’s Spiderlings overwhelm Outworld Devourer in lane, and Astral Imprisonment is ineffective against swarm units. She takes over the map and forces Outworld Devourer to fight on her terms. Broodmother snowballs faster than Outworld Devourer can scale and dodges teamfights where he shines.

pairs.name: Lone Druid
pairs.reason: The Spirit Bear soaks Astral Imprisonment or Sanity’s Eclipse, minimizing Outworld Devourer's damage impact. Lone Druid pushes lanes quickly and pressures towers before Outworld Devourer comes online. Outworld Devourer lacks the control or burst to stop the bear from shredding him in fights.

pairs.name: Visage
pairs.reason: Familiars are immune to Astral Imprisonment and take very little magic damage, neutering Outworld Devourer’s core strength. Visage snowballs with push and team presence Outworld Devourer can’t match. His Gravekeeper’s Cloak makes him resistant to burst, and Outworld Devourer struggles to break it fast.

pairs.name: Wraith King
pairs.reason: Outworld Devourer is ineffective against Reincarnation he blows cooldowns just to get through the first life. Sanity’s Eclipse has reduced value due to Wraith King’s high HP and low mana cost skills. In fights, Outworld Devourer wastes time dealing with skeleton summons and tanky targets.

pairs.name: Beastmaster
pairs.reason: Once Brewmaster splits, Outworld Devourer's abilities are nearly useless Astral Imprisonment can’t stop multiple Brewlings. Cyclone completely removes Outworld Devourer from fights, and he can’t deal with the micro. Brewmaster’s utility and disruption counter Outworld Devourer’s need for stationary, uninterrupted casting.

pairs.name: Silencer
pairs.reason: Silencer’s Global Silence prevents Outworld Devourer from casting Astral Imprisonment defensively, completely ruining his utility. Arcane Curse punishes Outworld Devourer's spell-dependent nature. In lane and fights, Silencer shuts down Outworld Devourer's impact before he can react.

pairs.name: Bloodseeker
pairs.reason: Bloodseeker's Rupture is consider a great counter since using it prevents you from running around with your Ultimate.

pairs.name: Bristleback
pairs.reason: Quill Spray can be used to kill Lycan's summons as well as Bristleback allows him to stay alive against Lycan while dishing out counter attacks.

pairs.name: Tidehunter
pairs.reason: Kraken Shell grants him massive physical attack protection and Anchor Smash will wipe the area, clearing Lycan's wolves.

pairs.name: Naga Siren
pairs.reason: Naga Siren’s illusions slow down Lycan's summons and confuse his target focus. Song of the Siren stops Lycan mid-push or teamfight initiation. She scales better into the late game and out-splits Lycan. Her tanky illusions also waste Lycan's Shapeshift duration.

pairs.name: Chen
pairs.reason: Chen can dominate creeps, weakening Lycan’s unit advantage in lane and teamfights. Holy Persuasion creeps block paths and absorb wolf damage. Chen often groups early, countering Lycan's split-push strategy.

pairs.name: Techies
pairs.reason: Techies slows down Lycan’s snowball with mine traps and area denial. Wolves trigger Proximity Mines, wasting Lycan’s resources. Blast Off silences Lycan during his Shapeshift. Lycan’s push is hard to commit to due to threat of instant burst.

pairs.name: Kunkka
pairs.reason: Kunkka's boat buff and cleave can wipe out Lycan’s summons easily. X Marks the Spot and Torrent make kiting Lycan trivial. Kunkka’s tankiness makes it hard for Lycan to burst him. His teamfight control punishes Lycan's all-in style.

pairs.name: Sven
pairs.reason: Sven has Great Cleave to instantly kill Lycan's wolves and units. He becomes immune to slows with Black King Bar, making Lycan’s chase ineffective. Sven outdamages Lycan in most engagements post-15 minutes. Storm Hammer stuns Lycan before he gets full value from Shapeshift.

pairs.name: Batrider
pairs.reason: Batrider easily kites Lycan with sticky Napalm and Flaming Lasso. Lycan’s summons don’t help against magic damage over time and repositioning. Firefly burns through creeps and wolves quickly. Once lassoed, Lycan can't deal his burst damage effectively.

pairs.name: Necrophos
pairs.reason: Necrophos punishes Lycan’s commitment with Reaper’s Scythe. Ghost Shroud makes him untargetable by Lycan’s physical damage. Lycan’s units feed Death Pulse sustain. Lycan can't burst him down before he outheals the damage.

pairs.name: Meepo
pairs.reason: Meepo’s high stat gain and clones can overwhelm Lycan faster than he can respond. He uses Poof and Earthbind to lock Lycan in place. Lycan’s summons become ineffective due to AoE nukes. In a farm race, Meepo scales faster and snowballs harder.

pairs.name: Visage
pairs.reason: Visage can easily outfight Brewmaster by leveraging his powerful familiars. The familiars add consistent damage and lockdown, making it difficult for Brewmaster to engage safely. Their burst and control can overwhelm Brewmaster before he fully commits to fights. Visage’s ability to zone and pressure with familiars gives him an advantage in sustained engagements.

pairs.name: Lycan
pairs.reason: Lycan can easily turn on Brewmaster using Shape Shift for increased movement speed and damage. He can quickly chase down and pick off Brewlings due to their low durability and slower movement. Lycan’s high mobility and burst make it hard for Brewmaster to maintain control in fights. This allows Lycan to exploit Brewmaster’s weaknesses and dominate engagements

pairs.name: Primal Beast
pairs.reason: Primal Beast can get on top of Brewmaster using Onslaught of the Beast and Pulverize to initiate aggressively. He can use Trample to quickly kill Brewmaster’s Brewlings, removing Brewmaster’s key control tools. Primal Beast’s lockdown and burst damage make him a strong counter to Brewmaster in fights

pairs.name: Marci
pairs.reason: Marci can man-fight Brewmaster effectively with her high mobility and damage. Her ultimate, Unleash, allows her to take out Brewmaster’s Brewlings quickly, reducing his control in fights. With sustained pressure and disables, Marci can force Brewmaster on the defensive. This makes Marci a strong opponent who can challenge Brewmaster’s presence in engagements.

pairs.name: Lone Druid
pairs.reason: Lone Druid can fear off Brewmaster’s Brewlings or Beastmaster with Savage Roar, disrupting their control. He can root Brewmaster or his Brewlings with Root, limiting their mobility. Being naturally tanky, Lone Druid can man-fight Brewmaster effectively in longer teamfights. His combination of control and durability makes him a strong opponent against Brewmaster’s aggression.

pairs.name: Broodmother
pairs.reason: Broodmother excels against Brewmaster by using her spiderlings to overwhelm his Brewlings and control the battlefield. Broodmother’s ability to split push and apply map pressure forces Brewmaster to respond, limiting his teamfight impact. Her mobility and sustained damage allow her to kite Brewmaster and punish him during extended fights.

pairs.name: Naga Siren
pairs.reason: Naga Siren’s Song of the Siren allows her team to set up perfectly on Brewmaster, preventing him from casting Primal Split. This disables Brewmaster’s key escape and control tool, leaving him vulnerable in fights. Her illusions add pressure and confusion, making it harder for Brewmaster to respond effectively. Naga’s control and setup potential make her a strong counter against Brewmaster’s playstyle.

pairs.name: Enigma
pairs.reason: Enigma can target Brewmaster if he becomes a potential threat, using Black Hole to eliminate him early in fights. By locking Brewmaster down, Enigma prevents him from using Primal Split and disrupting team engagements. This early control can swing fights heavily in Enigma’s team’s favor. Enigma’s crowd control makes him a strong counter to Brewmaster’s initiation and split tactics.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: Slark can dispel Brewmaster’s disables and slows with his Dark Pact, making it harder for Brewmaster to control him. He can burn Brewmaster’s mana pool using Defusal Blade, limiting Brewmaster’s ability to cast Primal Split. This pressure reduces Brewmaster’s effectiveness in fights and forces him to play more cautiously.

pairs.name: Riki
pairs.reason: A Disruption save for a teammate of SD can easily turn into set up for an enemy Riki as he can preemptively place Smoke Screen and Tricks of the Trade on top of it. Tricks of the Trade can be timed to avoid Demonic Purge's or Shadow Poison's damage.

pairs.name: Leshrac
pairs.reason: A Disruption save for a teammate of SD can easily turn into set up for an enemy Leshrac as he can preemptively cast Split Earth to time its duration. Leshrac doesn't really have buffs or passives for Demonic Purge to Dispel or Break (including his level 20 damage reduction talent) and Disruption doesn't stop him from doing damage with Diabolic Edict or Pulse Nova.

pairs.name: Meepo
pairs.reason: A Disruption save for a teammate of SD can easily turn into set up for an enemy Meepo as he can preemptively cast Earthbind or Poof to time its duration for a chain root or massive magic damage burst. Dig can be timed to avoid Demonic Purge's or Shadow Poison's damage and effects.

pairs.name: Sand King
pairs.reason: A Disruption save for a teammate of SD can easily turn into set up for an enemy Sand King as he can preemptively cast Epicenter or Burrow Strike to time its duration for an instant stun or massive magic damage. SK doesn't really have buffs or passives for Demonic Purge to Dispel or Break, appart from Caustin Finale and Disruption doesn't stop him from doing damage with Sand Storm or Epicenter.

pairs.name: Io
pairs.reason: Io functions perfectly fine under the effects of Disruption. Io can still Relocate his allies even DURING Disruption, although Disruption would interrupt Io's Relocate if used on Io himself, while channeling. Tether can keep affecting Io's allies and provide them with healing and mana even DURING Disruption. Spirits stay active and can do damage DURING Disruption. He doesn't really have any buffs or passives to be dispelled or broken with Demonic Purge.

pairs.name: Kunkka
pairs.reason: Ghost Ship mitigates Lone Druid’s burst damage, and X Mark locks down the Druid or the Bear. The cleave from Tidebringer clears the Bear and Druid if they clump, making Kunkka a consistent teamfight counter.

pairs.name: Pangolier
pairs.reason: Pango’s Rolling Thunder stuns both the Druid and Bear repeatedly, stopping them from attacking. Shield Crash reduces incoming damage, and Swashbuckle bypasses the Bear’s root. His control overwhelms Lone Druid in fights.

pairs.name: Lich
pairs.reason: Chain Frost punishes Lone Druid’s tendency to group with his Bear. Frost Shield also reduces Bear damage and slows push tempo. Lich is great at punishing melee-centric heroes with AoE.

pairs.name: Viper
pairs.reason: Viper melts the Bear quickly with Nethertoxin, removing its passive. He slows the Druid down with Poison Attack, and Viper Strike cripples any attempt to disengage. A classic lane and mid-game counter.

pairs.name: Underlord
pairs.reason: Underlord’s Pit of Malice controls both the Bear and Druid. Firestorm melts their HP pools, and Atrophy Aura cripples their damage. Lone Druid struggles to take objectives through Underlord’s wave clear.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: The Bear can’t keep up with PL illusions. Lone Druid’s kit is built around focusing a single target, so he struggles to identify and kill the real PL, especially post-Manta and Heart. PL also burns through the Bear with Diffusal Blade.

pairs.name: Jakiro
pairs.reason: Jakiro has strong push stall with Liquid Fire and Macropyre. He chips at the Bear’s HP with DoT, and Ice Path stops Bear initiations. Lone Druid’s push gets delayed significantly.

pairs.name: Monkey King
pairs.reason: Monkey King uses tree vision to avoid fights and punishes Bear initiations with Wukong’s Command. The Bear gets shredded inside the arena, and Monkey’s armor and crit scaling allow him to trade better in extended fights.

pairs.name: Dark Seer
pairs.reason: Ion Shell kills waves instantly and punishes clumping. Vacuum + Wall destroys both Druid and Bear in tight areas. The Bear clone from Wall of Replica is a dangerous threat that turns Druid’s strength against him.

pairs.name: Winter Wyvern
pairs.reason: Winter’s Curse turns Lone Druid’s Bear into a team killer. The Bear often stays near his allies, making Wyvern’s ult devastating. Her Arctic Burn and Splinter Blast also stall pushes and kite the Bear.

pairs.name: Shadow Demon
pairs.reason: SD can use Disruption on both CK and his Phantasm Illusions to create Illusions of his own that inherit Chaos Strike, while CK's own innate Reins of Chaos can be triggered by Disruption to create additional Illusions for SD. Disruption can also be used as a save to disrupt CK's Chaos Bolt/Reality Rift combo and prevent him from bursting a single target down.

pairs.name: Dark Seer
pairs.reason: Wall of Replica and Normal Punch (Aghanim's Scepter Upgrade) can create Illusions of CK that inherit Chaos Strike. CK's own innate Reins of Chaos can trigger both on Wall of Replica and Normal Punch, creating additional Illusions. Normal Punch can additionally create Illusions from ANY CK Illusions and not necessarily CK himself.

pairs.name: Tidehunter
pairs.reason: Blubber can dispel both Chaos Strike and Reality Rift, allowing Tide to counter initiate and stun CK and all of his Illusions with Ravage. Anchor Smash can mitigate most of CK's and his Illusions' damage as most of his total damage output comes from attacking. Dead in the Water (Aghanim's Shard Upgrade) prevents CK from using Reality Rift and his Illusions do reduced damage to it. Kraken Shell provides further damage mitigation against CK's attacks.

pairs.name: Medusa
pairs.reason: All of Medusa's abilities are AOE, making her very effective versus CK and his Illusions. Split Shot allows Dusa to attack CK and any of his Illusions. Reality Rift cannot be used during Gorgon's Grasp. Stone Gaze and Mystic Snake's Aghanim's Scepter upgrade allow Medusa to stun all of CK's Illusions. Mana Shield does not take into account Reality Rift's armor reduction and as much single target burst damage CK can output with his Phantasm, realistically he struggles to go trough all of Dusa's mana pool in a single Chaos Bolt - once Dusa is able to get Stone Gaze of CK is forced to retreat.

pairs.name: Axe
pairs.reason: CK's total damage output is mostly physical, trough his and his Illusions' attacks, which get greatly mitigated by Axe's infinetely scaling Armor and trigger Counter Helix. Berserker's Call can lock down both CK and his Illusions and Aghanim's Scepter can reduce CK's right-click damage significantly, which is most of his total damage output.

pairs.name: Terrorblade
pairs.reason: Due to Chaos Knight’s Reins of Chaos facet constantly summoning illusions, Terrorblade can use Reflection to spawn his own illusions of Chaos Knight. These reflected illusions hit hard and help Terrorblade dominate the lane, especially during early trades. This interaction makes it difficult for Chaos Knight to sustain or commit aggressively, giving Terrorblade a strong laning advantage.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: Phantom Lancer can dodge Chaos Knight's Chaos Bolt using Doppelganger. Doppelganger grants a brief period of invulnerability and disjoints projectiles. If timed correctly, it completely evades Chaos Bolt. It also creates illusions, making it harder for Chaos Knight to find the real PL. This makes Doppelganger a strong counterplay tool against Chaos Knight's stun

pairs.name: Naga Siren
pairs.reason: Naga's ultimate, Song of the Siren, puts all nearby enemies to sleep, allowing her to disengage from fights or set up team plays. This is particularly useful against Chaos Mirror Image creates illusions and disjoints projectiles, enabling Naga to dodge Chaos Knight's Chaos Bolt if timed correctly. Naga's illusions can match or surpass those of Chaos Knight, especially when equipped with items like Manta Style and Radiance. Her illusions benefit from Rip Tide, which reduces enemy armor and deals area damage, effectively clearing Chaos Knight's illusion, Ensnare roots Chaos Knight, preventing him from using Reality Rift to reposition or escape, giving Naga's team an advantage in engagements.

pairs.name: Warlock
pairs.reason: Warlock is strong against Chaos Knight due to his area-of-effect abilities. He can cast Fatal Bonds on Chaos Knight and his illusions, linking their damage. Follow up with Chaotic Offering to stun and damage them all at once. Upheaval slows Chaos Knight and his illusions, making escape or chasing difficult. This combo can quickly eliminate Chaos Knight’s illusions and turn teamfights.

pairs.name: Kunkka
pairs.reason: Kunkka is generally favored against Chaos Knight in fights. Torrent and Ghostship deal AoE damage, clearing Chaos Knight's illusions effectively. X Marks the Spot prevents Chaos Knight from escaping after using Reality Rift. Kunkka’s high durability and Cleave from Tidebringer punish grouped illusion

pairs.name: Timbersaw
pairs.reason: His Whirling Death and Chakram deal pure AoE damage, quickly clearing illusions. Reactive Armor gives him tankiness against Chaos Knight’s burst and right-clicks. Timber Chain allows him to escape Reality Rift and reposition easily. Chaos Knight struggles to deal sustained damage to Timbersaw due to his durability and illusion-clearing tools.

pairs.name: Sand King
pairs.reason: Sand Storm and Caustic Finale deal AoE damage, clearing illusions efficiently. Burrowstrike provides reliable stun and escape from Reality Rift. Epicenter deals massive AoE magic damage, overwhelming Chaos Knight and his illusions. Sand King's AoE burst and mobility make him a strong counter to Chaos Knight’s illusion-based playstyle.

pairs.name: Winter Wyvern
pairs.reason: Winter’s Curse can force Chaos Knight and his illusions to attack each other, often killing him. Splinter Blast hits a main target and damages nearby illusions, helping clear them. Arctic Burn slows and deals percentage-based damage, piercing Chaos Knight’s tankiness. Cold Embrace can save allies from Chaos Knight’s burst by granting strong healing and armor.

pairs.name: Brewmaster
pairs.reason: His Primal Split creates powerful elemental spirits that can disable and harass Chaos Knight and his illusions. Thunder Clap reduces enemy attack speed, limiting Chaos Knight’s damage output. Brewmaster’s tankiness and crowd control help survive Chaos Knight’s burst and control the fight. Using Storm Brewling’s Cyclone during Primal Split can lock down Chaos Knight, preventing him from using abilities.

pairs.name: Earthshaker
pairs.reason: His Fissure provides a reliable stun and terrain block, disrupting Chaos Knight’s initiation. Aftershock combos with his abilities to deal burst AoE damage, clearing illusions quickly. Echo Slam is devastating against Chaos Knight’s illusions, often turning fights decisively. Earthshaker’s crowd control and AoE damage make him a strong counter to Chaos Knight’s playstyle.

pairs.name: Underlord
pairs.reason: All of Pitlords abilities are AOE, which allow him to affect most if not all Meepos. Atrophy Aura reduces BASE attack damage and Meepo generally builds heavy stats items to empower his clones. Pit of Malice's root prevents Meepo from using Poof or Dig (Meepo's Aghanim's Shard) and does NOT get dispelled by Megameepo ( Meepo's Aghanim's Scepter). High stats means high HP and Armor, which Firestorm cares little for due to it's Magic and % Max HP damage.

pairs.name: Beastmaster
pairs.reason: Divided We Stand gives Drums of Slom multiple targets to affect and when combined with Crimson Guard usually results in Meepo struggling to output enough damage to kill Beastmaster. Wild Axes deal scaling Magic Damage on a low cooldown, which provides considarable AOE damage to help damage all of Meepos clones and Primal Roar is vital for isolating a single Meepo and focusing it down..

pairs.name: Bristleback
pairs.reason: Earthbind does not prevent Bristleback from turning around, allowing him to turn his Bristleback towards Meepo during it. Divided we Stand provides extra HERO targets for Bristleback to get additional Spell Lifesteal for full value with Quill Spray and Bristleback procs.

pairs.name: Enigma
pairs.reason: Black Hole and Midnight Pulse are capable of controlling and doing immense damage to all Meepos. Black Hole can be used on a single Meepo to prevent the rest of his clones from comming to his aid with Poof as they would also be instantly affected by it. Midnight Pulse can deal immense damage to MegaMeepo (Aghanim's Scepter upgrade) as it deals % current HP, while Black Hole can be placed on top of Dig to instantly control any Meepo that exits it.

pairs.name: Leshrac
pairs.reason: Leshrac thrives in games where he can get high uptime on his spells onto his enemies to keep healing and do massive amounts of damage. Meepo provides him with up to 4 extra immobile targets to do so, making it difficult for him to output enough damage to get trough Lesh's sustain alone.

pairs.name: Winter Wyvern
pairs.reason: Winter's Curse turns Meepo's clones against the primary target, often resulting in an easy kill. Splinter Blast deals significant AoE magic damage to all Meepos, while Cold Embrace protects allies caught by Earthbind, pontentially saving them.

pairs.name: Timbersaw
pairs.reason: Timbersaw's set of skills completely counters Treant as it destroys trees and can easily catch him in them.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: Slark's Dark Pact can easily dispel Overgrowth and Leech Seed naturally and run to safety or run in knowing he is safe.

pairs.name: Tidehunter
pairs.reason: Tidehunters Kraken Shell removes all your debuffs at a certain threshold which makes Treant less useful in the mid to late game.

pairs.name: Chen
pairs.reason: Chen floods the map with creeps, bypassing Living Armor’s value through constant pressure. He outheals or dispels Treant’s chip damage, and his Hand of God negates Leech Seed damage completely.

pairs.name: Naga Siren
pairs.reason: Naga pushes multiple lanes and illusions burn through Living Armor fast. Song of the Siren resets any Overgrowth initiation, wasting Treant's major cooldown. Treant struggles to clear illusions or find the real Naga.

pairs.name: Necrophos
pairs.reason: Treant’s high HP and sustain become liabilities versus Reaper’s Scythe. Heartstopper Aura ignores armor and whittles him down. Treant can’t burst Necro or stop him from sustaining through Leech Seed.

pairs.name: Enchantress
pairs.reason: Treant's right-clicks are almost meaningless against Untouchable. Enchantress out-sustains him and punishes melee supports with impetuous harass. Her creeps also tank through Overgrowth and pressure early towers.

pairs.name: Phoenix
pairs.reason: Phoenix’s Supernova zones Treant hard. He has low attack speed and cannot contest the egg. Fire Spirits destroy Treant’s early presence and reduce the healing potential from Living Armor and Leech Seed.

pairs.name: Doom
pairs.reason: Doom removes Treant’s entire kit with one spell. After being doomed, Treant contributes nothing to the fight. Scorched Earth also negates healing from Leech Seed and Living Armor, nullifying his sustain playstyle.

pairs.name: Dark Willow
pairs.reason: Treant’s slow movement and predictable plays are easy to punish with Brambles and Cursed Crown. Shadow Realm lets Willow avoid Overgrowth and strike back with massive damage. Treant also can't reveal her easily.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: Phantom Lancer overwhelms Ogre Magi with illusions that Ignite cannot clear quickly. Ogre Magi lacks strong Area of effect damage and becomes mana-drained in long fights. Phantom Lancer dodges stuns and resets with Doppelganger. Ogre Magi’s single-target spells are inefficient against illusion heroes.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Anti-Mage reflects Ogre Magi’s high mana pool back against him with Mana Void. He can Blink out of Ignite and Fireblast range. Ogre Magi is unable to lock Anti-Mage down long enough without teammates. Bloodlust gives little value if Anti-Mage controls the backline.

pairs.name: Enigma
pairs.reason: Ogre Magi lacks the range to interrupt Enigma’s Black Hole reliably. Ignite is not enough to force Enigma out of position. His slow mobility makes him an easy target during teamfights. Enigma can outscale Ogre Magi with better control and Area of effect presence.

pairs.name: Beastmaster
pairs.reason: Beastmaster punishes static heroes like Ogre Magi with Hawk vision and early pressure. His summons absorb Ignite and create overwhelming physical damage. Ogre Magi cannot easily escape from Roar plus summon damage. He gets zoned during lane phase and offers little in return.

pairs.name: Meepo
pairs.reason: Meepo spreads Ogre Magi’s single-target stuns thin across multiple targets. Ignite fails to deal significant Area of effect damage to his clones. Ogre Magi becomes overrun by net chains and burst nukes. Meepo farms faster and dominates Ogre Magi in early game tempo.

pairs.name: Chaos Knight
pairs.reason: Chaos Knight’s illusions are hard to distinguish and survive through Ogre Magi’s magic damage. Ogre Magi has no reliable Area of effect control to handle multiple illusions. Chaos Knight burst-kills Ogre Magi with Reality Rift and Chaos Bolt. Ogre Magi’s low mobility lets Chaos Knight isolate him easily.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: Slark can purge Ignite and Bloodlust using Dark Pact, reducing Ogre Magi’s utility. He farms stacks off Ogre Magi during extended fights. Slark’s mobility prevents him from being easily stunned. Ogre Magi’s inability to secure vision makes him vulnerable to constant ganks.

pairs.name: Shadow Demon
pairs.reason: Shadow Demon disrupts Ogre Magi or his allies, dodging Fireblast chains. His illusions benefit from Ogre Magi’s Bloodlust, working against him. He zones Ogre Magi out of fights with ranged harassment. Ogre Magi lacks the tools to burst him down reliably.

pairs.name: Warlock
pairs.reason: Warlock’s Fatal Bonds punishes Ogre Magi’s tendency to stick with his team. Chaotic Offering stuns him from a distance where Ogre Magi cannot respond. Warlock outscales Ogre Magi in teamfights with massive Area of effect impact. Ogre Magi cannot cancel Warlock’s cast animations reliably.

pairs.name: Magnus
pairs.reason: Magnus blinks past Ogre Magi to grab cores with Reverse Polarity. Ogre Magi’s stuns cannot prevent his initiation reliably. Empower buffs melee carries beyond what Ogre Magi’s Bloodlust provides. He becomes outclassed in teamfight presence as the game progresses.

pairs.name: Ursa
pairs.reason: Ursas Overpower is a great counter for killing the tombstone. Fury Swipes also counters the tanky profile Undying has.

pairs.name: Lina
pairs.reason: Lina's attack range and Fiery Soul are an incredible counter to Tombstone.

pairs.name: Snapfire
pairs.reason: Lil' Shredder destroys Tombstone quickly from a safe range. Her high magic burst punishes Undying's low mobility and poor scaling. She also zones Undying out of teamfights and punishes his early grouping.

pairs.name: Jakiro
pairs.reason: Jakiro attacks twice so he can easily destroy tombstone. Ice Path and Dual Breath interrupt Tombstone fights and slow Undying’s early aggression. His long-range spell makes Undying’s push ineffective.

pairs.name: Medusa
pairs.reason: Zombies barely affect Medusa due to her Split Shot and high effective mana pool. Stone Gaze disables Undying and forces him out of position if he commits early. She simply outscales and ignores his impact in long fights.

pairs.name: Luna
pairs.reason: Luna’s fast right-clicks and bouncing Glaives kill Tombstone instantly, even from afar. Her Eclipse punishes Undying's low magic resistance and clustered teamfights. She’s fast, farm-heavy, and doesn’t care about his decay stacking.

pairs.name: Gyrocopter
pairs.reason: Gyrocopter clears zombies with Flak Cannon, and can kill Tombstone from long range. His AoE magic damage punishes early group fights, where Undying usually shines. Once he gets BKB, Undying can't threaten him at all.

pairs.name: Meepo
pairs.reason: Meepo’s multi hits kills Tombstone and zombies instantly. He can ignore Decay due to sheer numbers and overwhelm Undying with fast tempo. Undying has no answer to Meepo’s early snowball and control.

Undying is gold-starved, and Bounty thrives by abusing him with Track for snowball gold. Bounty can kite and harass Undying, and pick off backline supports when Tombstone is down. He’s elusive and very hard for Undying to lock down.

pairs.name: Monkey King
pairs.reason: MK can easily kill Tombstone from trees or inside his ultimate. Zombies don’t stop Monkey King’s Jingu stacks or ult, and his mobility outmaneuvers Undying. In lane, MK can out-trade Decay with lifesteal and higher burst.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Fade Bolt does little damage to Anti-Mage due to Counterspell's magic resistance. Most of Rubick's spells are single targets and can be reflected by Counterspell. The only spell that provides some utility for Rubick is Blink. Blink does little on its own to counter Anti-Mage when coming from behind except allowing Rubick to escape. Rubick can easily run out of mana to cast the spell due to Mana Break, if not dying to Anti-Mage's physical damage already.

pairs.name: Night Stalker
pairs.reason: Crippling Fear silences nearby heroes and cannot be dispelled, which hinders Rubick's way to retaliate when being jumped on. With Hunter in the Night and Dark Ascension, Night Stalker can find Rubick easily in teamfights. The two spells grants more than enough damage to hunt Rubick down without defensive items.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: Pounce and Dark Pact together with some attacks can take Rubick down quickly. Rubick's spells are ineffective due to the strong dispel effect of Dark Pact. Even though Shadow Dance is a great spell to steal, Slark's untargetable nature and his low cooldown spells prevents Rubick from stealing. Also Slark can freely use other abilities for the duration of Shadow Dance.

pairs.name: Elder Titan
pairs.reason: Elder Titan’s aura makes Rubick extremely squishy. Rubick can’t steal any truly game-breaking spells from him, and Echo Stomp's setup often catches Rubick before he can respond. Titan thrives in chaotic fights where Rubick struggles to cast.

pairs.name: Tusk
pairs.reason: Tusk closes the gap quickly with Snowball and punishes Rubick’s weak mobility. He isolates Rubick with Walrus Punch and Ice Shards, removing him from the fight before he can react. Tusk is hard to steal anything impactful from.

pairs.name: Leshrac
pairs.reason: Leshrac deals constant AoE magic damage, which shreds Rubick’s low HP pool. Even with Spell Steal, Rubick doesn’t benefit much unless he gets Pulse Nova, and Lesh is hard to catch without heavy follow-up.

pairs.name: Batrider
pairs.reason: Batrider destroys Rubick with Sticky Napalm stacks and Flaming Lasso. Rubick has no way to save himself and has poor turn-rate for escape. Lasso is hard to steal without risking positioning.

pairs.name: Razor
pairs.reason: Razor's Static Link shuts Rubick down completely if latched. Rubick can’t burst or escape him, and he rarely gets to steal anything meaningful. Razor thrives in extended fights where Rubick struggles to contribute.

pairs.name: Pangolier
pairs.reason: Pangolier's Rolling Thunder ruins Rubick’s ability to channel or position properly. Even if Rubick steals Shield Crash or Swashbuckle, it’s hard to get value without being interrupted by the rolling stun.

pairs.name: Phantom Assassin
pairs.reason: Rubick’s low armor and HP make him food for Coup de Grace. He can’t control PA alone, and she shrugs off most of his disables. PA also often builds BKB, making Rubick useless against her mid-to-late game.

pairs.name: Sniper
pairs.reason: Sniper’s long attack range and stationary fighting style make him difficult for Disruptor to deal with directly. Disruptor’s spells have limited reach, and without proper vision or initiation, it’s hard to catch Sniper before he deals significant damage.

pairs.name: Drow Ranger
pairs.reason: Drow Ranger’s long-range damage and high mobility with Gust and Multishot make her a tough target for Disruptor. Without reliable gap closers or vision, it can be difficult to pin her down with your spells before she deals heavy damage.

pairs.name: Clinkz
pairs.reason: Clinkz’s high burst damage and invisibility allow him to ambush and instantly kill Disruptor if caught out of position. Without detection or strong team coordination, it’s challenging to lock him down before he eliminates you.

pairs.name: Legion Commander
pairs.reason: Legion Commander’s strong initiation and Duel ability pose a serious threat to Disruptor. Since Duel forces Disruptor to attack, his innate passive won’t help him escape, making it crucial to avoid getting caught or rely on teammates for saves.

pairs.name: Lifestealer
pairs.reason: Lifestealer’s Rage makes him immune to Glimpse and Kinetic Field, and it also allows him to ignore Static Storm if timed correctly. To counter Lifestealer effectively, you need to catch him off-guard before Rage activates or coordinate with your team to lock him down once it fades—which is not always easy to do.

pairs.name: Juggernaut
pairs.reason: Juggernaut’s Blade Fury grants Debuff Immunity, allowing him to ignore Kinetic Field, Glimpse, and Static Storm while active — making it easy for him to close the gap and secure kills. However, if you manage to initiate with Static Storm before he activates Blade Fury, you can potentially burst him down before he has a chance to use his abilities

pairs.name: Meepo
pairs.reason: Nyx is ineffective against multiple Meepo clones due to poor AoE. Meepo punishes Nyx’s low durability when caught. Mana Burn and Vendetta lose value against multiple targets. Nyx struggles to disable all clones in a fight.

pairs.name: Grimstroke
pairs.reason: Grimstroke’s Ink Swell makes it dangerous for Nyx to initiate. Soulbind prevents Nyx from using Vendetta escape. Nyx cannot easily reflect or disable Grimstroke’s spells. Grim punishes Nyx in teamfights and offers better lockdown.

pairs.name: Beastmaster
pairs.reason: Beastmaster controls the map well, reducing Nyx’s ganking potential. Nyx can’t solo-kill Beastmaster easily due to aura and summon tanking. His physical damage overwhelms Nyx in fights.

pairs.name: Slardar
pairs.reason: Slardar's Corrosive Haze reveals Nyx during invisibility. He outpaces Nyx with strong physical damage and mobility. Slardar punishes Nyx’s fragile build with quick bursts. Nyx has no escape once spotted under vision.

pairs.name: Disruptor
pairs.reason: Disruptor shuts down Nyx with Glimpse and Static Storm. Nyx can’t escape or gank safely once revealed. Carapace is ineffective against kinetic field setups. Disruptor nullifies Nyx’s map presence and forces passive play.

pairs.name: Lifestealer
pairs.reason: Lifestealer shrugs off Nyx’s disables with Rage. Mana Burn and Impale don’t affect him during spell immunity. Nyx cannot burst or kite Lifestealer reliably. Nyx offers little control against Lifestealer’s brawling style.

pairs.name: Dragon Knight
pairs.reason: Dragon Knight is too tanky for Nyx to burst with spells. His magic resistance and regen make Mana Burn negligible. Nyx struggles to slow DK’s push and sustain. Vendetta has little value against his natural tankiness.

pairs.name: Viper
pairs.reason: Viper’s magic resistance and range punish Nyx’s approach. Nethertoxin disables Nyx’s passive stun utility. Nyx is forced out of fights by poison damage. He can’t reliably trade or harass Viper in lane or skirmishes.

pairs.name: Bane
pairs.reason: Bane has strong single-target lockdown to counter Nyx. Fiend’s Grip disables him through Vendetta. Bane’s sustain tools allow him to survive burst. Nyx is punished for overcommitting in fights.

pairs.name: Ogre Magi
pairs.reason: Ogre is too tanky and buys detection for Vendetta. He punishes Nyx with Fireblast chains and harassment. Nyx struggles to make him a priority target.

pairs.name: Techies
pairs.reason: Techies' immense AOE capabilities do wonders against Mirror Image, as Techies can clear them with Sticky Bomb, Blast Off! and Proximity Mines - hindering one of Naga's core gameplay advantages of splitpushing with Illusions. Reactive Tazer can disarm Naga and all of her Illusions.

pairs.name: Underlord
pairs.reason: Atrophy Aura reduces BASE attack damage and Naga being an Illusion hero greatly benefits from stacking Agility and increasing her base damage and Attack Speed to empowers her Illusions. Agility stacking means high armor so both Firestorm and Pit of Malice are great at providing reliable Magic damage and Crowd Control for Mirror Image due to their AOE properties.

pairs.name: Leshrac
pairs.reason: Leshrac's abundance of AOE damage can easily clear Naga's Mirror Image Illusions troughout the entirety of the game, which is her core farming and fighting tool. Being an Illusion, melee hero she struggles to stay on Leshrac to damage him as she prefers Heart over Satanic for sustain.

pairs.name: Axe
pairs.reason: Naga being an Agility Illusion hero means she dishes out a large number of attacks with lower,relative to other heroes, damage per hit. This means Axe can proc Counter Helix like crazy to clear Mirror Image Illusions, as the Pure damage bypasses her high armor. Berserker's Call is able to control Naga and her Illusions simultaneously.

pairs.name: Earthshaker
pairs.reason: Mirror Image provides extra targets for Echo Slam to build up echo damage, while Fissure and Aftershock provide consistent AOE control and damage to help deal with any Illusions and mitigate Naga's constant split pushing. Fissure in particular is effective at blocking off lanes and paths making it difficult for Mirror Image Illusions to function.

pairs.name: Necrophos
pairs.reason: Necro's abundance of AOE damage can easily clear Naga's Mirror Image Illusions troughout the entirety of the game, which is her core farming and fighting tool. Being an Illusion, melee hero she struggles to stay on Necro to damage him as she prefers Heart over Satanic for sustain.

pairs.name: Nyx Assassin
pairs.reason: Nyx thrives against KotL’s high manapool and low HP. Mana Burn deals huge damage due to KotL’s intelligence scaling. He easily catches KotL while he channels Illuminate or Recall with Vendetta and Carapace.

pairs.name: Slardar
pairs.reason: Slardar’s high mobility and Corrosive Haze quickly delete squishy backliners like KotL. He can blink-stun KotL before he reacts with Will-o-Wisp or Blinding Light. KotL has no hard disable to stop Slardar’s initiation.

pairs.name: Weaver
pairs.reason: Weaver ignores Will-o-Wisp with Shukuchi and Time Lapse. He can chase and kill KotL with Geminate Attack while remaining hard to catch. KotL's low armor and HP are vulnerable to Weaver’s sustained poke.

pairs.name: Mirana
pairs.reason: Moonlight Shadow helps gank or disengage from KotL’s channeled spells. Arrow punishes long Illuminate channels. High mobility lets her avoid Will-o-Wisp and Blinding Light easily.

pairs.name: Sand King
pairs.reason: KotL is vulnerable to surprise Burrowstrike into Epicenter. Sand King often sits in fog or burrows in, making KotL’s recall risky. He punishes KotL’s squishy positioning and long cast times

pairs.name: Chaos Knight
pairs.reason: Chaos Bolt and Phantasm burst down KotL before he casts anything. KotL has no AoE lockdown to control the illusions. Will-o-Wisp is slow and unreliable against CK’s fast, chaotic fighting style.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: KotL’s large mana pool makes him a prime Mana Void target. Blink lets AM close the gap and kill him easily. KotL has no reliable way to stop AM’s split-push or farm pace.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: KotL struggles with PL’s illusions — his spells don’t clear them effectively. Once PL closes the gap, KotL dies quickly with little peel. He can also dodge Illuminate and Will-o-Wisp effects with Doppelganger.

pairs.name: Earth Spirit
pairs.reason: Earth Spirit can silence and burst KotL before he casts spells. His mobility lets him roll in and out past Will-o-Wisp. KotL’s channeling is disrupted by Earth Spirit’s AoE control.

pairs.name: Ancient Apparition
pairs.reason: Io's entire kit is tailored towards healing, with his Tether, Overcharge and even Relocate that can be used to go back to the fountain for regen - Ice Blast shuts all of that down entirely. Since Io tends to stay close to his Tethered ally it makes it easy for Ice Blast to connect with multiple targets.

pairs.name: Underlord
pairs.reason: Underlord punishes clumped heroes with Pit of Malice and Firestorm, making Io’s tether risky. Io’s low HP pool gets shredded by magic AoE damage. Fiend’s Gate negates Io’s Relocate advantage for map control. Underlord’s teamfight presence counters Io’s healing tempo.

pairs.name: Troll Warlord
pairs.reason: Troll Warlord ignores Io’s saves due to Battle Trance and high attack speed. Io struggles to kite or disable him, and Overcharge isn’t enough to reduce his damage output. Troll excels in sustained fights where Io usually thrives. Relocate offers limited counterplay once Troll locks on.

pairs.name: Kunkka
pairs.reason: Kunkka’s AoE spells disrupt Io’s positioning and punish close tethering. X Mark ruins Relocate attempts by pulling allies back into danger. Boat's damage reduction counters Io’s burst healing. Io gets overwhelmed in teamfights when Kunkka controls space.

pairs.name: Lina
pairs.reason: Lina bursts Io instantly with her combo, making it hard for him to channel or save. Her range punishes any aggressive Relocate attempts. Io’s partner is usually squishy, and Lina can kill them even through healing. She forces Io to play passively and defensively.

pairs.name: Monkey King
pairs.reason: Monkey King punishes grouped heroes with Wukong’s Command, forcing Io to disengage. His high mobility allows him to follow Relocate attempts. Io can’t sustain allies inside Monkey’s arena without being at risk himself. Monkey thrives when Io tries to group and sustain.

pairs.name: Magnus
pairs.reason: Magnus’s Reverse Polarity hits both Io and his tethered partner, punishing close positioning. Empowered cores outscale Io’s healing advantage. Skewer displaces Io from his partner, making saves difficult. Io struggles to recover fights once Magnus initiates.

pairs.name: Lone Druid
pairs.reason: Lone Druid’s high physical burst from Spirit Bear overwhelms Io’s healing. The Bear can interrupt Io’s channeling and tank Relocate’s repositioning. Io gets zoned out of fights with Savage Roar and pressure. He can’t stop the push tempo or single-target kill pressure.

pairs.name: Winter Wyvern
pairs.reason: Winter Wyvern’s Winter’s Curse punishes Io’s close tethering by turning his own ally against him. Splinter Blast and Arctic Burn ignore Io’s healing advantages. Her defensive toolkit is stronger than Io’s saves in late fights. She scales better into long engagements.

pairs.name: Crystal Maiden
pairs.reason: Crystal Maiden roots Io and interrupts his channeling with Frostbite. Her AoE slow punishes clumped Relocate plays. Freezing Field zones Io out of teamfights entirely. Io can’t stop her disables or scale to keep up with her control.

pairs.name: Winter Wyvern
pairs.reason: Since the Familiars are always around Visage, catching him in a Winters Curse and potentially kill him.

pairs.name: Luna
pairs.reason: Moon Glaives is very effective against Visage because not only it can easily destroy Visage's Familiars, but can also remove one instance of Gravekeeper's Cloak upon each hit to Visage, leaving him susceptible to damage. Once Visage's Familiars are picked off and all instances of Gravekeeper's Cloak are removed, Luna will be able to easily kill Visage with Eclipse.

pairs.name: Tidehunter
pairs.reason: Visage's Familiars cannot penetrate Kraken Shell and will do almost no damage to Tidehunter. Anchor Smash's bonus damage has the potential to kill Familiars or reduce their damage.

pairs.name: Naga Siren
pairs.reason: Visage is bad against Naga Siren because her illusions overwhelm Visage and make it hard for him to identify and focus the real target. Her Song of the Siren resets fights and completely wastes Visage’s burst timing with Familiars. Naga’s illusions soak up Soul Assumption charges, denying burst potential. Over time, her Radiance and Diffusal Blade combo also burns Visage’s mana and weakens his survivability.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: Visage is bad against Phantom Lancer because the massive number of illusions confuse Visage’s auto-targeting from Familiars and force Soul Assumption onto the wrong units. Phantom Lancer is hard to catch due to Doppelganger and high agility scaling, while Visage lacks reliable area-of-effect damage to clear illusions. Once Phantom Lancer builds Manta Style and Heart, he becomes unkillable for Visage. The birds also lose effectiveness against dispersed illusions.

pairs.name: Lycan
pairs.reason: Visage struggles against Lycan because Lycan and his units can quickly focus and destroy Visage’s Familiars, reducing his teamfight impact. Lycan’s summons do not trigger Soul Assumption effectively due to their spread-out damage. Visage has no hard disable to stop Lycan from diving supports or taking objectives with his army. Lycan's physical burst overwhelms Visage before he can reposition or summon defensive Gravekeeper’s Cloak stacks.

pairs.name: Bristleback
pairs.reason: Visage is weak against Bristleback since Bristleback has high sustain and armor, which reduces Visage’s physical damage from Familiars and auto-attacks. Soul Assumption is not reliable because Bristleback doesn’t take burst damage, only slow chip damage. Visage cannot burst Bristleback down even with full charges, and his constant Quill Spray spam can shred Visage’s Familiars and Gravekeeper’s Cloak layers. Bristleback also builds tanky items that ignore Visage's output.

pairs.name: Void Spirit
pairs.reason: Visage is bad against Void Spirit because Void Spirit is highly mobile and can easily dodge Soul Assumption projectiles and Familiars. His Aether Remnant and Dissimilate allow him to quickly reposition and burst down Visage before he can react. Visage’s slow movement and cast animations make him a prime target for Void Spirit’s high tempo and magic burst. In addition, Void Spirit’s silence or control prevents Visage from responding.

pairs.name: Crystal Maiden
pairs.reason: Visage is bad against Crystal Maiden because she can easily freeze Visage or his Familiars with Frostbite, completely halting their impact. Her Freezing Field deals high AoE magic damage that melts Visage’s cloak layers and Familiars. Crystal Maiden also provides sustain to her team through Arcane Aura, helping allies deal with Visage’s mana-intensive pokes. Her crowd control punishes Visage’s lack of mobility.

pairs.name: Kunkka
pairs.reason: Visage is bad against Kunkka because Kunkka’s high AoE damage from Tidebringer and spells like Boat and Torrent disrupt Visage’s positioning and quickly remove Gravekeeper’s Cloak layers. X Mark the Spot ensures Visage cannot flee, and Ghost Ship gives the enemy team damage mitigation during Visage’s burst window. His Familiars are easily killed by Tidebringer cleave. Kunkka's tanky build also shrugs off Visage's limited magic burst.

pairs.name: Necrophos
pairs.reason: Death Pulse, Hearthstopper Aura and Death Seeker (Aghanim's Shard Upgrade) can affect Slark during Shadow Dance and Depth Shroud (Aghanim's Shard Upgrade), which are his main defensive tools. Dark Pact does not dispel Reaper's Scythe and Ghost Shroud prevents Slark from attacking Necro and gaining Essence Shift stacks.

pairs.name: Bloodseeker
pairs.reason: Rupture damages Slark during Pounce and makes it more difficult for him to play in and out of fights as eventually Thirst will reveal him and prevent him from healing with Barracuda. Blood Rite and Blood Mist (Aghanim's Scepter upg) can damage Slark during Shadow Dance and Depth Shroud due to it's AOE property.

pairs.name: Earthshaker
pairs.reason: Despite Dark Pact being able to dispell both Aftershock and Fissure's stuns the sheer amount of constant AOE control that Earthshaker provides simply overwhelms Slark as they are able to affect him during Shadow Dance and Depth Shroud.

pairs.name: Enigma
pairs.reason: Both Black Hole and Midnight Pulse can affect Slark despite his heavy defensive kit. Dark Pact does not dispel either, while Shadow Dance and Depth Shroud (Aghanim's Shard upgrade) do not prevent their effects due to them being AOE, giving Enigma a reliable way of locking down Slark . Black Hole can suck Slark back in as he Pounces and Midnight Pulse can destroy a large are of trees preventing him from hiding to heal up with Barracuda.

pairs.name: Leshrac
pairs.reason: Leshrac's abundance of AOE damage allows him to damage Slark during his core defensive mechanims - Shadow Dance and Depth Shroud. Slark's low Strength gain makes him an easy target for Lesh in the early and mid game, before Slark farms up some tanky items and often finds himself run down by Lesh.

pairs.name: Night Stalker
pairs.reason: Crippling Fear cares little about Dark Pact as it does not get dispelled by it - this prevents Slark from getting of his highest impact spells, which are also his main survivability tools: Shadow Dance and Depth Shroud (Aghanim's Shard upgrade); as well as limiting his mobility due to him not being able to cast Pounce and get away. Dark Ascension's unobstructed vision makes it a nightmare for Slark to disengage a fight and hide somewhere in order to heal up with Barracuda.

pairs.name: Grimstroke
pairs.reason: Soulbind prevents Slark from using Pounce and Shadow Dance to escape. Ink Swell disables Slark mid-fight and forces poor engagements. Grimstroke’s combo with stun partners locks Slark down long enough to kill. Slark can’t purge the Soulbind debuff with Dark Pact.

pairs.name: Disruptor
pairs.reason: Disruptor’s Glimpse pulls Slark back after escapes and cancels Shadow Dance healing. Static Storm prevents him from using spells during teamfights. Kinetic Field keeps him locked in place for coordinated burst. Disruptor counters Slark’s hit-and-run playstyle completely.

pairs.name: Leshrac
pairs.reason: Leshrac’s AoE damage bypasses Slark’s regen and punishes his low HP pool. Split Earth and Edict zone him out from fights and objectives. Slark can’t sustain through magic burst without BKB. Leshrac dominates in fights Slark wants to extend.

pairs.name: Omniknight
pairs.reason: Guardian Angel nullifies Slark’s physical damage entirely. He protects Slark’s targets, especially cores, from getting bursted. Slark is forced to disengage or waste key spells on supports.

pairs.name: Elder Titan
pairs.reason: Elder Titan reduces Slark’s base armor with Natural Order, exposing his fragility. Echo Stomp locks him down and prevents Shadow Dance. Astral Spirit reveals Slark even in fog or invis. Titan’s area control counters Slark’s sneaky mobility.

pairs.name: Riki
pairs.reason: Riki silences Slark with Smoke Screen and wins in mirror invis fights. Tricks of the Trade avoids most of Slark’s damage attempts. Riki punishes Slark during pounce cooldowns. His early burst control shuts down Slark before scaling.

pairs.name: Mars
pairs.reason: Mars pins Slark with Spear of Mars to cancel mobility spells. Arena of Blood traps him and blocks Pounce paths. Mars builds early armor and disables that make Slark ineffective. Slark struggles to fight when confined or kited out.

pairs.name: Alchemist
pairs.reason: Simply put by the time Medusa is ready to fight Alchemist is ready to end the game. Her inability to pressure early or scale quickly when paired against Alch's farming potential often result's in games where she has half an inventory versus a maxed out Alch. Chemical Rage and Berserk Potion dispel Gorgon's Grasp.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Mana Break is amazing at shredding trough Medusa's mana pool and turning her core defensive mechanic Mana Shield against her with a huge Mana Void follow up . Manta is a staple item for AM that provides him with dispel for Gorgon's Grasp root and Counter Spell can block/reflect Mystic Snake.

pairs.name: Dark Seer
pairs.reason: Wall of Replica and Normal Punch (Aghanim's Scepter Upgrade) can create multiple Illusions of Medusa to do devastating amounts of damage to her own team as she tends to build heavy stat items to improve her own Manta Illusions' damage and durability. The Illusions DS creates inherit both Mana Shield and Split Shot if it was active at the moment of creating the Illusion. Surge is amazing at disengaging from Stone Gaze or closing the gap on Dusa.

pairs.name: Nyx Assassin
pairs.reason: Nyx burns Medusa’s mana with Mana Burn and stuns her with Spiked Carapace off Split Shot. Vendetta bursts her before she can react. She triggers his spells unintentionally with constant attacks. Nyx repeatedly harasses and disables her during crucial fights.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: Slark dodges Split Shot and Stone Gaze with Shadow Dance and pounces out of danger. He builds up Essence Shift during drawn-out fights. Medusa can’t hit him reliably in fog or darkness. She struggles to lock him down or match his agility scaling.

pairs.name: Centaur Warrunner
pairs.reason: Centaur absorbs her attacks with Retaliate and initiates with Hoof Stomp. Stampede helps his team disengage from Stone Gaze. Medusa’s slow mobility becomes a liability against his high-tempo play. He survives her damage and enables his allies to burst her.

pairs.name: Alchemist
pairs.reason: Alchemist farms much faster than Medusa and applies pressure earlier. His BKB timing allows him to ignore Stone Gaze. Acid Spray and Unstable Concoction burst Medusa before she’s fully online. He snowballs into late game with more map control.

pairs.name: Pangolier
pairs.reason: Pangolier’s Rolling Thunder disables Medusa during her Stone Gaze and ruins positioning. Diffusal Blade drains her mana quickly and forces retreat. His mobility allows him to avoid Split Shot and kite her. Pango controls teamfights where she needs to stand ground.

pairs.name: Monkey King
pairs.reason: Monkey King builds Diffusal Blade and stays in Wukong’s Command to drain Medusa’s mana. She can’t escape the arena without items like Force Staff. His high physical DPS overwhelms her early before she scales. He jumps on top of her and avoids most of her damage.

pairs.name: Shadow Demon
pairs.reason: Shadow Demon disrupts Medusa during her Stone Gaze and makes illusions of her. These illusions deal high damage and drain her mana with Split Shot. Disruption saves allies from Life Drain and Mystic Snake. He stalls fights long enough to counter her momentum.

pairs.name: Sniper
pairs.reason: Sniper outranges Medusa and chips her down safely from distance. She struggles to reach him through his mobility and slows. Sniper doesn’t rely on mana, so Stone Gaze has minimal impact. He scales better with attack range and pure damage items.

pairs.name: Razor
pairs.reason: Static Link can drain most or all of Troll Warlord's damage, making him useless in a teamfight or unable to last hit in lane. This is especially effective during Battle Trance, because Troll has no option to cancel the link. Storm Surge allows Razor to chase after or run away from Troll Warlord while doing damage with Eye of the Storm.

pairs.name: Sniper
pairs.reason: Shrapnel and Headshot allows Sniper to kite Troll Warlord effectively. Having natural big attack range together with increased attack range from Hurricane Pike allow Sniper to sit and fire at Troll Warlord from a safe distance.

pairs.name: Winter Wyvern
pairs.reason: Cold Embrace can protect Troll Warlord's target, especially during Battle Trance. Winter's Curse can turn Troll Warlord's high physical damage and attack speed against his allies.

pairs.name: Axe
pairs.reason: Troll Warlord is bad against Axe because Axe's Berserker's Call forces Troll Warlord to attack him during his ultimate, which allows Axe to lock him down and kill him easily with Blade Mail and Culling Blade.
