Troll Warlord's reliance on right-clicking makes him vulnerable to the counterattack mechanic of Axe, especially during the laning and early mid-game phase. Troll Warlord cannot out-sustain the pure disable and burst Axe brings with his spell combo.

pairs.name: Naga Siren
pairs.reason: Troll Warlord struggles against Naga Siren because her illusions overwhelm him and make it difficult to focus the real hero during fights. Ensnare prevents Troll Warlord from repositioning or escaping, especially when he’s channeling Battle Trance. Naga Siren's Song of the Siren can reset fights or waste Troll Warlord’s ultimate duration. The illusion spam and evasion from Manta Style or Butterfly also weaken Troll Warlord’s impact in late-game duels.

pairs.name: Muerta
pairs.reason: Troll Warlord is bad against Muerta because when she activates Pierce the Veil, she becomes immune to physical damage, which completely nullifies Troll Warlord’s right-click-focused kit. His ultimate Battle Trance cannot affect Muerta during this time, making her a direct counter in one-on-one scenarios. Muerta can kite Troll Warlord using her ranged advantage and crowd control like The Calling. She also scales better in ranged matchups while Troll Warlord relies heavily on gap closing.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: Troll Warlord suffers against Slark because Slark can dispel Troll’s root from Whirling Axes with Dark Pact and disengage easily with Pounce. Slark becomes stronger during prolonged fights thanks to Essence Shift, which works against Troll Warlord's extended engagement style. Slark also builds items like Black King Bar and Skadi, which mitigate Troll’s burst and regen. In late fights, Slark can dodge Battle Trance and reset using Shadow Dance, making Troll Warlord ineffective.

pairs.name: Ancient Apparition
pairs.reason: Troll Warlord is weak versus Ancient Apparition due to Ice Blast completely countering his sustain during Battle Trance. Troll Warlord relies on life steal to stay alive when low HP, and Ancient Apparition’s ultimate prevents healing, making him an easy target when low. In addition, Cold Feet and Chilling Touch slow his mobility and attack effectiveness. Ancient Apparition stays far behind in fights, making it hard for Troll Warlord to punish him directly.

pairs.name: Bane
pairs.reason: Troll Warlord is countered by Bane because Bane has multiple strong disables including Nightmare and Fiend’s Grip that bypass Black King Bar and stop Troll Warlord during Battle Trance. Enfeeble reduces his damage and lifesteal, directly weakening his power in duels and skirmishes. Bane’s toolkit allows him to peel for his teammates or lock Troll down in critical moments. He can also stay out of Troll’s attack range while controlling him from afar.

pairs.name: Underlord
pairs.reason: Troll Warlord is bad against Clinkz because Clinkz has high burst damage and mobility, allowing him to kill Troll before he can use Battle Trance. Clinkz’s Skeleton Walk helps him kite or escape Troll’s chase, while Burning Barrage pierces through Troll’s defenses. Clinkz usually hits a strong mid-game timing before Troll Warlord is online, punishing him while he’s still farming. Troll Warlord also lacks reliable detection or lockdown to control Clinkz.

pairs.name: Lifestealer
pairs.reason: Rage/Unfettered can be used to soak/dispel Hoof Stomp and Double Edge. Aghanim Scepter allows LS to Infest any retreating with Stampede targets and stay on top of them. His abudance of sustain trough Feast, which scales with Rawhide and Open Wounds can easily result in a situation where LS completely outheals Centaur's Retaliate and total damage output.

pairs.name: Wraith King
pairs.reason: Reincarnation makes it difficult to all in WK with Stampede as he'd have an extra life to spare. Wraithfire Blast can lock down any retreating with Stampede targets so WK can stay on top of them. His abudance of sustain trough Vampiric Spirit can easily result in a situation where WK completely outheals Centaur's Retaliate and total damage output.

pairs.name: Juggernaut
pairs.reason: Blade Fury can be used to greatly mitigate the damage and Crowd Control of Hoof Stomp and Double Edge. Omnislash and Swiftslash (Aghanim's Scepter upgrade) allows Juggernaut to stay on top of any retreating with Stampede targets. His abudance of sustain trough Healing Ward and his Blade Dance Lifesteal talent can easily result in a situation where Juggernaut completely outheals Centaur's Retaliate and total damage output.

pairs.name: Ember Spirit
pairs.reason: Hoof stop has a relatively long cast point and can be dodged with both Sleight of Fist and dashing to a Remnant. Ember's biggest asset however is that he can root multiple targets with Searing Chains during Stampede for almost the entirety of it's duration.

pairs.name: Tidehunter
pairs.reason: Blubber provides a dispel for Hoof Stomp's stun, Double Edge's slow (Aghanim's Shard Upgrade) and Stampede's slow. Dead in the Water (Aghanim's Shard upgrade) leashes enemies and slows them even during Stampede. Ravage can obviously completely ruin a Stampede initiation or disengage.

pairs.name: Ursa
pairs.reason: Ursas Fury Swipes are a nuisance in all stages of the game to Centaur. In addition, in mid to late game Ursas shard and Aghanims upgrade are an incredible counter to the initiation of Centaur.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: Slark can easily kite Centaur Warrunner with his mobility. If Slark builds Diffusal Blade, he can burn Centaur’s mana, preventing key spells like Hoof Stomp or Stampede. Centaur struggles to lock Slark down due to his Dark Pact and Pounce. Slark can disengage and re-engage at will, avoiding return damage. With enough Essence Shift stacks, Slark can finish Centaur off in extended fights.

pairs.name: Ember Spirit
pairs.reason: Ember Spirit avoids Reverse Polarity with Sleight of Fist and Remnant mobility. Magnus struggles to lock him down consistently without help. Ember also clears waves and keeps pressure across the map, outpacing Magnus. Empower becomes less effective if Ember controls tempo.

pairs.name: Puck
pairs.reason: Puck dodges Reverse polarity with Phase Shift and cancels Blink Dagger with constant poke. Magnus’s combo is unreliable against Puck’s elusive nature. Dream Coil counters Magnus’s mobility by punishing Skewer plays. Puck dominates long fights where Magnus can’t connect clean spells.

pairs.name: Faceless Void
pairs.reason: Faceless Void’s Chronosphere counters Magnus’s teamfight initiation. Magnus cannot use Reverse polarity or Skewer while frozen in Chrono. Void also avoids Skewer with Time Walk. Empowered carries can’t deal damage if stuck in Chronosphere.

pairs.name: Huskar
pairs.reason: Huskar jumps into Magnus before he can initiate and punishes him with Burning Spears. Magnus doesn’t have enough burst to bring down Huskar through magic resistance. Reverse polarity is less impactful against tanky frontline heroes like him. Huskar plays faster than Magnus prefers.

pairs.name: Bane
pairs.reason: Bane disables Magnus through reverse polarity with Fiend’s Grip from long range. His brain sap trades well in lane and ruins Magnus’s early farm. Nightmare interrupts Blink Dagger setups. Bane excels at picking off Empowered cores before they can use their buffs.

pairs.name: Kez
pairs.reason: Kez keeps Magnus from finding clean reverse polarity by breaking his positioning with disruptive spells. His tempo makes it hard for Magnus to reach late-game timing. Skewer is punished and turned into over-commitments. Magnus’s spells lose value when forced to fight early

pairs.name: Earthshaker
pairs.reason: Earthshaker counters reverse polarity with his own initiation and long-range stuns. Fissure and Echo Slam interrupt Magnus's combos and punish grouped teamplay. Both heroes want to initiate but Earthshaker can do it more reliably from distance. Magnus is forced into poor initiations.

pairs.name: Tidehunter
pairs.reason: Tidehunter shrugs off Shockwave and Reverse polarity with Kraken Shell. Ravage counters Magnus’s initiation by stunning his whole team. Magnus struggles to displace Tide from the frontlines with Skewer. Tide dominates big 5v5 fights Magnus relies on.

pairs.name: Visage
pairs.reason: Visage’s familiars interrupt Magnus’s Blink Dagger, preventing clean initiation. Gravekeeper’s Cloak reduces cleave burst from Empowered allies. Reverse Polarity has low value against spread-out familiars and tanky cores. Visage outpressures Magnus in laning and early objectives.

pairs.name: Enigma
pairs.reason: Enigma turns Magnus’s grouped playstyle against him with Black Hole. Reverse polarity has similar cooldown and purpose, so Enigma can counter-initiate directly. Magnus has no way to stop BKB Black Hole without allies. Enigma scales harder in pure teamfight presence.

pairs.name: Batrider
pairs.reason: Batrider sticks Napalm stacks and forces Timbersaw to waste mobility early. Lasso pulls him out of Timber Chain path and into danger. Timbersaw can’t cleanse the debuff and melts under Firefly. Batrider snowballs easily if he wins the lane.

pairs.name: Bloodseeker
pairs.reason: Rupture prevents Timbersaw from using Timber Chain, his main escape. Bloodseeker capitalizes on Timbersaw’s frequent movement with huge burst. Thirst keeps him visioned and makes juking impossible. In most cases, Bloodseeker forces Timbersaw to play passively.

pairs.name: Faceless Void
pairs.reason: Chronosphere traps Timbersaw before he can react with Timber Chain. Timbersaw cannot save allies or himself inside the sphere. Faceless Void's physical burst bypasses his reactive armor. He’s especially vulnerable if caught without mana or Chain cooldown.

pairs.name: Pugna
pairs.reason: Pugna’s Nether Ward punishes Timbersaw’s high spell frequency. Decrepify interrupts Chakram burst and saves teammates. Life Drain cuts through Timbersaw’s defenses and regrowth. Pugna makes Timbersaw’s damage and durability unreliable in teamfights.

pairs.name: Grimstroke
pairs.reason: Soulbind prevents double Timber Chains or escaping with mobility. Ink Swell stuns him if he stays in close quarters. Grimstroke punishes Timbersaw’s grouped aggression. His combo disables even tanky targets long enough for allies to finish them off.

pairs.name: Silencer
pairs.reason: Silencer shuts Timbersaw down completely with Global Silence. Without spells, Timbersaw becomes useless and easy to burst. Arcane Curse punishes him for frequent spell usage. Timbersaw cannot purge or dispel the silences effectively.

pairs.name: Templar Assassin
pairs.reason: Timbersaw's early harass gets blocked by Refraction. TA bursts Timbersaw down before he can build defensive items. His lack of burst damage allows TA to melt supports uncontested. He struggles to reach her once she gets mobility items.

pairs.name: Leshrac
pairs.reason: Leshrac deals heavy magical damage that outpaces Timbersaw’s regen. Timbersaw’s armor and health pool don’t help much against Pulse Nova. Leshrac pushes towers faster than Timbersaw can stall. He outpaces him in both tempo and impact.

pairs.name: Ursa
pairs.reason: Ursa shreds through Timbersaw’s reactive stacks with Fury Swipes. His quick burst damage finishes Timbersaw before he can regen. Ursa closes the gap with Earthshock and ignores chain mobility. Timbersaw can’t survive extended duels.

pairs.name: Outworld Devourer
pairs.reason: Astral Imprisonment disrupts Timber Chain escapes and combos. Arcane Orb deals pure damage and pierces through armor stacking. Sanity’s Eclipse bursts Timbersaw due to his small mana pool. OD scales faster and counters him throughout the game.

pairs.name: Viper
pairs.reason: Viper Strike is a reliable low cooldown ability that Breaks the Damage Reduction and Quill Spray procs of Bristleback as well as the further acquiring of stacks from Warpath for it's duration - this completely cripples Bristleback and creates a window of opportunity to outright kill him.

pairs.name: Ancient Apparition
pairs.reason: Ice Blast prevents Bristleback from healing with Bloodstone or any other sources of sustain, making it difficult for him to play fights in a manner which he wants to - by trading his HP in order to get Bristleback procs and do damage in order to heal back up and keep repeating the cycle.

pairs.name: Legion Commander
pairs.reason: Duel forces Bristleback to face LC, preventing him from taking advantage of his Bristleback Damage Reduction and Quill Spray procs for it's duration providing LC's team with a window of opportunity to outright kill him even without Break or Healing reduction.

pairs.name: Axe
pairs.reason: Berserker's Call forces Bristleback to face Axe, preventing him from taking advantage of his Bristleback Damage Reduction and Quill Spray procs for it's duration providing Axe's team with a window of opportunity to outright kill him even without Break or Healing reduction.

pairs.name: Primal Beast
pairs.reason: Uproar when upgraded by Aghanim's Scepter provides a consistent Break for Bristleback's Damage Reduction and Quill Spray procs as well as any further acquiring of stacks from Warpath for it's duration - this completely cripples Bristleback and creates a window of opportunity to outright kill him.

pairs.name: Phantom Assassin
pairs.reason: Phantom Assassin can buy shard and break Bristlebacks Passive abilities and kill him.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: Slark can effectively kite and fight Bristleback, gaining Essence Shift stacks over time. He can purchase items like Diffusal Blade to drain mana and slow Bristleback, and Silver Edge to break his passive Bristleback, making him much easier to kill. Slark’s mobility and scaling damage allow him to outlast Bristleback in extended fights. This makes Slark a strong counter, especially in the mid to late game.

pairs.name: Hoodwink
pairs.reason: Hoodwink can counter Bristleback effectively with her Sharpshooter, which applies a break and heavy slow, disabling his Bristleback passive. Bushwhack allows her to lock him down near trees, setting up high-damage combos. She can also use Scurry to escape into the trees, avoiding Bristleback’s quill spray and staying safe during chases. Her mobility and break mechanic make her a strong ranged threat against Bristleback.

pairs.name: Venomancer
pairs.reason: Bristleback relies on movement to close the gap on enemies, using Viscous Nasal Goo to slow targets, but he lacks a reliable stun. Venomancer can easily kite Bristleback with Venomous Gale and Poison Sting, applying constant slows and damage over time. His Poison Nova prevents Bristleback from regenerating health effectively during fights

pairs.name: Tinker
pairs.reason: Tinker can spam March of the Machines to safely deal damage When using the Facet: Repair Bots, March of the Machines also heals allies in its path, helping sustain the team during prolonged fights. Tinker’s ability to refresh spells with Rearm and reposition using Blink Dagger makes it difficult for Bristleback to reach or outlast him. With consistent damage and team utility, Tinker becomes a strong counter to Bristleback in both lane and teamfights.

pairs.name: Queen of Pain
pairs.reason: Blink allows Queen of Pain to escape from an incoming Snowball and Ice Shards.

pairs.name: Earthshaker
pairs.reason: Echo Slam is good against Snowball since it bunches everyone up. This can set up some prime opportunities for Blink Echo Slams.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Mana Break is very effective against Tusk, as he has a very low mana pool. Blink allows Anti-Mage to escape from an incoming Snowball.

Timbersaw’s physical damage resistance significantly reduces the effectiveness of Tusk’s Tag Team and Walrus Punch. Additionally, by lowering Strength with Whirling Death, Timbersaw can make even tanky heroes like Tusk vulnerable to his high pure damage output

Underlord’s tankiness makes him hard to bring down, even with Tusk’s full combo. Pit of Malice counters Tusk effectively by rooting him and disabling Snowball, leaving him vulnerable to follow-up damage

Dawnbreaker can counter Tusk’s initiation by using Starbreaker to fight back and Celestial Hammer to escape Ice Shards. Solar Guardian offers strong defensive utility, saving allies or herself and turning engagements in her team’s favor

pairs.name: Visage
pairs.reason: Familiars interrupt Skywrath’s positioning and can cancel channeling supports nearby. Visage’s cloak resists burst, and Skywrath has no way to clear summons effectively. He gets punished hard in extended fights.

pairs.name: Chen
pairs.reason: Chen’s creeps tank Mystic Flare and break combo setups. He provides sustain and healing that negates Skywrath’s quick burst style. Skywrath can’t pick off targets easily through Hand of God and creeps.

pairs.name: Lycan
pairs.reason: Lycan’s high movement speed and summons overwhelm Skywrath. He runs Skywrath down with ease, and Skywrath’s spells don’t stop Lycan’s push. Once Lycan builds BKB, Skywrath is a non-threat.

pairs.name: Lone Druid
pairs.reason: The Spirit Bear tanks Mystic Flare and disables Skywrath with entangle. Skywrath has no control over the bear or its durability. The Druid himself can kill Sky quickly with ranged damage or Blink Bear rushes.

pairs.name: Wraith King
pairs.reason: Skywrath wastes a full combo on Wraith King’s first life. With BKB and reincarnation, Wraith King ignores Skywrath’s control completely. He closes the gap and punishes squishy supports easily.

Oracle nullifies Skywrath’s entire playstyle. False Promise prevents death from Mystic Flare, and Fate’s Edict gives magic immunity to allies. He hard-counters burst-heavy magic dealers like Skywrath.

pairs.name: Medusa
pairs.reason: Medusa’s mana shield absorbs Skywrath’s magical damage, and she survives long enough to outscale him. His burst becomes less useful as her tankiness increases. Mystic Flare is almost completely negated.

pairs.name: Templar Assassin
pairs.reason: TA’s Refraction absorbs all of Skywrath’s magic poke. She can kill him in a couple of hits with Blink + Meld before he gets a second spell off. His damage is wasted on her shield unless perfectly timed.

pairs.name: Meepo
pairs.reason: Meepo punishes low-mobility supports like Skywrath with net and poof combo. His clones spread out and take less damage from single-target spells. Skywrath has no AoE or way to keep Meepos off him.

pairs.name: Tiny
pairs.reason: Tiny shrugs off Skywrath’s damage once he gets items. He jumps in with Blink + Toss combo and deletes Skywrath instantly. Skywrath’s lack of control makes him easy prey for Tiny’s burst and mobility.

pairs.name: Ancient Apparition
pairs.reason: Ancient Apparition's Ice Blast completely nullifies Mist Coil and Borrowed Time as Abaddon cannot heal himself or his allies who are affected by the spell.

pairs.name: Axe
pairs.reason: Axe's Culling Blade can kill Abaddon during Borrowed Time if his HP falls below the threshold of the spell. Aphotic Shield also doesn't dispel Berserker's Call. However, it does help absorb some of the damage dealt by Axe and his team.

pairs.name: Brewmaster
pairs.reason: Brewmaster's Storm Brewling can Tornado Abaddon during Borrowed Time to keep him in place and waste his ultimate duration. The Storm Brewling can also dispel Abaddon's Aphotic Shield and take it off instantly.

pairs.name: Disruptor
pairs.reason: Disruptor can keep Abaddon inside Kinetic Field to prevent him from running at heroes or escaping during Borrowed Time. Disruptor's Glimpse also cannot be dispelled by Aphotic Shield and repositions Abaddon back into the enemy team if he managed to create some distance during Borrowed Time.

pairs.name: Doom
pairs.reason: Doom's Doom spell completely nullifies Mist Coil and Borrowed Time as Abaddon cannot heal himself or his allies who are affected by the ultimate.

pairs.name: Lycan
pairs.reason: Lycan's pack of Wolves make it difficult for Abaddon to fight or absorb damage for his cores in the laning stage. Beyond that, Abaddon also cannot stop Lycan from taking towers as he cannot stand and absorb the high damage coming from Lycan and his units.

pairs.name: Outworld Devourer
pairs.reason: Outworld Devourer's Astral Imprisonment wastes a lot of the Borrowed Time duration and cannot be dispelled with Aphotic Shield. Outworld Devourer also has the potential to burst down Abaddon with Sanity's Eclipse without letting Borrowed Time trigger, even if it is off cooldown.

pairs.name: Phantom Assassin
pairs.reason: Phantom Assassin's high physical damage is a bad matchup for Abaddon because of his low armor. Later in the game, Phantom Assassin gets Aghanim's Shard and can Break Abaddon using Fan of Knives, which makes Abaddon trigger Borrowed Time manually.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: Abaddon doesn't have much AoE damage to threaten Phantom Lancer while he has a lot of illusions around him. Once Phantom Lancer gets Diffusal Blade, it's very easy for him to burn Abaddon's mana with illusions and render him useless.

pairs.name: Razor
pairs.reason: Razor's Static Link cannot be dispelled by Aphotic Shield, and lets Razor rack up massive damage from Abaddon or his allies. Razor also does a ton of physical damage during Eye of the Storm, which is a bad matchup for Abaddon because of his low armor.

pairs.name: Shadow Demon
pairs.reason: Shadow Demon's Demonic Purge and Shadow Poison cannot be dispelled by Aphotic Shield, which are his biggest damage spells. Demonic Purge also dispels Aphotic Shield, and when upgraded with Aghanim's Scepter, also Breaks Abaddon and makes him trigger Borrowed Time manually. Disruption also lets Shadow Demon waste a lot of the Borrowed Time duration.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: Slark does not care much about Borrowed Time and keeps hitting Abaddon to rack up Essence Shift stacks. Since Abaddon gets healed up during Borrowed Time, it gives Slark an even bigger HP pool to keep attacking and build up his agility and other stats.

pairs.name: Timbersaw
pairs.reason: Timbersaw can easily trigger Borrowed Time very quickly by doing massive burst damage to Abaddon with his spells. Once the ultimate ends, Timbersaw can just as easily kill Abaddon with another round of spells.

pairs.name: Viper
pairs.reason: Viper's Poison Attack has no cooldown, and he can easily reapply the stacks dispelled by Abaddon's Aphotic Shield. Viper's Viper Strike also Breaks Abaddon and makes him trigger Borrowed Time manually. This interaction coupled with a Silence from Orchid or another hero can cause massive issues for Abaddon.

pairs.name: Puck
pairs.reason: Puck is very elusive and difficult to control with Echo Stomp. Landing Earth Splitter is nearly impossible unless Puck is already disabled before the cast

pairs.name: Vengeful Spirit
pairs.reason: Vengeful Spirit can save allies caught in Echo Stomp and Earth Splitter with Nether Swap. Magic Missile provides strong early control on Elder Titan, preventing him from chasing with Astral Spirit’s buff. Additionally, she can cancel the channel of Echo Stomp, making her a solid counter to Elder Titan.

pairs.name: Ursa
pairs.reason: Ursa can trade effectively with Elder Titan early in lane due to Fury Swipes, and has the potential to chase and kill him. Enrage grants significant status resistance and damage reduction, enabling Ursa to either escape Echo Stomp and Earth Splitter combos or mitigate much of their damage

pairs.name: Shadow Demon
pairs.reason: Shadow Demon can use Disruption to save allies caught by Elder Titan’s Echo Stomp. His Shadow Poison effectively harasses and kills Elder Titan in lane, as Elder Titan struggles to hit Shadow Demon—who can safely halt his aggression while stacking more poison thanks to Disruption

pairs.name: Shadow Shaman
pairs.reason: Shadow Shaman can harass Elder Titan in lane with his spells and keep him controlled for a long time using Shackles or Hex, preventing him from landing hits and dealing damage even with the Astral Spirit buff. These disables can also interrupt the channel of Echo Stomp.

pairs.name: Enchantress
pairs.reason: Enchantress can harass Elder Titan in lane with Impetus. Additionally, Enchant provides her a dispel against Astral Spirit’s buff, completely negating Elder Titan’s bonus damage and further countering him

pairs.name: Lycan
pairs.reason: Lycan’s high mobility and summon pressure ignore Elder Titan’s AoE control. His units dodge Echo Stomp easily and force Titan into poor positioning. Natural Order has little effect on his summons. Titan gets overrun before he can charge up damage.

pairs.name: Naga Siren
pairs.reason: Naga Siren’s illusions are too numerous for Elder Titan to focus effectively. Song of the Siren resets after Earth Splitter setups, wasting his combo. Her illusions waste Astral Spirit hits, limiting his damage output. Titan’s abilities are inefficient against illusion-heavy heroes.

pairs.name: Hoodwink
pairs.reason: Dark Seer forces Elder Titan to fight in clustered zones where Vacuum into Wall destroys him. Illusions benefit from his own aura and Spirit damage. Titan’s stomp is often interrupted by Vacuum and Ion Shell poke. He can’t zone Dark Seer’s team effectively.

pairs.name: Troll Warlord
pairs.reason: Troll Warlord wins prolonged fights, which Elder Titan prefers, but outperforms him in that context. Battle Trance prevents Troll from dying to Earth Splitter. Titan has no hard disables to stop Troll from sustaining. Troll out-scales Titan in most scenarios.

pairs.name: Dazzle
pairs.reason: Shallow Grave prevents Legion Commander from killing her opponents in Duels. Shadow Wave will heal an ally caught in a Duel, as well as dealing damage to Legion Commander.

pairs.name: Outworld Devourer
pairs.reason: Astral Imprisonment prevents Legion Commander from killing her opponents in Duels.

pairs.name: Pugna
pairs.reason: Decrepify on either hero stops Legion Commander from completing a Duel, and dissuades her from initiating Duels on ethereal allies. Life Drain can help Pugna's teammates win a fight, either by killing Legion Commander or replenishing her target's health.

pairs.name: Winter Wyvern
pairs.reason: Winter Wyvern is one of the hardest counters to Legion Commander. Cold Embrace completely mitigates LC’s physical damage and can save allies during Duel. In addition, Winter’s Curse can be cast on LC mid-Duel, stopping her attacks and potentially turning the fight against her.

pairs.name: Shadow Demon
pairs.reason: Shadow Demon’s Disruption can save allies caught in Duel, preventing Legion Commander from securing bonus damage. His ultimate, Demonic Purge, removes buffs from Overwhelming Odds and Press the Attack, leaving LC vulnerable and easier to kill.

pairs.name: Dawnbreaker
pairs.reason: Dawnbreaker can often survive Duel when played as a core, thanks to her tankiness and healing during the fight. As a support, she can heal allies during Duel with Solar Guardian, frequently saving them from being finished off.

Oracle’s ultimate, False Promise, prevents Legion Commander from winning Duel and gaining bonus damage. Fate’s Edict can disarm LC during Duel if she lacks debuff immunity, while Fortune’s End can dispel buffs from Overwhelming Odds and Press the Attack, further weakening her.

pairs.name: Wraith King
pairs.reason: Legion Commander often struggles to kill Wraith King during Duel due to his lifesteal, crits, and high tankiness. Even if the duel succeeds, Wraith King’s Reincarnation brings him back to life, making him a difficult and risky target for LC to lock down.

pairs.name: Abaddon
pairs.reason: Abaddon's Aphotic Shield protects him and his allies by absorbing most of Techies' burst damage through his spell combo to prevent him from getting kills. Abaddon can also pop Borrowed Time, even during the Blast Off! stun, and run into Proximity Mines to not only waste them, but also heal himself back to full. The Aphotic Shield dispel also takes off the Reactive Tazer disarm, letting Abaddon destroy Proximity Mines and run at Techies with his right clicks.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Anti Mage's high magic resistance through Counterspell lets him tank and survive Techies' spell combo, and possibly Blink away before all his Proximity Mines explode to avoid getting bursted. Anti Mage can also Blink on Techies and burn his mana through Mana Break on right clicks, making him completely useless. Once Anti Mage buys Manta Style, he can dispel the Reactive Tazer disarm and easily burst down Techies with Mana Void after jumping him with Blink.

pairs.name: Ember Spirit
pairs.reason: Ember Spirit can easily dodge Techies' Blast Off! and Sticky Bomb by timing his Sleight of Fist on a bunch of units. Ember Spirit can also throw Fire Remnants and jump to them during Sleight of Fist to avoid exploding Proximity Mines around him. Flame Guard also provides a magic damage barrier to absorb a lot of Techies' damage from his spells. Ember Spirit can also deal damage from range with his Sleight of Fist into Searing Chains combo to avoid running into Proximity Mines.

pairs.name: Juggernaut
pairs.reason: Juggernaut's Blade Fury provides massive magic resistance during the spin to mitigate most of Techies' high damage from Sticky Bomb, Blast Off!, and Proximity Mines. The Blade Fury debuff immunity also avoids the Blast Off! stun, while the dispel takes off the Reactive Tazer disarm. Juggernaut can also Omnislash and Swiftslash Techies during his Blast Off! jump to turn the fight. Healing Ward is also great at healing up Juggernaut and his entire team to counteract Techies' heavy AoE damage.

pairs.name: Lifestealer
pairs.reason: Lifestealer's Rage provides massive magic resistance during the spell to mitigate most of Techies' high damage from Sticky Bomb, Blast Off!, and Proximity Mines. The Rage debuff immunity also avoids the Blast Off! stun, while the dispel takes off the Reactive Tazer disarm. Rage is particularly effective at soaking multiple Proximity Mines while taking very little damage.

pairs.name: Mars
pairs.reason: Mars can easily time either Spear of Mars or God's Rebuke to push Techies away during his Blast Off! jump to interrupt the spell while also putting it on cooldown. This prevents Techies from ever initiating properly and putting Proximity Mines around Mars while he has his spells available. A squishy Techies can also not jump outside Arena of Blood with Blast Off! and dies easily to Mars' spells and right clicks inside it.

pairs.name: Medusa
pairs.reason: Mana Shield is simply too effective against the burst combo of Techies throughout the game. Mana Shield does not take Armor or Magic Resistance into account, thus ignoring the magic resistance reduction from Proximity Mines. Gorgon's Grasp also prevents Techies from using Blast Off! by rooting Techies in place and canceling the cast point of his spell.

pairs.name: Oracle
pairs.reason: Fate's Edict allows Oracle and his allies to ignore most of Techies' kit altogether as it can mitigate all the damage of Sticky Bomb, Blast Off!, and Proximity Mines. Fortune's End can dispel Reactive Tazer both defensively and offensively, while False Promise is an all purpose fail safe that prevents Techies from bursting anyone on Oracle's team.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: Phantom Lancer can easily time Doppelganger to dodge Sticky Bomb and Blast Off! while summoning illusions around him to tank the follow up Proximity Mines and run away with the main hero. Throughout the game, Phantom Lancer has multiple illusions at his disposal to send out and tank any Proximity Mines placed by Techies in fights or around objectives. Once Phantom Lancer buys Diffusal Blade, he can burn Techies' mana with his illusions and make him completely useless.

pairs.name: Wraith King
pairs.reason: Reincarnation makes it hard for Techies to all in combo and kill Wraith King as he would Reincarnate back to life, while Techies would be out of gas. The Bone Guard Skeletons can also soak multiple Proximity Mines in fights, or when they run down lanes or through the jungle.

pairs.name: Oracle
pairs.reason: Fortune's End can dispel Flame Guard and Searing Chains, while being able to connect with Ember DURING Sleight of Fist and Activate Remnant, rooting him for the remainder of the duration as soon as he reaches his final destination. Purifying Flames is a low cooldown, high damage nuke that can make quick work of Flame Guard. Fate's Edict both mitigates the entirety of Ember's Magic Damage, as well as prevent him from attacking even during Sleight of Fist.

pairs.name: Night Stalker
pairs.reason: Crippling Fear makes it a nightmare for Ember to juke around with Fire Remnants and Sleights of Fist as Nightstalker can camp either his Sleight of Fist or Fire Remnant locations with Crippling Fear pre-activated. Dark Ascension providing flying movement and unobstructed vision further complicates Ember's core gameplay as he struggles to hide out of sight or behind impassable terrain.

pairs.name: Huskar
pairs.reason: Huskar DESTROYS Ember in lane and completely shuts down his early game as he deals too much damage and has too much sustain for Ember to deal with. Ember's best bet is to try and get as much resources as possible from the lane and leave as the matchup only gets worse for him troughout the entirety of the laning stage.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: Slark's Dark Pact dispels Searing Chains. Pounce provides strong lockdown for Ember, which can be further upgraded with Aghanim's Scepter to extend it's duration. Slark's best defensive mechanics are Shadow Dance and Depth Shroud, which prevent Ember from applying Searing Chains or connecting with Sleight of Fist, while giving him enough sustain to survive trough Flame Guard and Fire Remnants.

pairs.name: Lone Druid
pairs.reason: Lone Druid DESTROYS Ember in lane and completely shuts down his early game as he deals too much damage and has too much sustain for Ember to deal with. Ember's best bet is to try and get as much resources as possible from the lane and leave as the matchup only gets worse for him troughout the entirety of the laning stage. His Entangling Claws render Ember unable to use both his Sleight of Fist and Activate Fire Remnant.

pairs.name: Meepo
pairs.reason: As Meepo gets his first Meepo clone the laning stage pretty much ends for Ember as it becomes a 2 on 1 situation. As the game goes on Meepo can provide a reliable chain root for Ember in order to lock him down. His general item selection of heavy stats items end up overwhelming Ember as he often struggles to output enough damage to ever kill Meepo by himself.

pairs.name: Shadow Fiend
pairs.reason: A good Shadow Fiend can completely destroy Ember in lane, just like most other melee hroes. He is a natural Eul'builder in order to set up his ult, which dispels Ember's Flameguard. Even if Shadow Fiend manages too miss one too many Shadow Razes and not completely boot Ember out of lane he can still push out the wave in just a second and roam, leaving Ember to defend his tower.

pairs.name: Legion Commander
pairs.reason: Legion's Duel provides a long lockdown for Ember and the longer the game goes the less probable it becomes for Ember to survive it, irrelevant of his itemization. LC's Press the Attack is able to dispel Searing Chains and a single Overwhelming Odds in the midst of battle is usually enough damage to break Ember's Flame Guard.

pairs.name: Monkey King
pairs.reason: Monkey King can sustain in lane against Ember Spirit, disrupting his early game and preventing him from farming freely. This pressure delays Ember’s core items and slows his transition into the mid and late game. Keeping Ember under farmed reduces his overall impact in teamfights.

pairs.name: Tinker
pairs.reason: Tinker can heal his team with Healing Bots, making Ember Spirit’s chip damage largely ineffective. This reduces Ember's impact in fights, especially during early skirmishes.

pairs.name: Bane
pairs.reason: Bane’s kit allows him to completely disable Ember Spirit in team fights with single-target lockdown. Abilities like Fiend’s Grip and Nightmare can interrupt Ember’s mobility and burst him down. This makes it difficult for Ember to weave in and out of fights effectively.

pairs.name: Bane
pairs.reason: Earth Spirit struggles versus Bane because Bane’s Fiend’s Grip can disable him for a long duration, preventing Earth Spirit from using his spells or escaping. Bane’s strong single-target lockdown and nightmare control limit Earth Spirit’s ability to initiate or counterinitiate effectively. This makes it dangerous for Earth Spirit to enter fights without backup.

pairs.name: Lycan
pairs.reason: Against Lycan, Earth Spirit finds it difficult to deal with Lycan’s strong pushing power and summoned units, which can overwhelm his abilities. Lycan’s high physical damage and mobility let him chase Earth Spirit down, making it risky for Earth to engage. Additionally, Lycan’s ultimate boosts his survivability and damage, reducing Earth Spirit’s impact in fights.

pairs.name: Dazzle
pairs.reason: Earth Spirit struggles against Dazzle because Dazzle’s Shallow Grave can save allies from his burst damage and stuns, making it harder for Earth Spirit to secure kills. Dazzle’s strong healing and armor reduction also help his team survive Earth Spirit’s damage and control, prolonging fights.

pairs.name: Marci
pairs.reason: Earth Spirit is bad against Marci because her high mobility and disables make it hard for him to lock her down. Marci can quickly dodge his skillshots and punish him during his cooldowns. Her sustain and crowd control disrupt Earth Spirit’s initiation and burst damage.

pairs.name: Enigma
pairs.reason: Against Enigma, Earth Spirit struggles because Enigma’s Black Hole disables multiple heroes, making it difficult for Earth Spirit to act or escape during fights. Enigma’s ability to summon Eidolons also creates distractions and forces Earth Spirit to split his attention, reducing his effectiveness.

pairs.name: Huskar
pairs.reason: Earth Spirit is weak versus Huskar because Huskar’s life-steal and magic resistance let him survive Earth Spirit’s burst damage. Huskar can aggressively fight Earth Spirit, especially at low health, forcing him to play cautiously. His Burning Spear damage and sustain make it tough for Earth Spirit to secure kills early.

pairs.name: Grimstroke
pairs.reason: Earth Spirit struggles against Grimstroke because Grimstroke’s Ink Swell provides strong crowd control and damage, making it risky for Earth Spirit to initiate. Grimstroke’s Stroke of Fate can poke and harass from a distance, limiting Earth Spirit’s ability to engage safely. Additionally, Grimstroke’s Soulbind amplifies disables on multiple targets, increasing the threat Earth Spirit poses.

pairs.name: Lifestealer
pairs.reason: Against Lifestealer, Earth Spirit has a hard time dealing with Lifestealer’s high durability and Rage ability, which grants magic immunity during fights. Lifestealer can easily shrug off Earth Spirit’s disables and punish him with strong melee damage. The close-range nature of Lifestealer forces Earth Spirit to be cautious about when and how to engage.

pairs.name: Elder Titan
pairs.reason: Earth Spirit is weak versus Elder Titan because his Spirit and natural tankiness absorb much of Earth Spirit’s burst damage. Elder Titan’s Earth Splitter ultimate creates zone control that limits Earth Spirit’s movement and initiation options. The Astral Spirit can also scout and harass Earth Spirit, making it harder for him to find openings.

pairs.name: Rubick
pairs.reason: Spell Steal turns all of Underlord's spells against his own team and even further empowers their already amazing values. The % Max HP damage from Firestorm scales with Arcane Supremacy's Spell Amlification resulting in devastating damage troughout the entirety of the game.

pairs.name: Ursa
pairs.reason: Ursa is both a hard lane and game matchup for Underlord as Fury Swipes' stacking damage does not get mitigated by Atrophy Aura. Enrage dispels both Pit of Malice and Firestorm and Earthshock can still be used during Pit of Malice, given it does not make Ursa leap forward.

pairs.name: Lifestealer
pairs.reason: Lifestealer has multiple ways of dispelling both Pit of Malice and Firestorm trough Rage/Unfettered and Infest. Infest can be used during Pit of Malice's root and Rage negates Atrophy Aura's damage reduction for it's duration. Being a tank shredder Lifestealer naturally matches up well versus Underlord as he has ample sustain trough Open Wounds, Infest and Feast.

pairs.name: Juggernaut
pairs.reason: Blade Fury can dispel both Pit of Malice and Firestorm. Healing Ward provides Jugg and his team with AOE healing to counteract Underlords AOE damage. Omnislash and Swiftslash (Jugg's Aghanim's Scepter) can be used during Pit of Malice's root and dispel him, while not being affected by Atrophy Aura for their duration.

pairs.name: Huskar
pairs.reason: Berserker's Blood provides Huskar with Magic Resistance to mitigate the damage from Firestorm and ample sustain to counteract it's DOT effect. Life Break can be used during Pit of Malice to dispel the root and leave it's AOE altogether.

pairs.name: Dark Seer
pairs.reason: Wall of Replica and Normal Punch (Aghanim's Scepter Upgrade) can create multiple Illusions of TB to do devastating amounts of damage to his own team as he tends to build heavy stat items to improve his own Mirror Image Illusions' damage and durability. The Illusions DS creates inherit Metamorphosis if it was active at the moment of creating the Illusion. In lane, TB struggles versus Ion Shell as he is a low HP but high Armor melee hero, that lacks wave clear. Surge is amazing at both disengaging and closing the gap on TB as Conjure Image's slow does not work during it.

pairs.name: Axe
pairs.reason: Axe is the hardest counter to TB. He clears illusions with Battle Hunger and Counter Helix, locks TB with Berserker’s Call, and bursts him down before Sunder with Culling Blade. His toolkit punishes illusion-based heroes hard.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: PL overwhelms TB with illusions. TB can't tell the real PL apart, and Reflection isn’t useful against illusions. PL also has natural Diffusal Blade to burn TB’s mana, making Sunder risky or impossible to use.

pairs.name: Tinker
pairs.reason: Tinker spams lasers to wipe illusions from afar. TB can’t reach or pressure him easily without support, and Laser's Blind heavily cripples TB’s right-click DPS. Tinker thrives against illusion carries like TB.

pairs.name: Winter Wyvern
pairs.reason: Winter’s Curse can turn TB’s illusions against him, dealing massive damage to his teammates. She stalls pushes with Splinter Blast and zones TB out with Arctic Burn. Wyvern punishes TB's clumping and illusions.

pairs.name: Keeper of the Light
pairs.reason: Keeper's Illuminate clears illusions from distance, and Blinding Light makes TB miss attacks during Metamorphosis. His high mobility and sustain keep teammates safe while TB struggles to lock anyone down.

pairs.name: Brewmaster
pairs.reason: Primal Split removes TB from the fight temporarily with Cyclone. Brew’s split units also ignore TB’s illusions and can delay long enough to waste Metamorphosis duration. TB can't manfight the brewlings effectively.

pairs.name: Lich
pairs.reason: Chain Frost shreds TB and his illusions during pushes or teamfights. Frost Shield slows TB and blocks a chunk of right-click damage. TB’s low early mobility and grouping style make him very vulnerable to Lich’s kit.

pairs.name: Puck
pairs.reason: Puck kites TB endlessly. Waning Rift silences him to prevent Sunder, and Dream Coil punishes his movement. TB has no way to reliably hit or lock down Puck, making her an annoying lane and fight threat.

pairs.name: Warlock
pairs.reason: Chaotic Offering drops through BKB and stuns TB mid-Sunder. Fatal Bonds punishes TB’s illusions by spreading damage. Warlock’s sustain and teamfight scaling delay TB’s timing and let his team punish TB’s grouping.

pairs.name: Alchemist
pairs.reason: Alch has the lowest Basic Attack Speed in the game by far during Chemical Rage, which allows him to dispatch of Phoenix's Supernova quickly. Phoenix uses Fire Spirits and Icarus Dive to reduce his opponents' Attack and Movement Speed in order to protect the egg, however Alch has not 1 but 2 dispels for it in Chemical Rage and Berserk Potion.

pairs.name: Bloodseeker
pairs.reason: Phoenix is heavily punished by Rupture when trying to use Icarus Dive. Bloodseeker’s speed allows him to kill Supernova quickly. He thrives in chaos, countering Phoenix’s slow and controlled fight style. Blood Rite zones Phoenix out of teamfights and ruins Dive escape paths.

pairs.name: Lina
pairs.reason: Lina’s long-range burst deletes Phoenix before he can get Supernova off. Phoenix’s low armor makes him vulnerable to right-clicks. She can stay outside of Fire Spirits range and still threaten kills. Lina outscales Phoenix in both damage and utility in late-game.

pairs.name: Skywrath Mage
pairs.reason: Skywrath Mage silences Phoenix instantly, preventing all of his mobility and heals. His magical burst is too fast for Phoenix to respond with Supernova. Phoenix’s large body makes him an easy Mystic Flare target. Skywrath Mage zones Phoenix out of teamfights early and mid-game.

pairs.name: Oracle
pairs.reason: Oracle’s False Promise completely nullifies Sun Ray’s damage over time. Phoenix cannot burn through Oracle’s saves fast enough. Fortune’s End and Purifying Flames disrupt Phoenix’s healing rhythm. Supernova is easily disengaged by Oracle’s defensive toolkit.

pairs.name: Shadow Demon
pairs.reason: Shadow Demon purges Fire Spirits and cancels Phoenix’s debuff advantage. His Disruption saves allies from Supernova burn zone. Illusions from Disruption benefit from Phoenix’s Bloodlust if misused. Shadow Demon wins vision control and zone fights, where Phoenix normally excels.

pairs.name: Juggernaut
pairs.reason: Juggernaut can Blade Fury during Supernova, freely attacking the egg. He is magic-immune during his spin, avoiding Fire Spirits and Sun Ray. Juggernaut can also Omnislash Phoenix during low mobility phases. He punishes Phoenix during healing and Dive animations.

pairs.name: Huskar
pairs.reason: Huskar’s magic resistance from Berserker’s Blood makes him hard to damage with Fire Spirits. Life Break allows him to quickly close the gap onto Phoenix. Phoenix struggles to escape without being punished. Sun Ray cannot keep up with Huskar’s sustain and burst simultaneously.

pairs.name: Legion Commander
pairs.reason: Phoenix is a prime Duel target, especially when casting Supernova. Legion Commander can easily burst Phoenix before he flies away. Fire Spirits cannot reduce Duel duration or stop her BKB engagements. Phoenix has no control to stop Duel attempts.

pairs.name: Visage
pairs.reason: Visage and his Familiars can break Supernova eggs quickly due to their attack frequency. Phoenix’s spells are too slow to catch Visage off guard. Soul Assumption punishes Phoenix’s long cast times. Visage controls tempo better in midgame teamfights.

pairs.name: Lifestealer
pairs.reason: Lifestealer’s Rage gives him magic immunity during Supernova attempts. He can solo the egg with fast attacks and BKB immunity. Phoenix cannot stop Lifestealer’s infest bombs or healing reduction. Phoenix becomes food if caught near Lifestealer without support.

pairs.name: Shadow Demon
pairs.reason: Demonic Purge dispels Fate's Edict Magic Resistance and Purifying Flame's heal buff, while Demonic Cleanse (Aghanim's Shard Upgade) dispels both Fortune's End's root and Fate's Edict Disarm. Shadow Poison cannot be dispelled by Fortune's End. Disruption can prevent Fortune's End from connecting to it's target and dispelling and vital buffs or debuffs from it.

pairs.name: Lone Druid
pairs.reason: LD can pick up an Aghanim's Shard and when combined with his level 15 talent for Savage Roar can have a low cooldown dispel for both Fate's Edict's disarm and Fortune's End's root for both LD and the Spirit Bear, that almost matches Fate's Edict cooldown. This makes it hard for Oracle to stop LD and Spirit Bear to run rampart.

pairs.name: Undying
pairs.reason: Decay partially works trough both False Promise and Fate's Edict's Magic Resistance as it keeps reducing Strength and the target's current HP. The only thing that Fortune's End can dispel are Flesh Golem's Plague and Tombstone's Deathlust Slow, which can be easily re-applied. Oracle does not contribute in any meaningful way towards Tombstone's destruction.

pairs.name: Outworld Devourer
pairs.reason: Arcane Orb does Pure damage and is OD's main damage source, which does not get mitigated by Fate's Edict's Magic Resistance. Astral Imprisonment can be used to dodge Fortune's End and perserve any vital buffs or debuffs on the target.

pairs.name: Razor
pairs.reason: Static Link keeps draining damage even if Razor is disarmed by Fate's Edict and the stolen damage cannot be dispelled with Fortune's End. All of Oracle's basic abilities trigger Storm Surge if they target Razor. Eye of the Storm's damage is physical and cannot be mitigated by Fate's Edict, while it's armor reducing debuff cannot be dispelled by Fortune's End.

pairs.name: Visage
pairs.reason: Visage’s Familiars interrupt Oracle’s channeling and apply constant pressure. Oracle struggles to clear them, and his spells don’t stop Visage’s tanky frontline presence. Oracle also dies quickly to focused physical burst.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Anti-Mage punishes Oracle’s heavy mana reliance. Mana Void deletes him mid-cast, and Oracle has no mobility to escape once Blink is on top of him. Fate’s Edict also becomes a liability due to Oracle’s need for spellcasting.

pairs.name: Io
pairs.reason: Io’s sustain, mobility, and Relocate allow his team to outscale Oracle’s defensive plays. Oracle can’t stop a save-relocate or punish Io’s constant tethered healing. In late game, Io simply outperforms Oracle in utility.

pairs.name: Monkey King
pairs.reason: Monkey King dominates Oracle with fast jumps and teamfight zoning from Wukong’s Command. Oracle has a hard time positioning safely, and False Promise can’t stop Monkey from deleting a target inside the circle.

pairs.name: Pangolier
pairs.reason: Pangolier’s mobility and spell immunity during Rolling Thunder make it hard for Oracle to counter him. He can’t reliably purge or disable Pango mid-roll, and Oracle is often an easy bounce target in the backline.

pairs.name: Tinker
pairs.reason: Tinker's Defense Matrix gives him Status Resistance and to all his teammates, which will have your Winters Curse effectiveness lowered. It is also exceptionally hard for you to catch Tinker.

pairs.name: Bounty Hunter
pairs.reason: Bounty Hunters playstyle usually relies on lurking and scouting. This will cost you a lot of gold in buying detection and as well as being tracked will reveal your position.

pairs.name: Pugna
pairs.reason: Pugna's Nether Ward punishes Winter Wyvern for casting spells by dealing damage, making her abilities costly to use. Additionally, Decrepify can save the target of Winter's Curse by making them immune to physical damage

pairs.name: Outworld Devourer
pairs.reason: Outworld Devourer can counter Winter’s Curse by using Astral Imprisonment to save allies. His magical damage also bypasses Cold Embrace, making Wyvern’s primary save much less effective

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Anti-Mage is a strong counter to Winter Wyvern due to his high magic resistance and spell reflection from Counterspell. His mobility with Blink and Manta Style makes it hard for Wyvern to escape or react defensively before being killed .If he successfully reflects Winter’s Curse, he can potentially turn the entire fight in his favor

pairs.name: Vengeful Spirit
pairs.reason: Nether Swap is a top-tier counter to Winter’s Curse thanks to its instant cast and long range, making it one of the most reliable tools for saving cursed allies

pairs.name: Meepo
pairs.reason: Meepo packs a lot of raw HP and damage between him and all his clones making it dificult for Arc to do enough damage to outright kill him. Earthbind can chain root Arc into death preventing him from creating distance and Poof can be used to both burst Arc down and get on top of him. Flux's additional effects rarely apply to Meepo as he always has friendly units around him. Dig and Megameepo are both strong tools that buy time for Meepo to avoid damage and close the gap on Arc.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: Doppelganger is a low cooldown dispel that can remove Flux. Additionally, PL is able to create an abundance of Illusions with Spirit Lance, Doppelganger and his Juxtapose to soak up any Spark Wraiths without them ever getting to damage any actual heroes. Phantom Rush allows him to reliably get on top of Arc due to it's high range and low cooldown.

pairs.name: Broodmother
pairs.reason: Spawn Spiderlings create a lot of summons for Brood, which can soak Spark Wraiths for her and mitigate the effects of Flux significantly. Spin Web provides her with unobstructed movement making it easy for her to get on top of Arc and use Insatiable Hunger to deal enough damage and sustain herself in order to kill both Arc and his Tempest Double.

pairs.name: Lycan
pairs.reason: Shapeshift prevent Lycan from being slowed and Summon Wolves usually means he has friendly units near him to soak any Wrath Sparks and mitigate most Flux's strengths. Being a melee hero he doesn't care as much about Magnetic Field's Evasion and usually packs enough damage to just focus down Arc in a matter of seconds.

pairs.name: Marci
pairs.reason: Marci has a natural gap close on Arc Warden using Rebound to burst him down during Unleash. Dispose can further reposition Arc Warden out of his Magnetic Field and make him vulnerable.

pairs.name: Sand King
pairs.reason: Sand King can easily burst down Arc Warden with a surprise Epicenter initiation. A quick Blink Dagger into Burrowstrike combo leaves Arc little time to react or escape. Arc’s low durability makes him especially vulnerable to Sand King's magic burst. If caught off guard, both Arc and his clone can be eliminated before getting a chance to fight back.

pairs.name: Beastmaster
pairs.reason: Beastmaster can lock down Arc Warden instantly with Blink Dagger into Primal Roar. The follow-up Wild Axes burst can quickly bring Arc down before he can respond. Arc’s low HP pool and reliance on positioning make him an easy target for Beastmaster’s aggression. A well-timed initiation leaves Arc no time to cast Magnetic Field or escape

pairs.name: Warlock
pairs.reason: Warlock can control Arc Warden from a distance using Fatal Bonds to spread incoming damage. Chaotic Offering stuns Arc and his clone, disrupting their positioning and damage output. Upheaval slows Arc dramatically, making it hard for him to kite or reposition during fights.

pairs.name: Naga Siren
pairs.reason: Naga Siren can use Song of the Siren to set up clean initiations on Arc Warden. With her illusions, she can easily get on top of Arc and his clone, overwhelming them with physical damage. During the mid game, this pressure prevents Arc from safely farming and hitting his key item timings. A well-timed Song into burst eliminates Arc before he can use Magnetic Field or reposition.

pairs.name: Batrider
pairs.reason: Batrider's Firefly lets him break trees and stun Monkey King if he is perched on top of a broken tree with Tree Dance. Batrider can also follow and chase down Monkey King during Firefly when he tries to use the trees to get away. Batrider's Flaming Lasso and the displacement from Flamebreak also lets him bring Monkey King outside the Wukong's Command ring, which stops his ultimate.

pairs.name: Beastmaster
pairs.reason: Beastmaster's Wild Axes lets him cut down trees to stun Monkey King if he is perched on top of a broken tree with Tree Dance. Monkey King also struggles to run down Beastmaster because of the Hawk root and Boar movement speed slow on attacks. Later in the game, Beastmaster can also burst down Monkey King every time during his long duration lockdown with Primal Roar.

pairs.name: Bounty Hunter
pairs.reason: Bounty Hunter's Track lets him maintain vision of Monkey King when he is perched on top of trees with Tree Dance, effectively countering his ability to stay hidden in tree lines. A casual Quelling Blade can also cut down Monkey King's tree from the Shadow Walk invisibility and stun him if he is not careful.

pairs.name: Enchantress
pairs.reason: Enchantress can dispel Monkey King's Jingu Mastery stacks every time with Enchant, which massively reduces his damage and survivability in fights. With levels in Untouchable, Monkey King also struggles to right click Enchantress to build up Jingu Mastery stacks. Enchantress can also burst down Monkey King inside the Wukong's Command ring with the high damage from Impetus that ignores his high armor.

pairs.name: Enigma
pairs.reason: Enigma's Midnight Pulse lets him cut down a bunch of trees to stun Monkey King if he is perched on top of a broken tree with Tree Dance. This also counters his mobility quite a bit during the laning stage. The periodic stun from Malefice also makes it difficult for Monkey King to cast a timely Wukong's Command.

pairs.name: Keeper of the Light
pairs.reason: Keeper of the Light's Blinding Light push can easily bring Monkey King out of his Wukong's Command ring, which ends his ultimate. Blinding Light also pushes Monkey King off of trees, and can also be used to push him away when he jumps in with Primal Spring and tries to build up Jingu Mastery stacks. The Solar Bind magic resistance reduction can also get Monkey King bursted inside the Wukong's Command ring.

pairs.name: Magnus
pairs.reason: Magnus' Skewer and the slight displacement from Reverse Polarity can easily bring Monkey King out of his Wukong's Command ring, which ends his ultimate. Skewer also breaks trees, which can stun Monkey King if he is perched on top of a broken tree with Tree Dance. Shockwave also makes Monkey King step down if he is perched on a tree, while also putting Tree Dance on cooldown.

pairs.name: Mars
pairs.reason: Mars' Spear of Mars and the slight displacement from God's Rebuke can easily bring Monkey King out of his Wukong's Command ring, which ends his ultimate. Arena of Blood also breaks trees in a massive radius, even outside its AoE, which can be used to find and stun Monkey King when he is perched on top of a tree. Mars also takes reduced damage from Monkey King's right clicks when facing him because of Bulwark.

pairs.name: Muerta
pairs.reason: Muerta's Pierce the Veil makes her immune to physical damage, and lets her counter Monkey King's physical damage. Pierce the Veil also does magical damage, which completely ignores Monkey King's armor gain inside Wukong's Command to burst him down with right clicks. Muerta's Dead Shot also breaks trees on the initial target to stun Monkey King when he is perched on a tree, and the fear makes him step down from the tree.

pairs.name: Phantom Assassin
pairs.reason: Phantom Assassin's evasion from her innate dodges a lot of Monkey King's attacks to prevent him from building up Jingu Mastery stacks. Phantom Assassin can also jump Monkey King with Phantom Strike, and fight him inside Wukong's Command as her crit damage with Coup de Grace overwhelms Monkey King, despite his high armor.

pairs.name: Phoenix
pairs.reason: Phoenix's Supernova breaks trees in a massive radius, which can be used to find and stun Monkey King when he is perched on top of a tree. Icarus Dive also breaks trees to stun Monkey King in the same way. The damage over time from Phoenix's abilities also puts Tree Dance on cooldown for a lengthy duration, preventing him from using the spell to get in fights or escape.

pairs.name: Queen of Pain
pairs.reason: Queen of Pain's damage with her spells easily kills Monkey King, even inside Wukong's Command, as most of her damage is pure and magical. The push from Sonic Wave can also push Monkey King outside the Wukong's Command ring, which ends his ultimate. Queen of Pain can also jump away from Monkey King with Blink when he jumps her with Primal Spring. Shadow Strike also puts Tree Dance on cooldown for a lengthy duration.

pairs.name: Riki
pairs.reason: Riki's mobility with Blink Strike and Tricks of the Trade easily lets him dodge the damage from Monkey King's Primal Spring and Boundless Strike. The same spells also let Riki get away and prevent the buildup of Jingu Mastery stacks. Once Riki becomes invisible with Cloak and Dagger, he can wait for Monkey King on creep waves, and silence him inside Smoke Screen to prevent him from getting away, which leads to easy kills.

pairs.name: Storm Spirit
pairs.reason: Storm Spirit's mobility with Ball Lightning makes him extremely difficult to target with the Boundless Strike stun or the Primal Spring damage. The high mobility also lets Storm Spirit jump Monkey King inside Wukong's Command and burst him down with his magical damage. Ball Lightning also breaks trees, which can stun Monkey King if he is perched on top of a broken tree with Tree Dance.

pairs.name: Sven
pairs.reason: Sven provides armor to his entire team with Warcry to negate a lot of Monkey King's dominant physical damage. The same spell also provides movement speed to Sven's team to run and get outside the Wukong's Command ring. Once Sven gets Revenant's Brooch, his damage gain from God's Strength can easily overwhelm Monkey King inside Wukong's Command, despite his armor gain.

pairs.name: Techies
pairs.reason: Blast Off! destroys trees and can stun Monkey King while he is perched on a tree with Tree Dance. Techies likes to hide Proximity Mines in tree lines, which can trigger when Monkey King jumps across trees to move around, giving away his position and damaging him in the process as he can't immediately attack them atop a tree.

pairs.name: Timbersaw
pairs.reason: All of Timbersaw's active abilities break trees, which can stun Monkey King if he is perched on top of a broken tree with Tree Dance. Timbersaw also does pure damage, which ignores Monkey King's high armor inside Wukong's Command to burst him down. Reactive Armor also helps reduce Monkey King's dominant physical damage.

pairs.name: Vengeful Spirit
pairs.reason: Vengeful Spirit's Nether Swap can easily displace Monkey King outside his Wukong's Command ring, which ends his ultimate. The vision provided by Wave of Terror also lets Vengeful Spirit find Monkey King when he is perched on top of a tree with Tree Dance. The Magic Missile stun also helps fend off Monkey King when he jumps Vengeful Spirit with Primal Spring.

pairs.name: Viper
pairs.reason: Viper's Viper Strike can break Monkey King, preventing him from building up Jingu Mastery stacks in the duration of the spell. This massively reduces his damage and survivability in fights. Viper's damage over time with his active and passive abilities put Tree Dance on cooldown for a length duration, which counters Monkey King's ability to get into fights or escape.

pairs.name: Windranger
pairs.reason: Windranger's Powershot breaks trees, which can stun Monkey King if he is perched on top of a broken tree with Tree Dance. Shackleshot becomes easier to land on Monkey King as he is usually in and around tree lines to use Tree Dance. Windranger also completely evades Monkey King's right clicks during Windrun, preventing him from building Jingu Mastery stacks, and lets her run at him even inside the Wukong's Command ring.

pairs.name: Juggernaut
pairs.reason: Blade Fury makes him magic immune, allowing him to avoid Willow’s disables and burst damage. His Healing Ward provides sustain for himself and allies during fights, countering Willow’s poke. Juggernaut’s Omnislash can quickly burst Willow down if she gets caught out

pairs.name: Axe
pairs.reason: Berserker’s Call forces Willow to attack him, disrupting her spellcasting. His Counter Helix punishes Willow’s close-range attacks and summons. Axe’s high durability and tankiness allow him to survive Willow’s burst damage. With Culling Blade, he can finish Willow off quickly if she gets low.

pairs.name: Legion Commander
pairs.reason: Duel locks Willow in place preventing her from escaping or casting spells freely.Legion’s high burst damage can quickly take down Willow during the duel.Willow’s disables are less effective when caught in Duel limiting her teamfight impact.Legion’s Press the Attack can also remove Dark Willow Brambles or Cursed Crown.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: His multiple illusions can absorb Willow’s disables like Cursed Crown and Brambles making it harder to control him. Terrorize is less effective against illusions. Phantom Lancer’s mobility and dispersion allow him to evade Willow’s burst damage. With good positioning he can overwhelm Willow in fights.

pairs.name: Warlock
pairs.reason: Warlock’s Shadow Word provides sustain against Willow’s poke.His Chaotic Offering stuns and deals AoE damage disrupting Willow’s positioning.Warlock’s teamfight presence and healing give him an edge over Willow in prolonged fights.

pairs.name: Wraith King
pairs.reason: His Reincarnation allows him to survive Willow’s burst damage. Wraith King’s passive lifesteal and stuns help him sustain and control fights. Willow’s disables are less effective against his durability and second life .In fights Wraith King can outlast Willow and punish her cooldowns.

pairs.name: Leshrac
pairs.reason: His high magical damage and Diabolic Edict quickly burn Willow. Leshrac’s disables like Pulse Nova and Lightning Storm can disrupt Willow’s spells. His strong lane presence and push make it hard for Willow to control the game. Leshrac’s burst and sustain overpower Willow in fights.

pairs.name: Puck
pairs.reason: Puck’s Illusory Orb and Waning Rift silence and damage Willow, preventing her from casting spells. Puck’s high mobility and Dream Coil control limit Willow’s movement and escape. Puck can outmaneuver and burst Willow down effectively.

pairs.name: Queen of Pain
pairs.reason: Her high burst damage and mobility allow her to quickly kill Willow before she can react.QoP’s Blink helps her dodge Willow’s disables and reposition in fights.Her Scream of Pain and Shadow Strike pressure Willow in lane and teamfights.

pairs.name: Elder Titan
pairs.reason: His Echo Stomp can stun Willow, preventing her from casting spells. Natural Order reduces Willow’s armor and magic resistance, increasing damage taken. Elder Titan’s Astral Spirit provides vision and damage to pressure Willow. His teamfight presence disrupts Willow’s control and burst potential.

pairs.name: Beastmaster
pairs.reason: Beastmaster's Primal Roar pierces debuff immunity, and lets him control Pangolier during Rolling Thunder for a lengthy duration to waste most of his ultimate. Outside of Rolling Thunder, Beastmaster can easily jump and stun Pangolier with Primal Roar and burst him down with his physical damage.

pairs.name: Bloodseeker
pairs.reason: Bloodseeker's Rupture heavily counters Pangolier's Rolling Thunder as the movement while rolling does massive damage when affected by the ultimate. This makes Pangolier immediately stop Rolling Thunder or die while rolling. The Blood Rite silence also prevents Pangolier from using his other spells to fight back, letting Bloodseeker easily fight him and burst him down.

pairs.name: Centaur Warrunner
pairs.reason: Centaur Warrunner's Retaliate reflects a ton of Pangolier's massive damage back to him, while his high HP pool keeps him from getting bursted by Pangolier's spells. Once Centaur gets Blade Mail, Swashbuckle threatens Pangolier even more with the reflected damage. Centaur's Stampede also boost the movement speed of his entire team to avoid the Rolling Thunder collision and disengage during Pangolier's ultimate.

pairs.name: Clockwerk
pairs.reason: Clockwerk's long range Hook Shot lets him find Pangolier and keep him from channeling Rolling Thunder with Battery Assault as the constant mini stun never lets him complete the initial cast of his ultimate. While Pangolier is rolling during his ultimate, a well placed Power Cogs can trap Pangolier inside or push him away from the fight, making it extremely tricky for Pangolier to move around and do damage during Rolling Thunder.

pairs.name: Faceless Void
pairs.reason: Faceless Void's Time Walk lets him reverse the damage taken from Pangolier's burst damage spells, as well as dodge the Rolling Thunder collision by jumping away from its path. Time Dilation also prevents Pangolier from using his low cooldown spells multiple times in fights. Faceless Void also easily bursts down Pangolier inside Chronosphere, or waste his ultimate if Pangolier is already rolling with his ultimate.

pairs.name: Grimstroke
pairs.reason: Grimstroke's Soulbind can link Pangolier to one of his allies during Rolling Thunder, making him completely stagnant and roll in place, wasting his entire ultimate. The Soulbind leash also prevents Pangolier's mobility from Shield Crash and Swashbuckle. This makes it extremely tricky for Pangolier to enter fights and makes him stand away from his entire team.

pairs.name: Medusa
pairs.reason: Medusa's Stone Gaze can turn Pangolier to stone during his ultimate if he rolls in her direction during his ultimate, wasting a majority of the Rolling Thunder duration. Medusa also doesn't get bursted down by Pangolier's high damage spells, and her physical damage lets her threaten, and even kill, Pangolier during Rolling Thunder.

pairs.name: Puck
pairs.reason: Puck's Dream Coil leashes Pangolier in a small area and prevents him from casting any of his active spells, except for Shield Crash, to get away until he breaks the link. Puck's follow up damage and control through Illusory Orb and Waning Rift lets her silence and kill Pangolier without letting him do anything in fights. Puck can also easily dodge the Rolling Thunder collision with a well timed Phase Shift.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: Slark's Pounce leashes Pangolier close to him and prevents him from casting any of his active spells, except for Shield Crash, to get away or fight back. The Shield Crash barrier only gives Slark a bigger HP pool to attack and build up Essence Shift stacks. Pangolier can never chain stun Slark during Rolling Thunder because of the Dark Pact dispel, and Pounce also lets Slark jump out of the collision path.

pairs.name: Tusk
pairs.reason: A well placed Ice Shards from Tusk pushes away Pangolier during Rolling Thunder, and can even trap him in the small area to waste his entire ultimate. This makes it extremely tricky for Pangolier to do damage in fights with his ultimate. Tusk's control spells also interrupt Pangolier from casting Rolling Thunder, while Snowball can save an ally from the collision as well as match Pangolier's mobility from Shield Crash and Swashbuckle.

pairs.name: Winter Wyvern
pairs.reason: The Winter's Curse from Winter Wyvern pierces debuff immunity, which lets him cast the ultimate on Pangolier during Rolling Thunder to waste his ultimate, depending on the number of enemy heroes caught in the AoE. A well timed Cold Embrace from Winter Wyvern also prevents the entire damage from Rolling Thunder and Swashbuckle while healing up whoever Pangolier is trying to burst down with his spells.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Anti-Mage easily dispels Grimstroke’s Inkswell with Manta Style and avoids his combo with Blink. Grimstroke's high mana pool makes him vulnerable to Mana Void.

pairs.name: Naga Siren
pairs.reason: Naga’s illusions confuse targeting for Inkswell and Soulbind. Her Song resets fights completely, making Grimstroke’s long cooldowns unreliable.

pairs.name: Clinkz
pairs.reason: Clinkz picks off Grimstroke before he can cast spells. His mobility and invisibility make it hard for Grim to land skillshots or defend himself.

pairs.name: Spectre
pairs.reason: Spectre jumps to the backline with Haunt and instantly pressures Grimstroke. He lacks escape or tankiness, making him an easy pickoff.

pairs.name: Dark Willow
pairs.reason: Willow’s mobility and shadow realm lets her dodge Inkswell and Phantoms. Terrorize can counter-initiate against Grimstroke’s aggressive combo.

pairs.name: Arc Warden
pairs.reason: Grimstroke struggles to deal with Arc's double presence from Tempest Double. Spark Wraiths and constant harass zone Grimstroke out of fights.

pairs.name: Bristleback
pairs.reason: Bristle shrugs off Grimstroke’s magical poke. Soulbind rarely gets value due to Bristle's natural spread positioning and high durability.

pairs.name: Mirana
pairs.reason: Mirana’s Leap and Moonlight Shadow allow her and allies to evade Inkswell and Soulbind. She also arrows Grimstroke easily from fog when he channels.

pairs.name: Lycan
pairs.reason: Grimstroke has no way to stop Lycan’s physical burst or high-speed pushes. His summons waste Phantom’s Embrace and quickly dive Grimstroke in fights.

pairs.name: Gyrocopter
pairs.reason: Grimstroke’s low mobility makes him vulnerable to Flak Cannon and Call Down. Gyro thrives in chaotic teamfights where Grimstroke gets overwhelmed.

pairs.name: Mars
pairs.reason: Mars's arena can break all the trees where Hoodwink is using to push out lanes or stay behind his teammates.

pairs.name: Spirit Breaker
pairs.reason: Spirit Breaker's charge can provide vision from a distance while Hoodwink is using the trees to hide.

pairs.name: Centaur Warrunner
pairs.reason: Hoodwink struggles against Centaur because he is tanky and hard to burst. He can return a lot of damage with Retaliate when she trades. Stampede also allows him and his team to disengage or catch her easily.

pairs.name: Sand King
pairs.reason: Sand King’s Sand Storm gives him invisibility and damage over time, making it hard for Hoodwink to land her combo. He can also blink and burst her with Epicenter before she escapes. His teamfight presence outscales hers in mid to late game

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: Hoodwink’s single-target burst is weak against Phantom Lancer’s illusions. She has no built-in AoE or clear way to identify the real one. Once he gets Diffusal Blade, she runs out of mana quickly and can't escape easily.

pairs.name: Timbersaw
pairs.reason: Timbersaw is tanky and shrugs off Hoodwink’s magic burst. He also cuts down trees constantly with his abilities, disabling her Scurry movement. Her tree-based spells become unreliable when Timbersaw is nearby.

pairs.name: Spirit Breaker
pairs.reason: Spirit Breaker can lock down Hoodwink easily with Charge of Darkness and Nether Strike. Her escape is limited once he connects. He is tanky enough to survive her burst and excels at punishing squishy heroes like her.

pairs.name: Wraith King
pairs.reason: Wraith King’s Reincarnation makes it hard for Hoodwink to kill him efficiently. She wastes her combo on his first life, and he can slow or stun her after reviving. He becomes harder to burst down as the game progresses.

pairs.name: Ogre Magi
pairs.reason: Hoodwink struggles against Ogre Magi because he is very tanky and has high base armor, making it hard for her to burst him. His Fireblast and Ignite can lock her down and harass her in lane. Multicast makes his disables unpredictable and dangerous.

pairs.name: Visage
pairs.reason: Visage is hard for Hoodwink to deal with due to his high magic resistance and Gravekeeper’s Cloak, which reduces her burst damage. His Familiars can scout and chase her easily, and her spells don’t clear them effectively. He also thrives in clustered fights where Hoodwink is less effective.

pairs.name: Meepo
pairs.reason: Meepo overwhelms Void Spirit with clones and disables before he escapes. Void Spirit’s spells aren’t enough to burst down all Meepos. He gets rooted and nuked before using his mobility. Meepo snowballs harder and punishes every small mistake.

pairs.name: Lone Druid
pairs.reason: Void Spirit cannot quickly kill Lone Druid or his bear, wasting his combo. The bear roots Void Spirit and punishes his limited HP pool. LD also wins lane by tanking through early nukes. Once the bear gets Desolator or Bash, Void Spirit can’t escape easily.

pairs.name: Chen
pairs.reason: Chen’s summons tank Void Spirit’s burst and make pickoffs harder. Divine Favor and Hand of God keep allies alive after being engaged on. Chen’s early push punishes Void Spirit’s slow wave clear. Void Spirit has trouble fighting multiple creeps and heals

pairs.name: Night Stalker
pairs.reason: Night Stalker silences and sticks to Void Spirit during nighttime. Void Spirit can't escape easily with Void and Crippling Fear. Once BKB is online, Night Stalker becomes unkillable for him. Void Spirit needs defensive items to survive early ganks.

pairs.name: Monkey King
pairs.reason: Monkey King controls Void Spirit with Jingu and Boundless Strike. Void Spirit can’t freely move inside Wukong’s Command. He loses lane trades and gets zoned in fights. Monkey punishes missed steps with burst and lifesteal.

pairs.name: Broodmother
pairs.reason: Brood’s webs make her too mobile to catch with Void Spirit’s combo. She controls space too well for him to fight in. He gets run over without strong AoE follow-up.

pairs.name: Huskar
pairs.reason: Huskar shrugs off Void Spirit’s burst and forces bad trades with Burning Spears. Void Spirit cannot disarm him or escape easily once jumped on. Inner Fire interrupts Void Spirit’s combo and resets fights. Huskar scales better in sustained brawls.

pairs.name: Io
pairs.reason: Io keeps cores alive through Void Spirit’s burst with Overcharge and Tether. Relocate saves allies from pickoffs, wasting Void’s cooldowns. Void Spirit can’t isolate supports easily with Io backing them. He struggles to outdamage healing.

pairs.name: Terrorblade
pairs.reason: Terrorblade survives Void Spirit's burst and punishes him during Metamorphosis. Void Spirit lacks the AoE or physical damage to bring illusions down. Sunder resets fights before Void Spirit can finish him. TB’s range also keeps Void Spirit zoned out.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Anti-Mage blinks away from Void Spirit’s combo and punishes his low mana pool. He scales harder and counters Void Spirit with Mana Void. Void Spirit can’t burst AM unless silenced early and perfectly executed. Once Manta is online, AM escapes every time.

pairs.name: Brewmaster
pairs.reason: Brewmaster’s split units dodge Mortimer Kisses and disable Snapfire. Cyclone removes her from fights before she casts spells. His mobility lets him dodge Scatterblast and Cookie stuns. Snapfire gets little value against his spread-out playstyle.

pairs.name: Faceless Void
pairs.reason: Faceless Void punishes Snapfire with Chronosphere before she can react. She relies on positioning and is vulnerable to instant initiation. Her damage becomes irrelevant if caught in Chrono. Snapfire struggles to fight into his lockdown and scaling.

pairs.name: Bounty Hunter
pairs.reason: Bounty Hunter snipes Snapfire in the backlines with Track and burst. He snowballs off gold from repeated kills on her. Snapfire has no escape if caught out of position. Track removes her fog safety and limits her aggressive posturing.

pairs.name: Void Spirit
pairs.reason: Void Spirit avoids her spells with Dissimilate and Astral Step. He closes gaps quickly and silences Snapfire before she casts anything. She can’t react fast enough to his mobility. Snapfire is punished hard for overextending or mispositioning.

pairs.name: Broodmother
