pairs.reason: Broodmother avoids Snapfire’s AoE with Spiderlings and overwhelms her. Snapfire’s spells have long cooldowns and can’t clear full waves of spiders fast enough. Brood dominates the map and Snapfire can’t keep up in tempo. Her low mobility is a liability.

pairs.name: Lycan
pairs.reason: Lycan runs down Snapfire with his wolves and Shapeshift. Her defensive tools can’t stop his full commitment. She lacks mobility to reposition safely when chased. Lycan punishes her weak early defense and takes towers faster than she can respond.

pairs.name: Sven
pairs.reason: Sven blinks and kills Snapfire before she can cast spells. BKB nullifies all her damage output. Snapfire gets overwhelmed by his physical burst. Her long-range poke doesn’t stop Sven from deleting her in seconds.

pairs.name: Storm Spirit
pairs.reason: Storm jumps onto Snapfire before she can contribute to fights. Her long cast animations make her vulnerable to Orchid and vortex. She gets burst quickly and lacks disables to stop him. Storm wins every engagement unless Snapfire gets perfect follow-up.

pairs.name: Spirit Breaker
pairs.reason: Spirit Breaker’s Charge disables Snapfire mid-cast and punishes her squishy nature. Her spells can’t interrupt his initiation. He breaks her backline role and forces awkward fights. Snapfire becomes an easy target if caught out.

pairs.name: Puck
pairs.reason: Puck avoids all Snapfire’s damage with Phase Shift and mobility. Dream Coil locks her in place, preventing safe Mortimer Kisses. She can’t catch or kill him due to his elusiveness. Snapfire loses value in fights where spells don’t connect.

pairs.name: Lifestealer
pairs.reason: Lifestealer can use Rage to escape Arena of Blood and avoid Spear of Mars’ stun, making him difficult to control. Additionally, he thrives against heroes with large health pools, which can reduce Mars’ relative tankiness and make him more vulnerable.

pairs.name: Juggernaut
pairs.reason: Blade Fury lets Juggernaut escape Arena of Blood and dodge Spear of Mars’ stun. It’s also a strong tool for chasing and killing Mars early, since he is more susceptible to magical damage.

pairs.name: Puck
pairs.reason: Puck is highly elusive and difficult to control. Without items like Hex or Eul’s Scepter, landing a Spear of Mars and killing her can be very challenging.

pairs.name: Dazzle
pairs.reason: Dazzle excels at saving teammates during fights with his Shallow Grave, which can keep allies alive even inside Mars’ Arena of Blood. His strong healing and damage mitigation make it difficult for Mars to secure kills inside the arena, giving Dazzle’s team a significant advantage in prolonged engagements.

pairs.name: Oracle
pairs.reason: Oracle can save allies from lethal damage inside Arena of Blood using False Promise, negating Mars’ burst potential. Additionally, Fate’s Edict can disarm Mars, lowering his threat in fights, or grant magic immunity to teammates against Spear of Mars and Arena of Blood.

pairs.name: Outworld Devourer
pairs.reason: Astral Imprisonment can save allies trapped inside Arena of Blood. Additionally, Outworld Devourer ignores Bulwark by dealing pure damage. His Sanity’s Eclipse deals significant damage due to the large mana difference between Mars and OD.

pairs.name: Oracle
pairs.reason: Oracle's Forutne's End is a low cooldown AOE dispel that can remove Escape Act without even having to target the enemy but instead an ally.

pairs.name: Shadow Demon
pairs.reason: Demonic Purge prevents Ringmaster from saving his allies with Escape Act.

pairs.name: Invoker
pairs.reason: Invoker can use Tornado to dispel Escape Act.

pairs.name: Brewmaster
pairs.reason: Brewmaster can use Dispel Magic from his Storm Panda to dispel Escape Act.

pairs.name: Bloodseeker
pairs.reason: Rupture and Blood Rite take their effect despite of Escape Act's defensive properties.

pairs.name: Pangolier
pairs.reason: Escape Act does little to help against Pango's kit as he does exclusively Area of Effect Physical damage.

pairs.name: Viper
pairs.reason: Viper is going to be able to Break your passive ability and slow your attack speed which is going to significantly reduce your effectiveness and damage output.

pairs.name: Nyx Assassin
pairs.reason: Spiked Carapace can stop Dawnbreaker's Solar Guardian which will eliminate her global presence and limits her movement around the map.

pairs.name: Drow Ranger
pairs.reason: Gust can shut down most of Dawnbreaker's abilities, rendering her useless. Laning is also hard against this ranged carry hero.

pairs.name: Disruptor
pairs.reason: Your ultimate will be a perfect setup for Kinetic Field and Static Storm. You can also not escape from Kinetic Field with your hammer and you can be glimpsed when you land with your ultimate.

pairs.name: Silencer
pairs.reason: Global Silence cancels Dawnbreaker’s ultimate, preventing her from joining fights and reducing her impact during team engagements.

pairs.name: Phoenix
pairs.reason: Phoenix counters Dawnbreaker because she has low attack speed, making it hard to trade damage. Additionally, Phoenix’s supernova is unaffected by Dawnbreaker’s spells, allowing Phoenix to dominate teamfights.

pairs.name: Ancient Apparition
pairs.reason: The Ice Blast from Ancient Apparition nullifies the lifesteal from either Sidekick or Bodyguard and makes it difficult for Marci to commit to fights with Unleash.

pairs.name: Axe
pairs.reason: The armor gain during Bersekers Call combined with the Blade Mail active makes it difficult for Marci to commit on Axe with Unleash as the Counter Helix procs and return damage will likely kill Marci instead.

pairs.name: Bloodseeker
pairs.reason: Rupture does massive damage to Marci if she uses Rebound during it, effectively halting her mobility. A follow up Blood Rite and right click committal makes Marci easy pickings for Bloodseeker.

pairs.name: Dark Willow
pairs.reason: Bramble Maze makes it difficult for Marci to maneuver and commit to fights using Rebound. Dark Willow also becomes untargetable with right clicks during Shadow Realm, rendering Marcis Unleash useless against her.

pairs.name: Death Prophet
pairs.reason: The Death Prophet silence, high damage, and HP sustain in close proximity makes it difficult for Marci to commit onto her and burst her down during Unleash. Doing so will likely get Marci killed instead.

pairs.name: Lifestealer
pairs.reason: A well timed Rage from Lifestealer ignores Marcis control spells and gives him the upper hand in a right click battle with the high damage and HP sustain through Feast and Open Wounds.

pairs.name: Lycan
pairs.reason: The movement speed gain during Shapeshift allows Lycan to heavily kite Marci during Unleash while Howl makes it difficult for her to dish out her full right click damage. Marci also is not effective at defending towers against the heavy push from Lycan and his wolf pack.

pairs.name: Mars
pairs.reason: The Arena of Blood stops Marci from jumping in or out of its walls, nullifying her mobility through Rebound. Marci also finds it difficult to burst down Mars in a right click battle because of the damage reduction from Bulwark.

pairs.name: Necrophos
pairs.reason: Necrophos can make himself invulnerable to Marcis right clicks during Unleash by using Ghost Shroud and kiting her. The heavy burst from Reapers Scythe also keeps Marci on thin ice if she commits to fights as she can die if she gets below half HP.

pairs.name: Oracle
pairs.reason: Oracle can heavily disrupt Marcis right click damage output during Unleash with the disarm from Fates Edict as well as nullify her mobility with the root from Fortunes End. Marci also relies on quickly bursting down heroes and False Promise completely counters that.

pairs.name: Puck
pairs.reason: The silence and leash from Pucks spells makes it difficult for Marci to maneuver in fights with Rebound. Puck is also difficult to lock down and hit during Unleash as she can easily dodge the Rebound stun using Phase Shift and move away with Illusory Orb.

pairs.name: Pugna
pairs.reason: Marci relies on quickly bursting down heroes and Pugna completely counters that by using Decrepify on either Marci or her target to waste a lot of her Unleash duration.

pairs.name: Weaver
pairs.reason: Weaver is difficult to lock down and hit during Unleash as he can become invisible and extremely fast using Shukuchi to dodge the Rebound stun. Weaver can also dish out his right click damage from range while kiting Marci.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Anti-Mage blinks out of Onslaught and avoids Trample entirely. Mana Break weakens Primal Beast’s ability to spam spells. Pulverize is hard to land reliably due to Anti-Mage’s mobility. In late game, Anti-Mage outscales and deletes Primal Beast effortlessly.

pairs.name: Undying
pairs.reason: Undying out-sustains Primal Beast in early fights with Decay spam. Tombstone forces Primal Beast to reposition instead of diving. Undying’s tanky build slows down Primal Beast’s snowball potential. Teamfighting against Undying becomes difficult without backup.

pairs.name: Doom
pairs.reason: Doom completely disables Primal Beast’s entire kit during fights. Once Doomed, Primal Beast cannot Trample, Pulverize, or escape. Doom’s tanky presence also survives Primal Beast’s burst. One well-timed ultimate can shut down Primal Beast’s game plan.

pairs.name: Death Prophet
pairs.reason: Spirit Siphon heals through Trample and punishes Primal Beast’s aggression. Exorcism zones him out of objectives where he excels. Death Prophet outlasts him in every extended brawl. Primal Beast cannot break her scaling without assistance.

pairs.name: Outworld Devourer
pairs.reason: Outworld Destroyer banishes Primal Beast during Onslaught, wasting his initiation. Arcane Orb deals massive damage to his large mana pool. Pulverize is easy to interrupt with Astral Imprisonment. Outworld Destroyer wins mid lane and teamfights with ease.

pairs.name: Huskar
pairs.reason: Huskar shrugs off Primal Beast’s initial damage and punishes dives. Once his Burning Spear stacks build up, Primal Beast cannot fight back. Primal Beast’s long cast animations make him an easy target. Huskar dominates small-scale skirmishes.

pairs.name: Treant Protector
pairs.reason: Leech Seed slows and drains Primal Beast during his dive attempts. Living Armor slows down any attempts to snowball through towers. Treant Protector can lock Primal Beast in place with Overgrowth. He delays tempo and denies early objectives.

pairs.name: Grimstroke
pairs.reason: Grimstroke’s Ink Swell ruins Onslaught paths and punishes dive attempts. Soulbind disables Pulverize mid-cast and traps him with another target. Grimstroke’s long-range nukes chip away before Primal Beast can engage. Primal Beast struggles to find clean openings.

pairs.name: Zeus
pairs.reason: Zeus can poke from a distance while avoiding close contact. Primal Beast cannot punish Zeus’s low health if he ever gets close. Lightning Bolt cancels Blink Dagger and chips away at him constantly. Zeus snowballs while Primal Beast is forced to disengage.

pairs.name: Io
pairs.reason: Io sustains teammates through Primal Beast’s early combos. Relocate saves squishy cores from Pulverize. Overcharge buffs allies to out-damage Trample and Onslaught. Io hard counters Primal Beast’s burst timing and momentum.

pairs.name: Spectre
pairs.reason: Spectre punishes backline, squishy heroes like Muerta with Haunt and Dispersion. She ignores Dead Shot zoning and thrives in chaos. Her tankiness outlasts Muerta’s damage window. Once she reaches her items, Muerta cannot duel her effectively.

pairs.name: Wraith King
pairs.reason: Wraith King revives with Reincarnation, which wastes Muerta’s burst window during Pierce the Veil. His sustain and crit-based damage out-trade her in late fights. He can close the gap and slow her before she escapes. Her lack of stuns gives him room to dominate.

pairs.name: Chen
pairs.reason: Chen’s army of creeps absorbs Muerta’s abilities and reduces her effectiveness. His healing and sustain offset her poke and burst. Divine Favor and Hand of God counteract her execution power. Muerta cannot keep up in push scenarios against his units.

pairs.name: Axe
pairs.reason: Axe punishes Muerta’s low mobility with Blink Call and Blade Mail. She cannot easily escape Berserker’s Call or survive his Counter Helix spins. If she uses Pierce the Veil near him, he reflects all the damage. Axe forces her into bad positioning consistently.

pairs.name: Centaur Warrunner
pairs.reason: Centaur’s Blink stun and tankiness make it hard for Muerta to win trades. Her pure damage is good, but not fast enough to stop Retaliate. He disrupts her positioning with Stampede and burst follow-up. Muerta struggles to kite or kill him alone.

pairs.name: Zeus
pairs.reason: Zeus outputs more burst damage than Muerta in teamfights and trades. He can nuke her before she uses Pierce the Veil. His global presence and spell damage give him a clear edge. Muerta cannot hide or burst him fast enough without being punished.

pairs.name: Kunkka
pairs.reason: Kunkka's X Mark the Spot and Torrent make her escape tools irrelevant. He is tanky and hard to burst due to Ghostship’s damage reduction. Her low armor is exploited by his cleave and physical spells. She gets caught easily by his Area of effect combo.

pairs.name: Rubick
pairs.reason: Rubick can steal The Calling or Dead Shot and use them just as well. His Telekinesis disables her before she bursts him. He can position defensively to avoid Pierce the Veil. Muerta’s predictable abilities make her a good spell donor to him.

pairs.name: Ringmaster
pairs.reason: Ringmaster can tank Muerta’s burst while out-scaling her with high Area of effect and disruption. His traps and control punish her stationary ultimate. He can pull or snare her out of position. Muerta finds it hard to contest objectives against him.

pairs.name: Templar Assassin
pairs.reason: Templar Assassin bursts Muerta with high physical damage before she gets value from Pierce the Veil. Her Refraction blocks Muerta’s shots effectively. Templar Assassin snowballs faster and punishes poor positioning. Muerta cannot deal with her tempo advantage.

pairs.name: Axe
pairs.reason: Axe's high armor gain with Berserker's Call usage lets him negate much of Kez's dominant physical damage at all stages of the game. Axe is also a natural Blade Mail carrier, which is a massive counter to Kez's high burst damage and the return damage threatens his life every time he uses his spell combo.

pairs.name: Bloodseeker
pairs.reason: Bloodseeker's Rupture massively counters Kez's mobility as he cannot dispel it with Raptor Dance and takes massive damage if he tries to Grapple away. Once Kez becomes static because of Rupture, he is easy to take down with a follow up Bloodrite silence and right clicks.

pairs.name: Doom
pairs.reason: Doom's ultimate Doom prevents Kez from lifestealing back his HP through his spells while also countering his mobility as he is effectively silenced. Once his mobility is taken away, Doom has an easy time of running down a squishy Kez during Scorched Earth.

pairs.name: Faceless Void
pairs.reason: Faceless Void's Time Dilation causes a lot of damage over time and slows down Kez when he has used his spell combo and most of his spells are on cooldown. Time Dilation also prevents Switching Discipline more than once in fights because of the extended cooldown. Kez also has no counter to the Chronosphere lockdown and is easily killed every time by Faceless Void during the ultimate.

pairs.name: Legion Commander
pairs.reason: Legion Commander Stonehall Plate facet gives her a damage barrier with Overwhelming Odds usage, which lets her absorb a lot of the damage from Kez's spell combo in the laning stage. Later in the game, once Legion Commander has Blade Mail and Blink Dagger, a squishy Kez makes for easy Duel wins while he cannot get away with his mobility spells.

pairs.name: Lion
pairs.reason: Lion has a couple of lengthy lockdown spells to keep Kez in place and Drain his mana, without which Kez does little to no damage when just right clicking enemy heroes. Lion's Finger of Death also provides massive burst damage to take down a squishy Kez.

pairs.name: Mars
pairs.reason: Mars' spells interrupt most of Kez's mobility spells and does not let him move as he wishes in teamfights. Once he reaches level 6, Mars can keep Kez in a restricted area inside Arena of Blood, which makes it easy to lock him down with Spear and finish off with damage spells and right clicks.

pairs.name: Necrophos
pairs.reason: Necrophos' Ghost Shroud makes him invulnerable to Kez's dominant physical damage, which gives him the upper hand in fights throughout the game. Necrophos' instant heal from Death Pulse is also not reduced by Kazurai Katana, and his Reaper's Scythe makes short work of a squishy Kez along with his high damage spells.

pairs.name: Nyx Assassin
pairs.reason: Nyx Assassin's high burst damage from his spell combo after level 6 lets him find and kill a squishy Kez every time throughout the game. The matchup becomes even more favorable for Nyx Assassin once he buys Dagon. On top of that, Nyx Assassin's Impale and Spiked Carapace, which he can also proc from Kez's AoE spells and damage over time, can keep him locked down for a lengthy duration.

pairs.name: Puck
pairs.reason: Puck's ultimate Dream Coil leashes Kez in place and prevents him from using his mobility spells to jump between targets or escape. The Waning Rift silence is also a massive hinderance for Kez to move around or deal damage. Kez also has a hard time silencing Puck with Talon Toss as she can dodge it every time with Phase Shift.

pairs.name: Queen of Pain
pairs.reason: Queen of Pain's insanely high burst damage from her spell combo is a nightmare to deal with for a squishy Kez, who dies to it every time. The pressure only ramps up as Queen of Pain gets a Dagon later in the game to magnify her burst potential. Queen of Pain's Blink also lets her kite and disengage when not silenced by Talon Toss.

pairs.name: Riki
pairs.reason: Riki's Smoke Screen silences Kez in its AoE and prevents him from moving around or dealing damage with his spells, effectively nullifying him completely. Once Riki gets Diffusal Blade, it becomes easier to keep a squishy Kez inside Smoke Screen and burst him down while he cannot get away.

pairs.name: Silencer
pairs.reason: Silencer's silence through Global Silence and Last Word are a nightmare to deal with for Kez, who relies on his spells for both mobility and damage. Arcane Curse also lets Silencer do a lot of slow and damage to Kez if he casts his spell combo while affected by the spell, but it is easily dispelled by Raptor Dance.

pairs.name: Spectre
pairs.reason: Spectre can jump Kez anywhere on the map with Shadow Step and win the right click battle with the Desolate pure damage on her right clicks while Kez is slowed down by Spectral Dagger. Spectre is also a natural Blade Mail carrier, and together with Dispersion, returns a ton of damage to Kez from his spell combo and threatens his life every time.

pairs.name: Storm Spirit
pairs.reason: Storm Spirit's high burst damage paired with the lockdown from Electric Vortex lets him jump a squishy Kez with Ball Lightning and kill him while he cannot use his mobility spells to get away. The constant jumps from Ball Lightning also makes it hard for Kez to target and silence Storm Spirit with Talon Toss.

pairs.name: Timbersaw
pairs.reason: Timbersaw's armor gain from Reactive Armor stacks reduces a lot of the physical damage dealt by Kez with his spell combo and right clicks. Once Timbersaw gets Aghanim's Scepter, he becomes practically impossible for Kez to kill because of the massive damage barrier. Meanwhile, Timbersaw easily takes down a squishy Kez with the massive damage from his spell combo.

pairs.name: Ursa
pairs.reason: Ursa is one of the few carries who can stand his ground and win the right click battle against Kez. The Enrage buff reduces most of the damage dealt by Kez's spell combo while Fury Swipes stacks and the Overpower charges easily burst down a squishy Kez if he tries to stand his ground and fight back.
